jobs.title: Technical Account Manager
jobs.excerpt: What's the Vibe?  Our founders started Creative Force with a single goal in mind: to build industry-leading software with really cool people.
jobs.description:
What's the Vibe?
Our founders started Creative Force with a single goal in mind: to build industry-leading software with really cool people.
As we’ve grown, we’ve stayed true to that vision. Our products are ushering in a new era of creative operations for some of the world’s largest brands and retailers.
And all along the way, hiring great people has remained a critical business priority...
...See, we have this crazy idea that effective collaboration is THE skill of the future and critical to our success. As a remote company with staff across the globe, we've seen firsthand how important it is for our teams to work well together.
And that's why we focus on hiring talented people who are also great to work with.
That means we don't always hire the people with the most experience. Some of us have PhDs. Others have spent multiple decades working at the top of our field. But we've also hired former tennis coaches, film students, photographers, hotel front desk workers, freelance travel agents, and fashion designers.
While our backgrounds are diverse, we all share a few important traits:
  • We love solving challenging problems.
  • We're passionate about the work we do.
  • And we're the kind of good humans who make you look forward to that morning coffee chat, who bring positive energy to every meeting, who go the extra mile to support one another, and who make work feel a little less like work.
But hey, there are lots of job posts out there that are cool and vibey and explain how unique their company culture is (look, a ping-pong table!). We know, we’ve seen them. Some might be truer than others. As for us, we think you’ll notice the good vibes the first time we chat.

What we offer YOU

  • A fast-growing, exciting, and fun scaleup environment — with multiple international Employer Awards — and not those awards you can pay for, but the kind of awards given based on Employee reviews. It just doesn’t get any better than that. 💜
  • A flat and transparent organizational structure — no bureaucratic red tape. Your ideas and initiatives will be heard and embraced!
  • True work-life balance — we see our team members as people, not numbers, and know that a balanced personal and professional life is critical to happiness and long-term fulfillment
  • A collaborative international environment with colleagues across Europe and USA
  • A growing Technical Success function with opportunities to influence processes, strategy, and customer experience
  • A vibrant work culture grounded in the belief that we’re better together
  • Company trips and events, and much more!

What’s the Role?

Still interested? Awesome. Here's the deal:

At Creative Force, we work with some of the world's biggest brands and retailers. Our customers operate at scale, move fast, and rely on our platform to power complex creative workflows across teams, regions, and markets.

And that's where you come in.

We're looking for a Technical Account Manager to become the trusted technical partner for our Enterprise customers throughout their entire journey with Creative Force.
You'll be involved from the very beginning — partnering with Sales during the pre-sales process to understand customer needs, design the right technical solutions, and help show how Creative Force can solve complex workflow challenges.
From there, you'll guide customers through successful implementations by understanding their current setup, translating their business needs into scalable workflows, and making sure Creative Force delivers real value.
But this isn't a "finish implementation and move on" kind of role.
You'll continue partnering with customers long after go-live — helping them optimize their setup, solve complex technical challenges, advise on best practices, and get the most out of Creative Force as their business evolves.
Our customers operate at Enterprise scale, which means our solutions are not one-size-fits-all. You'll work with multiple stakeholders, different systems, global teams, and plenty of interesting problems to solve.
Most importantly, you'll join a Customer Experience team that cares deeply about solving hard problems, sharing knowledge, and helping each other get better every day.

Technical Account Manager Self-Assessment

Normally, this is where you'd find a three-page-long list of required skills, including but not limited to: underwater basket weaving, competitive cheese rolling, and advanced spreadsheet wizardry.
But it’s 2026, so we aren’t going to do that to you.
We do know, however, what characteristics we believe make an exceptional Technical Account Manager. To help you evaluate if you'd be a good fit for this role, we’ve provided them below.
And real talk: we care less about exact job titles and more about how you think, communicate, and build relationships.

You’re technical, but you speak humanYou're comfortable discussing technical details and concepts like integrations, APIs, cloud environments, and system architecture.
However, you don’t hide behind jargon. You know how to explain complex concepts in a way that customers, commercial teams, and internal stakeholders can actually understand.

When something breaks, your first reaction isn't "who can fix this?" — it's "let me understand what's happening."
You're genuinely excited about investigating problems, connecting dots, digging into workflows, and finding the root cause, and you understand that being “technical” isn’t just about knowing systems. It’s about creating clarity.

You thrive in complexityYou've worked with Enterprise SaaS before. You know what it means to navigate multi-stakeholder implementations without a perfect playbook -- and to stay sharp and organized across a long project timeline. You're energized by complexity, not overwhelmed by it.

And when the information is incomplete, or the situation is ambiguous?
You don't stall. You problem-solve, adapt, and keep things moving.
You own the room
You're comfortable leading customer conversations, setting direction, challenging assumptions, and helping teams make the right decisions and move forward.

Multiple stakeholders. Different priorities. Regional differences. Changing requirements. You know how to navigate it.

You can sit in a technical discovery call, ask the right questions, identify potential risks, and translate what you learn into clear recommendations. Whether you’re speaking with a technical stakeholder, an operations leader, or a commercial decision-maker, you adapt your communication style without losing clarity and precision.

You know how to project confidence even when you're still working through the details. You understand that the way you show up on these calls has a direct impact on whether customers adopt the product, stay long-term, and refer others.
That kind of ownership doesn't intimidate you -- it motivates you.

You challenge with graceBeing customer-focused doesn't mean saying yes to everything. Sometimes, the most valuable thing you can do for a customer is challenge their thinking.

High emotional intelligence is a core part of this job, not a soft bonus. You'll regularly work with customers who have strong opinions, incomplete information, and competing internal priorities.

You know how to push back when needed, redirect when necessary, ask better questions, and guide customers toward solutions that actually solve their problems.
You know when to say "that's not the right approach" -- and you know how to say it in a way that builds trust rather than breaking it.
You are well aware that trust is built through honesty, curiosity, and a genuine care for helping people succeed.
Who Isn't This Role For?
First up: while we’re open to remote candidates across Europe, we’ll have a preference for candidates based in Denmark, Poland, Germany, UK or the Netherlands.
What matters most to us isn’t a specific post code. It’s finding someone who thrives in collaborative, fast-moving environments and genuinely enjoys building strong relationships with customers and teammates across borders and time zones.
Second: things change at Creative Force. A lot. Like, a LOT a lot.
Our industry evolves quickly. Our customers evolve quickly. We evolve quickly.
Some people thrive in that kind of environment. They love the pace, the ownership, the innovation, and the constant learning.
We’re definitely those people.
But we also know that kind of dynamism isn’t for everyone. So if you’re looking for a highly structured environment where everything stays the same year after year, we’re probably not what you’re looking for.
How to apply?
Oh, and one more thing: attaching a resumé is totally optional.
We don’t believe a list of previous jobs tells us everything about who you are or what you’re capable of. Instead, as part of your application, we’d love for you to send us a short video introducing yourself.
It doesn’t need to be fancy or professionally produced. You can use any video creation tool you like, record it on your phone, or keep it simple with a webcam. The goal isn’t perfection — it’s authenticity.
In the video, we’d love to learn a little more about:
  • Who you are and what motivates you
  • What lights you up about working with customers
  • Why do you think you’d be a great fit for Creative Force
We simply want to get a glimpse of the human behind the application.
Once you’ve recorded your video, simply include the link in your application form.
We’re looking forward to meeting you and hearing your story! 💜

jobs.description:
Job Title: PDF Accessibility Specialist (Freelance / Independent Contractor)

Hours: 5–20 hours per week (Flexible / Remote – Philippines Timezone Preferred)

Overview:

Promet Source is seeking an Independent PDF Accessibility Specialist to consult with our clients on PDF accessibility best practices and remediate documents to meet WCAG, Section 508, and PDF/UA standards. This role ensures that all PDF content is fully usable by individuals relying on assistive technologies, including screen readers.

Responsibilities:

  • Remediate PDFs for accessibility, including tagging, reading order, alternative text, headings, tables, forms, and bookmarks.
  • Test documents using screen readers (JAWS, NVDA, VoiceOver) and automated tools (Adobe Acrobat Accessibility Checker, PAC, CommonLook).
  • Convert scanned or image-based PDFs into accessible, searchable documents using OCR.
  • Review source files (Word, InDesign, PowerPoint) and recommend upstream accessibility fixes to streamline remediation.
  • Conduct accessibility audits and produce VPAT/ACR documentation as needed.
  • Track and prioritize remediation tasks across a document backlog while consistently meeting deadlines and quality standards.
  • Stay current on WCAG 2.1/2.2, Section 508, ADA, and PDF/UA requirements.

Qualifications:

  • Proven experience remediating PDFs for accessibility compliance.
  • In-depth working knowledge of WCAG 2.1/2.2 AA guidelines and Section 508 standards.
  • Proficiency with Adobe Acrobat Pro, AEM Designer (tagging, reading order, form design), and automated accessibility testing tools.
  • Practical familiarity with screen reader testing and assistive technology.
  • Strong attention to detail and the ability to manage a high-volume document workload.
  • IAAP certification (CPACC, WAS, or CPWA) is highly preferred.

Preferred Experience:

  • Remediating complex structures, including interactive forms, multi-page tables, charts, and multi-column layouts.
  • Working with source authoring tools (Microsoft Word, Adobe InDesign, PowerPoint) using accessible-by-design principles.

We are an equal opportunity organization. All qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

About Accenture:


Accenture helps the world's leading enterprises reinvent by building their digital core and unleashing the power of AI to create value at speed for organizations across industries. We serve approximately 9,000 clients and generated approximately $74 billion in FY26 revenue. Visit us at accenture.com.


We are:


A forward-thinking services company at the forefront of AI-native engineering. We partner with enterprise clients to design, build, and run production systems in which AI is a first-class engineering capability, engineered into the product and into the way our teams build it. Our engineers embed deeply with customers, own the code they ship, and move work past experimentation into operational reality.


You are:


An engineer who builds across the stack: front end, APIs, services, data, and the infrastructure it runs on. You take ownership of a feature through to production, including the parts that sit outside your strongest layer, and you have shipped software that real users depend on. You can explain the design decisions behind your work and what you would do differently.

AI is part of how you work. You use AI tools daily to generate, test, debug, and document code, and you have built at least one production feature in which a model performs meaningful work. You understand what it takes for a system to hold up under production load, security review, and real users.

You'll grow into an engineer who can own an entire system, developing depth in cloud, security, data, and agentic engineering alongside senior engineers who remain hands-on in the code with you.


The Work:


You'll work as part of a client-embedded engineering team, taking real features from design through production. You will be handed problems to solve, and you will be expected to ask precise questions, make progress under ambiguity, and put working software in front of stakeholders quickly.


Build Across the Stack

  • Build and ship production features across front end, APIs, backend services, integration, and data, taking a feature end to end across every layer it touches.
  • Read and debug unfamiliar code, trace a problem across application, data, and infrastructure boundaries, and fix the underlying cause.
  • Build and Run on Cloud-Native Platforms
  • Develop, containerize, and deploy services on a major cloud platform using Docker, Kubernetes or serverless, and managed cloud services.
  • Apply infrastructure as code (Terraform, Helm, or equivalent), and take part in keeping your services healthy, observable, and recoverable in production.
  • Work Inside the Delivery Pipeline
  • Work within automated CI/CD pipelines, writing the automated tests, resolving pipeline failures, and taking your own changes through to production.
  • Apply secure engineering practices as you code, including identity and access fundamentals, secrets handling, dependency hygiene, and input validation.

Work With Data and Context:


  • Design and implement the data access your features need across relational and non-relational stores, APIs, object storage, and event platforms.
  • Build the retrieval and context layers AI features depend on, including knowledge sources, embeddings, metadata, and context management, applying data quality, access, and privacy controls as you go.

Build AI Features and Agent Workflows:


  • Integrate commercial and open models through APIs and enterprise AI platforms, using tool calling, structured outputs, retrieval, and context engineering to make them useful inside live business workflows.
  • Build agent workflows with tools, memory, and human checkpoints, and write the evaluations that measure their behavior against accuracy, latency, safety, and cost.

Engineer With AI Every Day:


  • Use AI-native development techniques throughout your own workflow, including code generation, test generation, debugging, refactoring, documentation, and code comprehension, and measure the effect on your throughput and quality.
  • Give agents the context, tools, and boundaries they need to safely handle bounded engineering tasks, and review their output to the same standard you would apply to a colleague's code.

Grow and Contribute:


  • Participate in design reviews, code reviews, and production troubleshooting, applying feedback quickly and raising the quality of the work around you.
  • Document what you learn and contribute patterns, reusable components, and tooling back to the team and to our internal AI-native engineering community.

Travel may be required for this role. The amount of travel will vary from 25% to 75% depending on business need and client requirements.


Here's What You Need:


  • Minimum of 3 years of professional software engineering experience building production software.
  • Minimum of 2 years of hands-on experience working across more than one layer of the stack, for example front end and API, or services and data.
  • Minimum of 3 years of programming experience in at least one major language such as Java, Python, Go, TypeScript/JavaScript, or C#.
  • Minimum of 3 year of hands-on experience with a major cloud platform (AWS, Azure, or GCP), including building and deploying containerized services.

  • Minimum of 1 year of hands-on experience building and shipping AI-enabled features or agent workflows, including model integration through APIs, tool calling, structured outputs, retrieval, and context engineering.

jobs.excerpt: About OmnidianOmnidian, Inc.  is a fast-growing Series C tech-enabled service company revolutionizing performance assurance for the distributed solar and energy storage industries.
jobs.description:
About Omnidian

Omnidian, Inc. is a fast-growing Series C tech-enabled service company revolutionizing performance assurance for the distributed solar and energy storage industries. Omnidian is building a more sustainable future for the planet through our passionate teams, our innovative technology, and by creating an amazing customer experience. We are a certified B Corps, headquartered in Seattle, WA

The Job

Are you ready to make a meaningful impact in the solar industry? As a Customer Experience Specialist at Omnidian, you'll play a pivotal role in managing high-sentiment escalations and ensuring our customers receive a path to total system recovery. In this role, you will be the main point of contact for escalated customer escalations, helping them find a clear path to getting their solar systems back up and running. Combining deep technical solar expertise with empathetic communication. You will report to the Customer Experience Manager and act as a central hub, coordinating with internal teams to resolve routine friction and keep the planet’s energy assets performing at their best.

What You'll Do

  • At Omnidian we believe in trust and autonomy. How you create an impact is ultimately up to you. Here is an outline of some of the things you’ll be doing:

    • Escalation Ownership & Resolution

  • Own the Outcome: Manage an individual queue of high-sentiment escalated cases, acting as the primary point of contact until the issue is confirmed and resolved.
  • Settlement Authority: Authorized to negotiate and settle financial disputes up to established limits to achieve first-contact resolution within the escalation layer.
  • Professional Updates: Respond to inbound escalations from homeowners, clients, and external partners with clear, professional, and empathetic communication that resolves friction and explains technical trade-offs.
  • Executive Case Management: Handle executive-level customer concerns, balancing customer advocacy with company policy to drive timely, equitable resolutions.

    • Regulatory & Legal Case Management

  • Regulatory Complaint Ownership: Receive, investigate, and respond to complaints from Attorneys General, the Better Business Bureau (BBB), consumer protection agencies, and other regulatory organizations while ensuring all response deadlines are met.
  • Legal Coordination: Manage legal escalations and claims by partnering directly with Omnidian's Legal team to gather documentation, investigate case history, coordinate internal stakeholders, and support case resolution.
  • Risk Assessment: Identify situations with elevated legal, financial, or reputational risk and escalate appropriately while maintaining accurate, defensible documentation.

    • Technical Solar Expert

  • System Recovery: Identify root causes of technical failures and execute policy overrides to restore system accuracy and performance.
  • Advanced Troubleshooting: Apply specialized knowledge in high-complexity areas, including roof leak protocols, electrical and safety concerns, and remote troubleshooting for all standard solar equipment.
  • Operational Coordination: Coordinate directly with Field Service Partners and internal Operations teams to ensure dispatches result in a verified fix and systems are returned to normal operation.

    • Team Leadership & Operational Excellence

  • Peer Development: Act as a subject matter expert by coaching, mentoring, and training peers on complex case handling, technical troubleshooting, and escalation best practices.
  • Process Improvement: Identify trends, recommend operational improvements, and contribute to the development of new processes, documentation, and training materials that improve the customer experience.
  • Cross-Functional Partnership: Collaborate across Customer Experience, Operations, Legal, Product, and Client Success to remove barriers, improve workflows, and ensure consistent customer outcomes.
  • Feedback Loops: Identify, document, and flag recurring technical anomalies or operational bottlenecks discovered during daily case handling.
  • Evidence-Based Change: Provide leadership with documented evidence and frontline insights needed to justify SOP adjustments and stop emerging trends before they impact the broader queue.

    • Working hours

  • Omnidian's main customer service contact hours are Monday through Friday, 7 AM to 5 PM Pacific Time. As our company grows, schedules may cover 9-hour shifts (including breaks) between 6 AM and 6 PM PST, Monday through Sunday. We ensure team members receive two steady days off per week.

Who You Are

  • ARTful: Accountability, Respect Transparency
  • High level of attention to detail and the ability to multitask
  • Self-directed under general supervision
  • You seek to understand others point of view
  • You are a team player
  • Your written and verbal communication is clear, concise and articulate.
  • You take detailed and efficient notes
  • Can adhere to a 1 business day or less response time
  • You are an empathetic problem solver

Experience You'll Need

  • 2+ years of experience resolving high-sentiment disputes (handling sensitive or complex customer concerns).
  • 2+ years of solar experience (e.g., technical support role, field service role, technical coursework, solar certificate, or other relevant experience)
  • Technical Proficiency: Proven ability to troubleshoot solar inverters and monitoring portals.

Experience That's a Plus

  • Experience with Zendesk or Salesforce.
  • Extensive knowledge of Solar Storage Systems.
  • Ability to communicate with customers in Spanish via phone and email

Work-life and Culture

  • All of our roles offer the opportunity to work remotely
  • If you are in the Seattle, WA area, we offer a vibrant and creative co-working space in the heart of downtown Seattle
  • If you are near one of our employee clusters, we offer one or more local gatherings per year
  • We provide outstanding benefits that we are continually improving upon, including family medical, dental, vision, disability, parental leave, 401(k) administration, thoughtful PTO, and paid sabbatical leave after four years
  • We offer a competitive total compensation package that includes monthly health insurance premiums, quarterly bonus and long-term stock options for every employee
  • We love to lift each other up through company-wide slack channels such as #puppiesandpets, #omnidian-wellness, #praiseandbooms and #sustainablefuture
  • We have affinity groups to help employees feel seen and supported, such as Rainbow Array, BIPOC, Thriving Survivors, Vets at Omnidian, Black Lights Matter and Neurospicy R Us
  • We are a passionate, mission driven team that believes in collaboration, mutual respect and trust. For examples, check out our posts What Makes an Ethical Company? and Why We’re Proud to Be a Certified B Corp

Grow With Us

  • We mentor and invest in our employees and prioritize them for future opportunities. Check out our Instagram reels to see a few career journey examples
  • Internal candidates: Check out our advice on Internal Transfer: Job Application Process
  • Here are the roles in this career track:
  • Customer Experience Specialist
  • Senior Customer Experience Specialist
  • We’re a fast-growing startup, which means we’re constantly reinventing processes, adding new products, and asking people to use all of their skills and talents. That means there’s gonna be a lot of opportunities for you to grow, which also means you will likely be stretched in ways you’ve never experienced in a job before. If you are resilient, determined, and not afraid of a big challenge, come apply.

Privacy

California-based candidates: To understand more about the data we collect and process as part of your application, please view our California Job Candidate Privacy Policy.

Diversity and Inclusion

We strongly believe that diversity of experience, perspectives, and background will lead to a better environment for our employees and a better product for our customers. We are committed to the principle of equal employment opportunity for all employees and to providing employees with a work environment free of discrimination and harassment. We value diversity and inclusion and are committed to ensuring our hiring and retention practices, as well as our office culture, reflects this value.
We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodation.
Omnidian is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to diversity in the workplace. We make employment decisions on the basis of merit and business need. We hire without consideration to age, ancestry, citizenship, disability, gender expression, gender identity, marital status, national origin, political activity or affiliation, race, religion, sexual orientation, veteran status, or any other basis protected by law.
We invite you to be part of our mission to create a workplace that is inclusive and welcoming to all.

Founded on the philosophy of a better way to borrow, we are dedicated to helping accomplished professionals, small businesses, and institutions build upon their success through innovative financial solutions, a hassle-free process, and personalized concierge service.
Our relentless commitment to the success of our customers is part of what has made BHG Financial thrive. We take a 360-degree view of our customers to tailor the best solutions for their financial aspirations. Today's professionals have multiple sources of income, not just their paycheck. Therefore, it is essential to factor those in when making responsible lending decisions. Our continued focus on data, analytics, and proprietary modeling has enabled faster funding for our customers.
From business to personal loans to relationships with community banks, the country’s top professionals and business owners rely on us for our exceptional financial solutions and concierge service to continue their success and legacy.

Who You Are

We are seeking an experienced Azure Databricks Administrator to manage, maintain, secure, and optimize Databricks environments in Azure. This role is focused on platform administration, governance, operational support, performance, reliability, and cost efficiency across the organization’s data analytics infrastructure.

The successful candidate will serve as a platform administrator and operational partner to data engineering, analytics, cybersecurity, compliance, and business teams, helping ensure Databricks is reliable, well-governed, secure, and effectively supported.

What You'll Do

  • Configure, maintain, and administer Azure Databricks workspaces and clusters across development, staging, and production environments.
  • Monitor cluster health, performance metrics, resource utilization, and platform availability.
  • Optimize cluster, SQL warehouse, and workspace configurations for performance and cost efficiency.
  • Manage workspace governance, including job scheduling, notebook organization, audit logging, and operational standards.
  • Administer user access, workspace permissions, SQL warehouse configurations, and group-based security controls.
  • Troubleshoot infrastructure issues, performance bottlenecks, connectivity problems, and workload failures.
  • Support disaster recovery and high-availability planning, validation, and operational readiness for Databricks workloads.
  • Collaborate with data engineering teams to establish Databricks usage standards, support workload reliability, troubleshoot platform issues, optimize Delta Lake performance, and promote governed platform adoption.
  • Administer and enforce security policies, RBAC, encryption standards, and access controls.
  • Maintain documentation and runbooks for operational procedures.
  • Support capacity planning, cost optimization, and platform improvement initiatives.

    • Security Governance

    • Maintain security governance standards for Azure Databricks in a financial services environment, including RBAC, least-privilege access, privileged access controls, and group-based permissions.
    • Administer Unity Catalog permissions, metastore access, catalogs, schemas, tables, volumes, and external locations to enforce governed data access.
    • Manage workspace permissions, admin roles, service principals, groups, SCIM provisioning, and Microsoft Entra ID integration to support secure identity governance.
    • Configure and review compute policies, cluster permissions, instance pool access, SQL warehouse permissions, and job ownership to reduce unnecessary privilege and control platform usage.
    • Oversee secrets management, token usage, storage credential access, and Key Vault-backed configurations to protect sensitive financial, customer, and operational data.
    • Coordinate recurring access reviews, access certification, and timely remediation of excessive, inappropriate, or outdated permissions to support internal control requirements.
    • Review Databricks audit logs, security events, access changes, and control findings to identify risks, policy exceptions, segregation-of-duties concerns, and required remediation actions.
    • Support audit and regulatory readiness by maintaining evidence for access controls, configuration standards, policy enforcement, operational procedures, and change management activities.
    • Partner with cybersecurity, compliance, risk, infrastructure, and data governance teams to align Databricks controls with financial services security, privacy, and compliance expectations.

What You'll Need

    • 5+ years of experience administering cloud-based data platforms or analytics environments, with a focus on operational support, governance, and reliability.
    • 3+ years of hands-on experience administering Azure Databricks workspaces, Unity Catalog, clusters, jobs, SQL warehouses, and platform settings.
    • Strong experience managing Databricks users, groups, workspace permissions, admin roles, service principals, SCIM provisioning, and Microsoft Entra ID integration.
    • Experience administering Unity Catalog, including metastores, catalogs, schemas, tables, volumes, permissions, storage credentials, and external locations.
    • Ability to configure and maintain compute policies, cluster permissions, instance pools, SQL warehouses, job ownership, and platform usage controls.
    • Experience monitoring Databricks platform health, cluster performance, job execution, workload failures, audit logs, and resource utilization.
    • Strong troubleshooting skills for Databricks platform issues, Spark workloads, connectivity problems, permission errors, and performance bottlenecks.
    • Working knowledge of Python, SQL, PowerShell, Databricks CLI, REST APIs, and automation practices used to support platform administration.
    • Experience supporting operational controls, access reviews, audit evidence, change management, runbooks, and platform documentation.
    • Knowledge of Databricks security governance, RBAC, least privilege, encryption, secrets management, audit readiness, and secure data access patterns.
    • Understanding of Azure networking and security concepts, including private endpoints, firewalls, network security groups, storage access, Key Vault, and secure connectivity.
    • Experience partnering with data engineering teams to support reliable pipelines, workload troubleshooting, performance tuning, platform standards, and secure Databricks operations.
    • Travel requirement: All roles require travel during the first 6 months of employment to attend the BHG Oars in Experience. After the initial 6 months, ongoing travel is expected at approximately ~5% annually for periodic team on-sites, team meetings, and cross-functional collaboration.
    • Work Authorization: This role is not eligible for employer-provided immigration sponsorship. To be considered, applicants must already possess valid U.S. work authorization that will not require sponsorship now or in the future.

      • Technical Skills & Technologies

      • Databricks Platform Administration: Workspaces, workspace settings, admin console, clusters, jobs, notebooks, SQL warehouses, instance pools, compute policies, and audit logs.
      • Unity Catalog Administration: Metastores, catalogs, schemas, tables, volumes, permissions, storage credentials, external locations, and governed data access.
      • Identity and Access Management: Users, groups, service principals, workspace permissions, admin roles, RBAC, SCIM provisioning, Microsoft Entra ID integration, and least-privilege access controls.
      • Security and Governance: Secrets management, token usage, encryption, Key Vault-backed configurations, access reviews, audit evidence, policy enforcement, and regulatory readiness.
      • Monitoring and Troubleshooting: Cluster health, job failures, SQL warehouse performance, Spark workload issues, audit log review, resource utilization, connectivity issues, and performance bottlenecks.
      • Automation and Administration Tools: Databricks CLI, REST APIs, Terraform awareness, Python, PowerShell, SQL, runbooks, operational scripts, and platform documentation.
      • Azure Platform Integration: Azure Storage, Key Vault, private endpoints, virtual networks, firewalls, network security groups, Azure Monitor, Log Analytics, and secure connectivity patterns.

        • Preferred Qualifications

        • Databricks Platform Administrator certification or equivalent hands-on Azure Databricks administration experience.
        • Experience administering Unity Catalog, workspace security, compute policies, SQL warehouses, service principals, audit logs, and platform governance controls.
        • Experience supporting Databricks in financial services or another regulated environment with strong audit, access review, and compliance requirements.
        • Experience creating runbooks, operational standards, monitoring procedures, access review processes, and administrator documentation for Databricks environments.
        • Background in database administration, cloud platform administration, or data platform operations supporting enterprise analytics workloads.

Life at BHG Financial

At BHG Financial, we work hard and aren’t afraid to take risks. Since the beginning, our core values of PMA (positive mental attitude), team player, and loyalty have been the driving force behind every interaction we have between each other and our customers. We have a healthy respect for the daily grind, yet we value work/life balance. We believe that all employees should have the opportunity to lead and that good ideas can come from anyone. If you’re ready for a career where you can exercise your passions, be surrounded by co-workers who are relentlessly committed to service, and have a team-player mindset, apply today!

Overview

Claims Process Coordinator

Reports to: Compliance Manager

Fully Remote, Exempt position

Salary Range: $70,000 to $85,000 depending on experience

Position Summary

Sun Auto Tire & Service is one of the nation's fastest-growing automotive service companies, operating more than 575 locations across the United States through a family of trusted local brands. Powered by the Sun Auto Network, we combine the personalized service of neighborhood repair shops with the resources, technology, and innovation of a national organization to deliver exceptional tire and automotive care.

We are seeking a detail-oriented and proactive Compliance Support Specialist to support insurance administration and claims management. This role is focused on reviewing and facilitating insurance claims, coordinating with store managers, district managers, market directors, vendors, and the Safety team, and managing claims from intake through resolution. The position also supports insurance documentation needs, including certificates of insurance, incident tracking and reporting, EHS Insight data entry and review, and day-to-day management of the claims and insurance email inbox. This role is focused on insurance administration and claims management. Vehicle title/registration management, DOT compliance, approved driver maintenance, vehicle disposition, toll accounts, licenses, permits, and other vehicle management responsibilities have been removed from this job description.

Key Responsibilities

Insurance Claims Management

  • Review incoming claims and supporting documentation for completeness, accuracy, and follow-up needs.
  • Coordinate with store managers, district managers, market directors, and other internal partners to gather missing information and resolve claim-related questions.
  • Manage claims from intake through resolution, including follow-up on open items, vendor responses, status updates, and documentation needs.
  • Communicate with insurance carriers, adjusters, third-party administrators, repair vendors, towing/storage vendors, and other outside partners as needed to support claim handling.
  • Track claim status, outstanding action items, costs, and resolution notes to maintain clear and accurate claim records.
  • Escalate complex, high-cost, litigated, or sensitive claims to the appropriate internal stakeholders.

Incident Reporting & EHS Insight Support

  • Work in EHS Insight to review, update, and maintain incident and claim-related information.
  • Partner closely with the Safety team to ensure incidents are documented consistently and routed appropriately.
  • Assist with reporting on incident volume, claim trends, cost types, claim status, and other insurance or incident-related metrics.
  • Identify gaps in incident documentation and follow up with field leadership or internal teams to obtain required details.

Insurance Administration

  • Obtain and distribute certificates of insurance as requested by internal teams, landlords, vendors, customers, or business partners.
  • Maintain organized insurance documentation, including certificates, policy-related records, claim files, correspondence, and supporting materials.
  • Coordinate with insurance carriers, brokers, and internal stakeholders on documentation requests, policy questions, and claim support needs.
  • Support insurance-related reporting, recordkeeping, and follow-up to help ensure timely and accurate responses.

Claims & Insurance Inbox Management

  • Monitor and manage the shared claims and insurance email inbox.
  • Categorize, prioritize, and route incoming messages based on urgency, claim type, insurance request, or required follow-up.
  • Respond to routine inquiries, request missing information, and ensure timely follow-up on pending items.
  • Maintain clear communication and professional documentation in all email correspondence.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in business administration, risk management, insurance, compliance, mechanical background or a related field preferred; comparable experience may be considered.
  • Minimum of 3 years of experience in insurance claims, claims administration, risk management support, compliance support, mechanical background or a related role preferred.
  • Experience working with incident reporting systems, claims management platforms, EHS Insight, or similar systems preferred.
  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple open claims, deadlines, and follow-up items at the same time.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate professionally with field leaders, vendors, insurance partners, and internal teams.
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to maintain accurate records, documentation, and follow-up notes.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office, Outlook, Excel, Teams, and shared inbox management.
  • Ability to handle sensitive claim and incident information with discretion and professionalism.
  • Proactive problem-solving approach with the ability to identify missing information, ask clarifying questions, and drive items to resolution.

Position Benefits:

    • Opportunities for professional development and growth.
    • Collaborative and supportive work environment.
    • Opportunity to support process improvement within insurance, claims, and incident reporting workflows.

At Sun Auto we recognize that benefits play a vital role in helping ensure the health and financial security of employees and their families. We offer a range of market-competitive total rewards that include merit increases, paid holidays, Paid Time Off, and incentive bonus programs as well as:

Description

TripleTen is an EdTech company that designs and runs tech career learning programs for the US and Latin American markets. We’ve been doing it for over five years, teaching complete beginners (people with no prior tech background) through cohort-based programs built on our own platform and curriculum, developed in partnership with Nebius AI. Our team is fully remote and globally distributed, and we serve a large, active student base across both regions.

We’re looking for an experienced Course Author in Applied AI to help design and develop a graduate-level online program in Applied Artificial Intelligence, delivered in partnership with a US university. The program is built for working professionals in fields such as marketing, operations, finance and HR. They learn to evaluate, build, integrate, deploy and govern AI solutions using modern no-code and low-code tools. You’ll turn approved course syllabi into engaging, rigorous learning materials and help shape how a new generation of AI practitioners learns to make sound, defensible decisions.

This is a part-time, project-based opportunity for subject matter experts who are passionate about teaching, curriculum design and helping learners succeed.

Please submit all resumes or CVs in English.

After applying for this position, you will be required to complete a test assignment after your Online Introductory Call.

Project details are shared after signing an NDA.

What you will do

  • Develop graduate-level course content in Applied AI based on approved syllabi: guided lessons, hands-on labs, case studies, weekly assignments and final projects, mostly in text and video format.
  • Write clear assignment briefs and analytic rubrics for all graded work, including explicit rules on when and how students may use AI tools.
  • Design practical labs on current AI platforms (LLM assistants, RAG applications, workflow automation, AI agents, APIs and monitoring tools), and make sure every graded task can be completed with free or open-source tools.
  • Curate reading lists of research papers, standards and vendor documentation, and explain why each source matters.
  • Create supporting materials: preparatory (non-credit) modules for learners without a technical background, a program glossary, templates and worked examples.
  • Collaborate with the LX designer and the student experience team on learning objectives, course structure and assessment design (if you don’t have experience with this, that’s ok).
  • Consult on Applied AI-related questions, and keep content up to date as tools and regulations change.
  • Revise content based on academic review by the partner university’s faculty, and make sure it meets graduate-level academic standards.

Requirements

  • 5+ years of recent professional experience in applied AI/ML, data, AI automation, or a related field, including hands-on experience with LLMs.
  • A master’s degree or PhD in a relevant field, or 10+ years of senior professional experience in AI or a related industry.
  • Practical knowledge of AI tools and workflows, including prompt engineering, RAG, AI agents, automation, APIs, and LLM evaluation.
  • Experience applying AI to real business problems, considering business value, cost, risk, and reliability.
  • Experience teaching, mentoring, or creating educational content, with the ability to explain complex concepts to non-technical audiences.
  • Strong English communication skills (C1+), including clear professional and educational writing.
  • Strong organizational and collaboration skills, with the ability to work proactively, incorporate feedback, and meet agreed deadlines.

Nice-to-have

  • Experience designing courses or learning materials for higher education or online programs.
  • Familiarity with AI strategy, business cases, or responsible AI practices or governance.
  • Experience with EdTech or learning platforms, or contributions to the AI community through publications, talks, or open-source projects.

What we can offer you

  • Fully remote, part-time collaboration (at least 25h/week).
  • Compensation: fixed fee per course package, paid in milestones.
  • A diverse team across Europe, the US, Latin America and more.
  • Modern digital tools for seamless collaboration.

Multiple Venture-Backed AI & Technology Startups | Current & Upcoming Opportunities

Locations: New York, NY | San Francisco, CA | Remote

Salary Range: $175,000-$275,000 base

About the Opportunities

Continuum Recruiting works with a portfolio of venture-backed AI and technology companies hiring exceptional Founding, Early-Stage, and high-ownership Software Engineers. We are interested in meeting strong engineers for multiple current and upcoming opportunities rather than a single specific opening.

These companies range from very early founding teams to rapidly scaling startups. While the exact stack and product vary, the common denominator is a need for well-rounded builders who can take ambiguous problems, make sound technical and product decisions, and ship production software end-to-end.

Many of the opportunities are AI-native and involve applied AI, LLMs, agentic systems, developer tooling, data infrastructure, or AI-enabled vertical software. Others are broader product and platform engineering roles where strong software fundamentals and 0-to-1 execution matter most.

What You May Work On

  • Own products, features, or core systems from initial concept and architecture through production deployment.
  • Build across the stack, including backend services, APIs, data infrastructure, frontend/product surfaces, and cloud systems.
  • Develop AI-native products and workflows using LLMs, agents, tool integrations, retrieval systems, and modern AI development tools where relevant.
  • Make pragmatic architecture and product decisions in environments with limited process and incomplete requirements.
  • Work directly with founders, customers, and other stakeholders to identify problems and translate them into shipped software.
  • Build integrations with external APIs, business systems, data sources, and third-party platforms.
  • Establish engineering patterns, tooling, testing, observability, and best practices as teams scale.
  • Help shape engineering culture and, in some roles, mentor or lead engineers who join after you.

Requirements

What We’re Generally Looking For

  • Strong professional software engineering experience with evidence of shipping production systems.
  • End-to-end ownership: you can move from an ambiguous problem to a working production solution without requiring a detailed specification.
  • Strong backend, full-stack, product engineering, or systems engineering fundamentals.
  • Experience with one or more modern production languages such as Python, TypeScript/JavaScript, Go, Java, or Rust.
  • Comfort working across multiple layers of a product rather than being limited to a very narrow specialty.
  • High agency, strong problem-solving ability, and comfort operating in fast-moving environments.
  • A track record of meaningful technical impact, rapid growth, entrepreneurial work, strong startup experience, or other clear signals of engineering excellence.
  • Clear communication and the ability to explain technical decisions and tradeoffs.

Particularly Relevant Backgrounds

  • Founding Engineer, Early Engineer, Product Engineer, Full-Stack Engineer, Backend Engineer, or Staff/Senior Software Engineer.
  • Experience at an early-stage or high-growth startup, or evidence that you can operate effectively in a startup-style environment.
  • 0-to-1 product or platform development.
  • Production AI/LLM or agentic-system experience.
  • Python and/or TypeScript/React experience.
  • API integrations, distributed systems, data infrastructure, or developer tooling.
  • Daily use of modern AI coding tools such as Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Codex, or similar tools.
  • Entrepreneurial experience, meaningful side projects, open-source work, or previous founder experience.

What Varies by Opportunity

Because this is an evergreen talent-pool search covering multiple companies, individual opportunities have different requirements. Current opportunities are based in New York, NY, San Francisco, CA, or are remote; specific in-office or hybrid expectations vary by opportunity. Seniority, compensation, equity, visa sponsorship, education preferences, and specific technical stacks also vary.

Our goal is to understand what you are strongest at and what you want next, then determine which current opportunities are genuinely aligned rather than forcing your background into a single job description.

Who Will Thrive in These Roles

These opportunities are best suited for engineers who like ownership more than narrowly defined tickets. You should enjoy building, learning quickly, making decisions with imperfect information, and seeing the direct impact of what you ship.

We are particularly interested in engineers who want meaningful influence over a product and technical direction, and who are energized by the pace and responsibility that come with joining a small or rapidly scaling engineering team.

jobs.excerpt: Job Type: Full-time | Location: Remote, US | Department: Innovation | Reporting to: Director, Data Center Commissioning | Work Location: #remote IREN is a vertically integrated AI Cloud provider, delivering large-scale data centers and GPU clusters for AI training and inference.
jobs.description:
Job Type: Full-time | Location: Remote, US | Department: Innovation | Reporting to: Director, Data Center Commissioning | Work Location: #remote

IREN is a vertically integrated AI Cloud provider, delivering large-scale data centers and GPU clusters for AI training and inference. IREN’s platform is underpinned by its expansive portfolio of grid-connected land and power in renewable-rich regions across North America, Europe and APAC.

The Commissioning Subject Matter Expert sets the discipline standard for commissioning across every IREN region and site. You will write and own IREN's commissioning specifications, acceptance criteria and the standard against which the Commissioning Authority's test scripts are approved; be the technical escalation point for the campus commissioning teams; review Commissioning Authority deliverables and first-of-kind installations; and give Engineering and Procurement technical input on designs, equipment and commissioning scopes. This is a program-level, senior individual-contributor role that stays with the Director rather than with one project, and it is one of the first hires into the function: the standards you write will be applied on every IREN site, by IREN's own commissioning crews and by the Commissioning Authorities IREN engages.

Controls covers the building management system, electrical power monitoring system, SCADA and PLC architecture, network and telemetry, leak detection, and their integration with monitoring and DCIM platforms: the point-to-point and I/O verification, sequence-of-operations and failure-mode testing, alarm testing and integrated systems testing that prove the facility behaves as designed under normal and failure conditions.

Responsibilities

  • Author and maintain IREN's commissioning specifications for the discipline: Division 1 commissioning specification content, acceptance criteria, Level 1 to Level 5 definitions and integrated systems test requirements, for new build and conversion projects and for both self-performed and general-contractor delivery.
  • Act as the technical escalation point for the campus commissioning teams; settle standard-versus-schedule questions with the Cx Project Manager and the Director, and record the decision.
  • Review the Commissioning Authority's commissioning plans, test scripts and reports for compliance with the standard; audit field execution, witness sampling and first-of-kind installations across sites.
  • Give commissioning input to Engineering on basis of design and specifications, and to Procurement on equipment, factory test requirements and Commissioning Authority scopes of work and request-for-proposal templates.
  • Lead the factory witness testing strategy for critical equipment in the discipline and approve factory acceptance test procedures.
  • Lead root-cause analysis on significant discipline failures or repeat deficiencies and turn the findings into changes to the standard.
  • Own the controls commissioning standard: BMS, EPMS, SCADA and PLC architecture requirements, points and alarm standards, telemetry naming, point-to-point and sequence-of-operations testing, failure-mode and integrated systems testing, DCIM integration and OT security verification.
  • Track emerging standards and codes for the regions IREN builds in (ASHRAE Guideline 0, Guideline 1.6P and Standard 202, ASHRAE 90.4, NEC and NETA ATS in the United States; the Canadian Electrical Code and CSA standards in Canada) and update IREN standards accordingly.
  • Develop and deliver the discipline's technical training modules with the Training Program Lead; sit on interview panels and mentor the project commissioning leads and IREN's site commissioning crews.
  • Support the procurement and mobilization of Commissioning Authorities in new regions so that the IREN standard applies from day one.

Requirements

REQUIRED
  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical or Electrical Engineering, Controls or a related engineering field.
  • 10+ years of data center or mission-critical commissioning, start-up or engineering in the discipline, including large-scale programs and full Level 1 to Level 5 delivery.
  • Demonstrated authorship of commissioning specifications, test procedures or standards that were used across more than one project.
  • Deep knowledge of data center controls: building management and electrical power monitoring systems, SCADA and PLC platforms, network protocols (BACnet, Modbus, OPC) and their integration with monitoring and DCIM platforms, including how they are tested and accepted.
  • Working knowledge of integrated systems testing across controls, mechanical and electrical, and of alarm management standards such as ISA 18.2.
  • Experience reviewing and directing third-party commissioning authorities and equipment vendors.
  • Able to travel up to 25% to IREN sites.
  • Authorized to work in the United States.
PREFERRED
  • BCxP or CCP held, plus a discipline credential such as ISA CAP or CCST; PE license or chartered status.
  • Ignition, Niagara or Schneider platforms; OT cybersecurity; digital-twin and DCIM integration.
  • Experience standing up commissioning in a new region or with a new commissioning authority.

LOCATION & TRAVEL
  • Remote within the United States, with travel of up to 25% to IREN sites in Texas and elsewhere in North America and to the Fort Worth office. Candidates in the Dallas–Fort Worth area or within easy reach of IREN's Texas sites are preferred.

Benefits

At IREN, we offer a comprehensive, market-competitive total rewards package designed to support employees’ well-being, career advancement, and financial wealth. Our offerings reflect our commitment to Proceed with Purpose while rewarding high performance and long-term growth. 

Compensation 
  • Salaried position; eligible for IREN's short-term and long-term incentive plans, medical, dental and vision coverage, 401(k) and paid time off, in line with IREN's US benefits program.

Health & Wellness 
  • 100% company paid health insurance premiums (medical, dental, and vision) for employees, 75% company paid coverage for dependents
  • Company-paid short-term and long-term disability insurance
  • Voluntary life, critical illness, and accident coverage available
  • Health Savings Accounts (HSA) – when combined with the High-Deductible Health Plan
  • Employee Assistance Program and wellness resources

Retirement & Financial Wealth 
  • 401(k) retirement plan with company match
  • Paid professional development and access to financial planning and legal services

Time Off & Leave Programs 
  • Paid Time Off (PTO) and paid holidays

Growth & Development 
  • Professional development to support certifications, continuing education, or role related training

Community & Culture 
  • Company events and team-building activities

jobs.title: Principal Software Engineer
jobs.excerpt: Job Overview:ExploreK12 Literacy is looking for a Principal Software Engineer who combines deep technical expertise, strong engineering judgment, and hands-on execution.
jobs.description:
Job Overview:

ExploreK12 Literacy is looking for a Principal Software Engineer who combines deep technical expertise, strong engineering judgment, and hands-on execution.


This role is for an engineer who can get deeply into a complex, mature application, understand how it actually works, and help determine how it should evolve. You will work directly in the code while also helping teams navigate difficult technical decisions, modernization efforts, architectural constraints, and ambiguous engineering problems.


You will be a senior technical leader within the Literacy product area, partnering closely with engineers, engineering leaders, and architects to help shape technical direction across multiple teams and products. You will help shape technical direction, surface risks and tradeoffs, and turn complex problems into practical paths forward. You will also work across product boundaries where shared capabilities or product convergence require coordination with other engineering teams.


Modernization is an important part of this role, but it is not the goal by itself. The goal is to enable the future of the product while making the system easier to understand, change, test, deploy, and operate. Sometimes that means modernizing a system. Sometimes it means integrating with it, isolating it, incrementally replacing part of it, or deliberately leaving it alone.


We are also looking for someone who is fluent in modern AI-assisted software development and interested in applying AI thoughtfully where it can improve engineering effectiveness or create meaningful product value. You do not need to be an AI specialist.


Job Responsibilities:

Solve Difficult Technical Problems

  • Get deeply into our applications, codebases, data flows, integrations, dependencies, and operational behavior to understand how the system actually works.
  • Investigate complex technical problems through multiple layers of the system until the underlying causes and constraints are understood.
  • Turn ambiguous or complicated engineering problems into clear problem statements, options, tradeoffs, and recommended approaches.
  • Bring strong technical judgment to decisions involving complexity, risk, customer value, cost, maintainability, team capacity, and future product needs.
  • Surface significant technical risks early and take clear, well-supported positions when you believe the organization is heading toward a poor technical outcome.

Remain a Hands-On Engineer

  • Contribute meaningful production code and take direct responsibility for technical work where your involvement can have high impact.
  • Depending on the needs of the product, own or contribute to projects, features, migrations, prototypes, architectural changes, and difficult engineering investigations.
  • Work at both the architecture and implementation levels, moving between system-level reasoning and code-level details as the problem requires.
  • Use hands-on involvement to build firsthand understanding of the system rather than operating primarily through architecture documents and reviews.
  • Exercise judgment about when personally implementing a solution is the highest-leverage contribution and when enabling another engineer or team will create greater value.

Help Evolve a Mature Product

  • Partner with architects and product engineering leaders to understand the current application landscape and help craft practical approaches for its evolution.
  • Identify where architectural constraints and technical debt are materially affecting engineering effectiveness or limiting future product capabilities.
  • Recommend modernization investments based on evidence, expected value, risk, cost, reversibility, team capacity, and product direction.
  • Apply approaches such as incremental replacement, modularization, API enablement, migration, strangler patterns, or parallel adoption when they are appropriate to the problem.
  • Help teams decompose significant technical change into achievable increments that reduce risk and produce useful progress.
  • Recognize when existing technology is adequate and modernization would create more cost or risk than value.
  • Help reduce friction in how engineers understand, change, test, deploy, and operate important parts of the product.
  • Contribute to a credible longer-term path for the product's technical evolution rather than treating modernization as a collection of isolated projects.

Provide Principal-Level Technical Leadership

  • Be a high-leverage technical partner on important architectural decisions, novel problems, technically risky initiatives, and work with significant cross-product implications.
  • Identify architectural constraints, technical risks, and systemic issues that span multiple teams, products, or strategic initiatives, and help drive resolution before they become significant delivery, operational, or customer-impacting problems.
  • Work with Product and Design during solution discovery and implementation planning to translate product needs into sound technical approaches and challenge proposed solutions when technical insight reveals a materially better path.
  • Partner with architects on broader architectural concerns such as shared capabilities, identity, data, integration patterns, and areas where products increasingly need to work together.
  • Influence technical direction across the Literacy product area by helping teams align around shared architectural assumptions, integration approaches, technical standards, and long-term evolution paths.
  • Help teams make stronger technical decisions through architectural guidance, decision frameworks, and shared understanding without becoming an approval gate or centralizing decisions around yourself.
  • Explain and defend technical recommendations clearly while respecting the accountability of engineering leaders and teams for final decisions and delivery.
  • When important technical disagreements cannot be resolved within a team, help make tradeoffs explicit and support escalation to the appropriate engineering leader.

Develop Stronger Technical Leaders

  • Intentionally develop senior engineers and technical leads by involving them in difficult technical problems and helping them strengthen their own judgment.
  • Coach through design discussions, investigation, pairing, implementation, and code review rather than simply supplying answers.
  • Give engineers increasing ownership of difficult technical work so that the organization becomes more capable rather than more dependent on the Principal Engineer.
  • Improve technical practices, design discussions, standards, documentation, or engineering forums when doing so addresses a meaningful recurring problem.

Apply AI Practically

  • Use modern AI-assisted development tools extensively and thoughtfully as part of your engineering workflow.
  • Understand the capabilities and limitations of current AI technologies well enough to reason about where they can and cannot add value.
  • Help identify practical opportunities for AI to improve engineering effectiveness or enable useful product capabilities.
  • Prototype or contribute to AI-enabled solutions when appropriate, with appropriate attention to privacy, security, quality, cost, and responsible use.
  • Help the engineering organization learn from practical AI adoption rather than pursuing AI for its own sake.

Job Requirements:

  • 10+ years of professional software engineering experience, including demonstrated experience operating as a senior technical leader on complex software systems. Previous experience with the title of Principal Engineer is not required.
  • Demonstrated recent, hands-on experience designing, developing, and supporting production systems using PHP, MySQL, Java, and MS SQL Server at a Principal or Staff Engineer level.
  • Exceptional ability to investigate complex technical problems and work through abstractions until you understand what is actually happening.
  • Strong application architecture skills, including the ability to reason about codebases, APIs, data models, integrations, dependencies, failure modes, testing, and operational behavior.
  • Strong technical judgment and a demonstrated ability to make pragmatic tradeoffs among immediate needs, long-term maintainability, risk, complexity, customer value, cost, and team capacity.
  • Experience evolving mature software systems and navigating the realities of long-lived codebases, accumulated technical constraints, and incremental change.
  • Experience with modernization or significant system evolution, including knowing when substantial change is justified and when it is not.
  • Recent hands-on software engineering experience and the desire to continue contributing meaningful production code.
  • Ability to turn ambiguous technical situations into clear problems, options, recommendations, and executable paths.
  • Ability to take strong technical positions, communicate the reasoning behind them, and influence decisions without relying on formal authority.
  • Experience developing the technical judgment and capabilities of other experienced engineers.
  • Practical fluency with modern AI-assisted software development and a working understanding of contemporary AI capabilities, limitations, and development patterns.
  • Ability to quickly build a coherent mental model of a complicated application and communicate that model effectively to engineers and leaders.

Preferred Experience:

Experience in any of the following areas can be valuable, but is not required:

  • Complex, long-lived application platforms with significant dependencies, integrations, or accumulated technical constraints.
  • Incremental modernization, migrations, modularization, or architectural evolution of actively used products.
  • Integrating products or systems with different architectures, data models, authentication approaches, or technology stacks.
  • Systems involving sensitive data, identity, authentication, privacy, or security concerns.
  • Working across product boundaries on shared capabilities or increasingly integrated customer experiences.
  • Education technology or other domains with complex customer and operational environments.
  • Building or contributing to AI-enabled product capabilities in production.

What Success Looks Like:

Over your first year, success should be visible in both the product and the engineering organization.


Important parts of the system are becoming easier for engineers to understand, change, test, deploy, or operate. The organization has a clearer, credible path for evolving the product's architecture, and meaningful modernization work is underway where it creates real value. Some of that evolution may also unlock product capabilities that were previously difficult or impractical to deliver.


Teams are making more consistent technical decisions across product boundaries because shared architectural assumptions, integration approaches, and long-term technical tradeoffs are understood earlier. Cross-team technical risks are surfaced sooner, and the organization has greater confidence in its technical direction beyond any individual application or team.


Senior engineers and technical leads are taking on increasingly difficult technical problems with stronger judgment and greater independence. Your presence increases the organization's technical capability rather than creating dependency on you.


AI is becoming a practical part of how engineering works, and useful opportunities for AI in the product are being identified and pursued based on customer and business value rather than novelty.

Why Work for Us

When you join ExploreK12™, you become part of a mission to help educators unlock brighter futures for every student.


As a trusted leader in educational technology, we serve more than 17 million students and educators across 150+ countries with innovative, research-backed learning solutions that truly make a difference. Our flagship products—Gizmos™, Raz-Plus®, and Reflex™—are beloved by educators and students alike for being as practical and effective as they are fun.


To learn more about our organization and the exciting work we do, visit .


Remote First Work Environment

Our Remote First approach gives employees the flexibility and trust they need to effectively balance work with life. It creates a culture in which all employees are valued and where success is measured in results. It allows us to work collaboratively, inclusively and for greater positive impact, regardless of our individual locations.


If you will be working remotely, either occasionally or on a permanent basis, you must have a reliable internet connection through a cable or fiber-optic broadband service with minimum speeds of 10 Mbps download and 5 Mbps upload.


The successful candidate will be expected to actively participate in video-based interviews during the recruiting process and ongoing virtual meetings with their camera on, as part of their role. To maintain confidentiality and ensure a fair evaluation process, the use of note-taking tools, reference materials, or AI-powered tools (including generative AI, language models, or similar technologies) during interviews or other selection activities is prohibited unless prior written approval has been obtained from the People Experience team. If you require an exception for medical, accessibility, or other reasons, please contact your Talent Acquisition team member to discuss accommodations in advance.


As part of our Remote-First benefits, Cambium offers reimbursement to help cover the cost of setting up your home or remote office.


An Equal Opportunity Employer

We are dedicated to fostering a culture that celebrates unique backgrounds, ideas, and experiences. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without discrimination on the basis of race, color, age, religion, sex (including pregnancy, gender, gender identity/expression, or sexual orientation), national origin, protected veteran status, disability, or genetic information (including family medical history).


We will provide reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities. You may request an accommodation during the recruiting process with your Talent Acquisition team member.

jobs.description:
Description

​​Centralized monitoring is an integral part of a risk-based monitoring strategy, defined as the timely, remote review of accumulating subject and operational data to help distinguish between reliable and unreliable data, trends, outliers, and unusual variability using analytics and statistical methods.

The central monitor is responsible for conducting a holistic and centralized statistical review of study data from study start through to study database lock according to the centralized monitoring plan, using analytical tools to identify emerging and existing risks to critical study data and process. The central monitor enables proactive identification, communication, escalation and management of risks at the study/country/site level. ​

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • ​​Follow established procedures for the review of clinical trial data (Operational and Subject data) using a variety of tools and systems in alignment with the centralized monitoring plan and with support from the senior team members.
  • ​Identify data quality trends indicative of systematic errors and potential performance issues at study/country/site and track the evidence of issues and potential risks with support from senior team members.
  • ​Ensure results of reviews are appropriately documented per procedures.
  • ​Support Central Monitoring teams with performance of assigned reviews with high quality, on-time results.
  • ​Provide input to senior team member as needed to support development of risk characterization and reporting.
  • ​Support review set-up as directed by assigned lead including updating department database, pulling reports, etc. as assigned.
  • ​Share the responsibility for data quality at the study, country and site levels.​

Requirements

Education

  • ​​Bachelor’s degree in a field relevant to clinical research.

Experience

  • ​Minimum of 1 year of experience in central statistical monitoring with overall 6 years of experience in two or more operational areas such as clinical monitoring, data management, drug safety, medical monitoring, biometrics, or project management.
  • ​Basic understanding of statistical monitoring and Risk Based Quality Management (RBQM) and their impact on data integrity.
  • ​Thorough understanding of the processes associated with clinical study management, data management, and regulatory operations.
  • ​Knowledge of clinical trial database systems (EDC, IRT, CTMS, etc.).
  • ​Good computer skills, with knowledge of advanced MS Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) and the ability to learn and use interactive computer systems and tools.
  • ​Ideally a basic level of understanding of descriptive analysis e.g. means, medians, significance, confidence intervals.
  • ​Must have been involved in the analysis and review of clinical data, ability to extract pertinent information from standard study documentation, such as protocols, electronic study data systems with the ability to learn to identify trending of site/study data.
  • ​Must be able to work in non-traditional work environments.

Attributes

  • Fluent in English (excellent oral and written).
  • Must be able to communicate clearly and effectively at all levels in an organization and with external customers.
  • Must be a fast learner and able to understand new concepts quickly.
  • Prioritization skills with ability to plan, monitor and manage workload fluidly in response to changing project demands.
  • Satisfactory understanding of project protocol, project documentation including centralized monitoring and risk-based monitoring.
  • Broad working knowledge of the roles, functions and process of conducting clinical trials.
  • Must be able to manage time effectively, working with multiple functions and requirements.
  • Must have been involved in the use of trial management or data management systems.
  • Good knowledge of good clinical practices, and applicable Health Canada and Food and Drug Administration (FDA) regulations/guidelines.

Our company

The work environment

At Indero, you will work with brilliant and driven colleagues. Our values are collaboration, innovation, reliability and responsiveness. We offer a stimulating work environment and attractive advancement opportunities.

In this position, you will be eligible for the following perks:

  • Flexible work schedule
  • Permanent full-time position
  • Ongoing learning and development

About Indero

A Global Clinical Leader In Dermatology and Rheumatology!

Formerly known as Innovaderm, Indero is a world-renowned expert and clinical research leader in dermatology. We have more than two decades of experience serving a broad range of indications, patient populations, administration routes, and drug classes, and a global footprint.

Indero is a dual-focus CRO for dermatology and rheumatology, with 25+ years’ experience in clinical research and trial delivery. Our full-service approach – which includes everything from protocol design and patient recruitment to trial monitoring and biometrics – provides biotech and pharmaceutical sponsors with the rigorous scientific foundation and tailored expertise their studies need to reach the finish line efficiently and effectively. With capabilities in North America, Europe, Asia Pacific and Latin America; vast, continuously growing relationships with investigators and patients; and a dedicated research clinic through which we design and execute our own studies, Indero is the ideal CRO partner for clinical needs at global scale.

Indero is committed to providing equitable treatment and equal opportunity to all individuals. As such, Indero will provide accommodations throughout the recruitment and selection process to applicants with disabilities, upon request.

Indero only accepts applicants who can legally work in Romania.

143L - Senior Data Engineer (Python/Go/Data Ingestion/Cloud) · Remote · LATAM

  • Location: LATAM
