jobs.description:
About the Role

At BenefitHub, we connect millions of members across 22 markets with perks and benefits that make life a little better. Email is central to how we engage our members and drive results for our advertising and merchant partners—and this role runs that engine.

We’re seeking a highly hands-on Director of Email & Lifecycle Marketing who lives and breathes newsletter strategy, deliverability, engagement, and monetization. This is a true player-coach role: you’ll shape the strategy, but you’ll also be in the work—building campaigns, solving problems, analyzing performance, testing, optimizing, and jumping in wherever needed, while leading a high-performing team.

You’ll own a high-volume program of 40+ campaigns per week plus automated lifecycle journeys, partnering closely with internal marketing stakeholders, Ad Sales and Merchant teams—advising on best practices and turning sold inventory and placements into engaging, effective campaigns. As a strategic right hand to the VP of Global Marketing, you’ll balance commercial performance with a great member experience while continuously pushing the program forward.

If you’re a hands-on email leader who wants to take a strong, high-volume program and make it even better—sharper targeting, cleaner deliverability, and more value for members and partners alike—we’d love to meet you.

What You’ll Do

Newsletter Excellence, Monetization, and Partner Performance

  • Execute the newsletter program as a high-performing media channel, optimizing how sponsored placements and commissionable offers are delivered to drive strong, defensible performance for our partners while protecting the member experience.
  • Serve as the email and newsletter expert to Ad Sales and the Merchant team, advising on inventory, placement, and campaign best practices and bringing data-backed recommendations that improve monetization to the teams responsible for what is sold and placed.
  • Report program and placement performance credibly to partners and leadership, using defensible, trustworthy metrics.
  • Own the execution and performance of every campaign, translating results into best-practice guidance and recommendations that help Ad Sales, Merchant, and Marketing teams improve outcomes over time.
  • Propose and, once approved, execute the global (22-market) newsletter strategy and roadmap, balancing send volume and frequency with engagement and long-term list health. Translate the strategy into a market-by-market campaign and inventory calendar used cross-functionally by Ad Sales, the Merchant team, and Marketing.

Campaign Execution and Deliverability Excellence

  • Oversee a full portfolio of concurrent campaigns—from planning through send and post-send analysis.
  • Build, QA, schedule, and deploy newsletter and email campaigns in our ESP, personally and through your team.
  • Manage dynamic, catalog-driven offer placement and per-segment/per-client targeting and suppression at scale.
  • Develop mobile-first templates flexible enough to A/B test any element, refreshed quarterly on performance, best practices, and trends; run an ongoing testing program across offers, segmentation, timing, and creative.
  • Own inbox placement, sender reputation, and deliverability across multiple sending domains and markets—IP/domain warm-up, authentication (SPF, DKIM, DMARC), list hygiene, audience data quality, and feedback loops—monitored with tools such as Validity/Everest, Google Postmaster Tools, and Microsoft SNDS.
  • Serve as the internal expert on deliverability best practices and mailbox-provider requirements.

Engagement, Lifecycle, and Product Campaigns

  • Balance commercial goals with a great member experience, delivering the right offer to the right member to drive discovery, clicks, and purchase activity.
  • Own audience segmentation and personalization by market, client, and member behavior, matching messaging and placements to the right audiences with a focus on engagement and deliverability, while ensuring client settings are always respected.
  • Design and run lifecycle and behavior-based journeys—activation, welcome, re-engagement, and win-back—to grow engagement and long-term value while reducing churn.
  • Own a smaller but strategically important set of product marketing and go-to-market sends that grow adoption of BenefitHub’s own products and verticals (e.g., home and auto insurance, the browser extension), in partnership with Marketing stakeholders.

Performance, Team, and Cross-Functional Leadership

  • Define and track KPIs across performance, engagement, deliverability, and lifecycle—including weekly reporting on open rate, CTR, CTOR, and sender reputation—and lead regular performance updates to marketing leadership, the executive team, and the broader company on results, trends, and priorities, adjusting based on data.
  • Ensure advertiser- and partner-facing metrics are accurate and defensible, with an awareness of non-human/invalid traffic (bots, scanners, prefetch) and its impact on reported performance, partnering with analytics to mitigate it.
  • Lead, coach, and develop a growing team of email marketers and email marketing specialists responsible for executing our newsletter, email marketing, and journey programs.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer (CCC Auto / Agentic)
jobs.excerpt: CCC Intelligent Solutions Inc.  (CCC) is a leading cloud platform for the multi-trillion-dollar insurance economy, creating intelligent experiences for insurers, repairers, automakers, part suppliers, and more.
jobs.description:
CCC Intelligent Solutions Inc. (CCC) is a leading cloud platform for the multi-trillion-dollar insurance economy, creating intelligent experiences for insurers, repairers, automakers, part suppliers, and more. At CCC, we’re making life just work by empowering more than 35,000 businesses with industry-leading technology to get drivers back on the road and to health quickly and seamlessly. We’re pushing boundaries with innovative AI solutions that simplify and enhance the claims and repair journey. Through purposeful innovation and the strength of its connections, CCC technologies empower the people and industry relied upon to keep lives moving forward when it matters most. Learn more about CCC at .

The Role

As a Senior Software Engineer - Agentic you will build the event-driven systems that keep claims moving for our customers, connecting our AI agents to the rest of CCC. When these systems work, claims move faster and the machinery stays invisible. Agentic coding tools are how you move fast. What you add is what they are worst at: distributed-systems design, correctness when things fail partway, and the debugging nobody else gets to the bottom of. You own a product area end to end and define the reliability bar it ships against.

Salary range is:

$180,000 - 225,000

This position is bonus eligible.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Own the delivery of backend services, built in Python and TypeScript, from an ambiguous problem, scoped with product managers and data scientists, through production operation.
  • Build and operate durable, event-driven, multi-tenant systems in which agents run as steps inside deterministic workflows, designing their failure modes, replay semantics, and cost profile before they show up under load.
  • Own tracing and audit for your area: every model call and agent step recorded, so any recommendation can be reconstructed and cited back to its sources by on-call and auditors alike.
  • Own how claims automation data is modeled and managed across our relational, document, and graph stores. Ensure the security and isolation of sensitive data.
  • Author the design documents for complex systems to get feedback and buy-in, review other engineers' designs and code with the same care, and mentor the engineers in your area.
  • Raise the bar for how the team works with agentic coding tools: sharpen the specifications, instruction files, hooks, and permission policies they run under, and hold generated code to the same review standard before it merges.
  • Take part in a shared on-call rotation for the systems you own.

Requirements:

  • 6+ years of professional software engineering experience, including an event-driven system you designed, shipped to customers, and ran in production.
  • Python and TypeScript at the level of setting a team's conventions, plus a background in a systems language such as Rust, Go, Java, or C#.
  • Strong computer science and distributed-systems fundamentals you use at work: concurrency, consistency, ordering, and how systems fail.
  • Event-driven systems built on a broker such as Kafka, Azure Event Hubs, or Service Bus that handle duplicate, late, and failed events without losing or double-processing work.
  • Data modeling and development across relational, document, and graph databases such as PostgreSQL, MongoDB, and Neo4j, including when each type fits and the partition-key, consistency, and tenant-isolation calls you made.
  • Systems architected and operated on Azure or AWS, with CI/CD and infrastructure as code, and hands-on time with a durable workflow engine such as Temporal or the Durable Task Scheduler.
  • A clear account of how you constrain an agentic coding tool's context and verify its output, from daily use of Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, or similar on production work, plus changes you turned back, and why.
  • Technical design documents you have authored for systems that span more than one team, used to get feedback and buy-in before building, and that those teams then built to.
  • Clear writing and discussion for technical and non-technical audiences: drawing out a customer's real problem and explaining the trade-offs back to them.

Even Better if You Have:

  • React and TypeScript experience, so you can deliver a full-stack feature end to end, especially chat, streaming, and citation-heavy AI experiences.
  • Formal methods or fault-injection testing, such as Lean, TLA+, or deterministic simulation.
  • Performance work below the application layer: profiling, memory, and concurrency tuning.
  • Familiarity with how AI agents reach their tools and enterprise systems, through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol, command-line tools, and microservices.
  • Exposure to the insurance, claims, or automotive repair domains.

What Success Looks Like:

  • In your first six months, services you built run in production against SLOs you set, and you can show they held as load grew.
  • You are trusted with the hardest correctness and scale problems, and you turn them into a design, a shipped system, and a number you can put in front of a customer.
  • You are energized by what agentic coding tools make possible. Your team ships more than its headcount suggests, and your specifications and reviews are why the output survives production.
  • You have a passion for systems that last: failures are designed for in advance, and when one happens anyway, the trace says exactly where.
  • Standards you set for reliability, reviews, and design documents outlive the project they started on.
  • Engineers you mentor ship reliable services without your direct involvement.
  • You enjoy getting a product manager, a data scientist, and a customer's team into one room and coming out with a single agreed scope, and you can argue a position without needing to win it.
  • You embrace our ambitious, collaborative, and empathetic values, and you like problems where the answer has to be measured rather than argued.

Interview Policy & Privacy Notice:

A video interview is required for this position. Video interviews are transcribed. Transcriptions are retained and may be reviewed by CCC and our recruiters. Candidates are not permitted to use generative AI or automated assistance during the interviews unless explicitly allowed by the interview team for a specific exercise. Our Job Applicant Privacy Notice is available HERE.

About CCC's Commitment to Employees:

CCC Intelligent Solutions understands that our employees play an integral role in our vision to shape a world where life just works. Our team is defined by our values of Integrity, Customer-Focus, Innovation, Inclusion & Diversity, Tenacity, and Connection. Through diverse perspectives, purposeful innovation, and the strength of connections, our technologies empower the people and industry relied upon to keep lives moving forward when it matters most.

At CCC, together everyone can thrive as we innovate and collaborate, creating employee experiences that just work. We are committed to providing opportunities for our people to make real-life impacts, advance in their careers, and contribute to CCC’s success.

CCC offers competitive compensation and benefits to support you and your families, including:

  • 401K Match

  • Paid time off

  • Annual Incentive Plan Performance Bonus

  • Comprehensive health insurance

  • Adoption Assistance

  • Tuition Reimbursement

  • Wellness Programs

  • Stock Purchase Plan options

  • Employee Resource Groups

For more information about our benefits, please check out our careers site.

Here, you belong. You are seen, valued, and respected. We celebrate you for who you are and all you bring. Every voice is heard and is important to our success. You can hear what employees have to say about our culture here

jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer - AI
jobs.excerpt: TechGrove is the Centre of Excellence for Banyan Software, based in Chennai, India.
jobs.description:
TechGrove is the Centre of Excellence for Banyan Software, based in Chennai, India. It plays a key role in supporting Banyan’s global businesses through technology, security, and software development. TechGrove brings together India’s deep pool of technical talent with Banyan’s long-term approach to growth, creating a trusted, developer-focused environment where people can do their best work.

About Element34

For years, Element34 has run large-scale test execution for enterprises that can't send their testing to a public cloud. Banks, insurers, healthcare companies and other regulated organizations use our platform, SBOX, to run thousands of Selenium, Playwright and Appium sessions in parallel on their own infrastructure.

Now we're building an AI-native platform for the whole end-to-end test lifecycle: authoring, execution, failure analysis, triage and self-healing maintenance, with LLMs and agents at the core of each stage rather than added on afterward.

We're a small, senior engineering team and we plan to stay that way. We have no layers of management, no handoffs between teams and no separate infra group. Each engineer owns a problem from design through production.

The Role

This is a hands-on Staff Engineer role with no direct reports. Your influence comes from the systems you design, the code you write and how you raise the engineering bar for the people around you.

About 90% of your time will be backend work in Java or Go: distributed systems, concurrency, data pipelines, AI and agent infrastructure, and performance work. The other 10% is frontend work in React.

This is not CRUD or API plumbing. You'll work on orchestration, scheduling, high-throughput ingestion, retrieval quality, agent reliability and performance problems that don't have a ready-made answer.

What You'll Do

  • Build the AI core of the platform. Design and ship LLM-powered features and autonomous agents that author tests, diagnose failures, find root causes and repair broken tests.
  • Build RAG and retrieval systems over test artifacts, logs, traces, DOM snapshots and code. You'll own chunking, embeddings, hybrid search, ranking and context construction, and measure retrieval quality rigorously.
  • Make AI production-grade. Build evaluation harnesses, guardrails, observability, cost and latency controls, and fallbacks so agents behave predictably in enterprise environments, including self-hosted and air-gapped ones.
  • Design and build core platform systems in Java or Go, including session orchestration, scheduling, resource management and high-concurrency services behind thousands of parallel browser and device sessions.
  • Own the data layer across PostgreSQL (transactional), ClickHouse (analytics and high-volume telemetry), OpenSearch (logs, search and vector retrieval) and Redis (caching, coordination, queues).
  • Own delivery across the whole lifecycle. We have no separate infra team. You'll containerize with Docker, deploy and run on Kubernetes, automate with Ansible, and make sure the software runs reliably in customer environments you don't control.
  • Solve hard problems end to end. Find the bottleneck, profile it, design the fix, ship it and watch it in production.
  • Ship features in React when the work needs it, with no frontend team to hand off to.
  • Set technical direction through design docs, architecture reviews and prototypes. Make the hard trade-off calls and explain them clearly.
  • Make the team AI-native. Use AI coding tools every day and help shape how the team builds with them.

What We're Looking For

  • Strong professional software engineering experience, with a strong record of building and owning complex backend systems.
  • Deep expertise in Java or Go, including concurrency, memory management, performance tuning and idiomatic modern code. You write code others learn from.
  • Mandatory: hands-on experience building with LLMs, including:
  • RAG systems in production or close to it: embeddings, vector or hybrid search, chunking strategies, reranking and retrieval evaluation.
  • AI agents: tool and function calling, multi-step planning, memory and state, and handling failures and non-determinism. Experience with MCP or agent frameworks is a plus. Knowing when to skip a framework counts too.
  • Prompt and context engineering, plus evaluation. You know how to measure whether an LLM feature actually works.
  • Daily, effective use of AI coding tools (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot or similar).
  • Strong computer science fundamentals and problem-solving ability. You can reason about correctness, performance and distributed-systems trade-offs from first principles.
  • Production experience with data stores. Solid PostgreSQL skills plus hands-on experience with at least one of ClickHouse, OpenSearch/Elasticsearch or Redis at scale.
  • Hands-on with Docker, Kubernetes and Ansible. You've deployed, debugged and operated your own services.
  • Working proficiency in React and modern frontend development.
  • An owner's mindset. You do well with autonomy and ambiguity, and you'd rather fix a problem than escalate it.
  • Clear written communication. You're comfortable working remotely and asynchronously, where a good design doc replaces a dozen meetings.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with browser automation and test infrastructure: Selenium/WebDriver, Playwright, Appium, Selenium Grid, or device and emulator farms.
  • Deeper Kubernetes knowledge: operators, custom controllers, autoscaling, or multi-tenant design.
  • Experience with high-throughput ingestion and analytics, such as event pipelines, time-series data, or ClickHouse schema and materialized view design.
  • Experience running self-hosted or open-weight LLMs (vLLM, Ollama, TGI) for air-gapped or data-sensitive deployments.
  • Experience with fine-tuning, small-model distillation, or multimodal models (screenshots, DOM, visual diffing).
  • Background building on-premise enterprise software for locked-down or regulated customer environments.
  • Familiarity with security and compliance expectations in financial services or healthcare.

Why Element34

  • Build an AI-native product, not add AI to an old one. You'll shape how end-to-end testing works with agents at the center.
  • Real ownership. Small team, large scope, and your work reaches production at major enterprises.
  • Hard problems. Agent reliability, retrieval at scale, distributed orchestration and performance.
  • Fully remote, with a team that values deep work and written communication.
  • No bureaucracy. Nothing stands between you and the decisions, the customers or the codebase.

Recruitment Notice

TechGrove may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to assist in screening and/or assessing applicants during the recruitment process. All hiring decisions are made by our team. Personal information submitted through your application will be collected and used for recruitment purposes in accordance with applicable privacy laws. Contact us at any time with questions about our process or to request accommodation.

Beware of Recruitment Scams

We have been made aware of individuals fraudulently posing as members of our Talent Acquisition team and extending fake job offers. These scams may involve requests for personal information or payment for equipment.

Protect yourself by following these steps:

  • Verify that all communications from our recruiting team come from an @banyansoftware.com email address.
  • Remember, employers will never request payment or banking information during the hiring process.
  • If you receive a suspicious message, do not respond — instead, forward it to and/or report it to the platform where you received it.

Your safety and security are important to us. Thank you for staying vigilant.

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Regulatory Affairs Labeling
jobs.excerpt: Revolution Medicines is a global, commercial-state oncology company dedicated to discovering, developing and delivering innovative medicines for patients with RAS-addicted cancers.
jobs.description:
Revolution Medicines is a global, commercial-state oncology company dedicated to discovering, developing and delivering innovative medicines for patients with RAS-addicted cancers. Leveraging its differentiated RAS(ON) tri-complex inhibitor platform, the company is advancing a broad, integrated portfolio of oral RAS(ON) inhibitors designed to directly target the active, cancer-driving state of RAS. Founded on rigorous scientific inquiry and a willingness to challenge long-held assumptions, Revolution Medicines is committed to changing the trajectory of disease for patients with RAS-addicted cancers worldwide.

Our people are united by a shared way of working: follow the science, challenge assumptions, act with urgency and hold ourselves to a high standard of rigor—all in service of patients.

The Opportunity:

The Senior Manager of Labeling serves as a labeling support strategist, partnering with the Global Labeling Lead to execute global labeling deliverables for assigned products. The role develops and maintains regional labeling using the Company Core Data Sheet (CCDS) or an approved reference regional label, adapting content to applicable local requirements while preserving alignment with global labeling strategy. The Senior Manager prepares labeling documents directly or oversees their preparation by external vendors. In both cases, the individual is accountable for document quality, timely delivery, and management of all required cross-functional review and approval activities through completion, in accordance with company procedures and designated approval authorities.

The position can be based at our Redwood City, CA site in a hybrid work schedule (preferred) or remote-based with quarterly and as needed travel.

Labeling Development and Strategic Support

  • Partner with the Global Labeling Lead to translate global labeling strategy into actionable regional and country labeling plans, including deliverables, dependencies, timelines, and review requirements.

  • Author, revise, and maintain regional prescribing information and patient labeling, as applicable, using the CCDS or an approved reference regional label and relevant supporting documentation

  • Assess the impact of CCDS changes, reference label updates, new clinical or safety information, and health authority feedback on assigned labeling; coordinate required updates with regional Regulatory Affairs.

  • Identify and document differences between proposed local labeling and the CCDS or reference label. Develop recommendations and coordinate review, escalation, and approval of deviations through established governance processes.

  • Responsible for proofreading and departmental QC work; ensure quality of labeling deliverables.

Vendor Oversight

  • Define the scope, source documents, content expectations, timelines, and quality standards for outsourced labeling activities; provide clear instructions and ongoing guidance.

  • Review vendor-prepared documents for accuracy, completeness, consistency with source labeling, and alignment with applicable requirements. Ensure comments are resolved and deliverables are ready for internal review and approval.

  • Monitor vendor performance and escalate quality, resource, or timeline concerns to relevant vendor management stakeholders.

Review and Approval Management

  • Own coordination of required reviews and approvals for assigned labeling, regardless of whether documents are authored internally or by a vendor. Identify reviewers and approvers, establish schedules, and manage review and approval workflows through completion.

  • Facilitate cross-functional review, consolidate feedback, resolve comments, and drive alignment on proposed content.

  • Prepare review materials, document decisions and their rationale, and escalate unresolved content or strategic issues to the Global Labeling Lead.

  • Ensure required approvals are obtained and recorded before documents are released for submission or implementation; maintain approved versions, annotations, supporting references, and an auditable decision history.

Delivery and Process Improvement

  • Coordinate with regional and local Regulatory Affairs and Regulatory Operations to provide approved labeling for submission, support responses to labeling queries, and track implementation status.

  • Maintain accurate project trackers and controlled document repositories; communicate progress, risks, and mitigation plans. Support inspection readiness and improvements to labeling procedures, templates, and vendor workflows.

Required Skills, Experience and Education:

  • Bachelor’s degree in scientific, pharmacy, life sciences, or related discipline.

  • At least 7+ years of pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry experience supporting regulatory labeling in at least two or more major geographic areas.

  • Ability to review regulatory labeling documents for accuracy and adherence to regulatory requirements.

jobs.description:
GuidePoint Security provides trusted cybersecurity expertise, solutions and services that help organizations make better decisions and minimize risk. By taking a three-tiered, holistic approach for evaluating security posture and ecosystems, GuidePoint enables some of the nation’s top organizations, such as Fortune 500 companies and U.S. government agencies, to identify threats, optimize resources and integrate best-fit solutions that mitigate risk.

General Description

We are looking for a skilled AI Architect to support the GuidePoint Security Application Security Practice across three areas: architecting, building, and securing the agentic workflows that support consultant delivery; serving as a technical lead for our work with AI labs and model providers; and leading client-facing AI strategy, AI security architecture, and AI training engagements, while providing “Wow Them” service to clients and/or internal customers or co-workers.

This is a builder, advisor, and technical liaison role. The AI Architect will be required to demonstrate strong AI/LLM engineering, agentic system design, and security architecture skills, and lead by influence across technical and business audiences. You will own the technical direction and secure design of the Practice’s internal AI platform, represent GuidePoint Security in technical discussions with the AI labs we work with, and embed in client environments as a security architect and AI strategy lead as engagements require.

About the Application Security Practice

The Application Security Practice helps clients identify, understand, and remediate risk in the applications and AI systems they build and buy. We perform hands-on technical assessments, threat modeling, secure code reviews, and architecture reviews, and we build and mature application security programs and Secure SDLC capabilities across our clients’ organizations.

Our team of application security consultants, secure code reviewers, and AI/LLM security specialists covers modern web, mobile, IoT, and thick client platforms as well as AI-native and agentic architectures, testing against standards such as the OWASP Top 10 and the OWASP Top 10 for LLM and Agentic Applications. We partner with client development, DevSecOps, data science, and security leadership teams to embed security throughout the development lifecycle.

We have invested heavily in agentic delivery: purpose-built agents, skills, and tool integrations that augment our consultants rather than replace them. Key areas of focus for this role include:

  • Architecting and scaling the agentic delivery platform behind our architecture reviews, threat modeling, program reviews, code reviews, and penetration testing, and securing our own AI systems to the same standard we hold our clients to
  • Building technical relationships with the AI labs so we can put new platform capabilities to work for clients quickly
  • Advancing client AI strategy, AI governance, and secure AI adoption as enterprises move from AI experimentation to production

We work directly with AI labs on technical enablement and support our consultants through lab training and certification programs, including Anthropic’s SME network and Claude certification track, so the team’s expertise keeps pace with the platforms our clients deploy.

Roles and Responsibilities:

  • Help design the architecture, technical roadmap, and secure design of the Practice’s agentic delivery platform, the agents, skills, prompts, tool integrations, MCP servers, and orchestration workflows that enable consultant delivery of application architecture reviews, threat modeling, application security program reviews, secure code reviews, and application security assessments.
  • Design, build, and maintain new agentic capabilities across the delivery portfolio, including agent workflows, retrieval and context strategies, tool and data-source integrations, and evaluation harnesses that measure the accuracy, coverage, and consistency of agent output against expert-reviewed baselines.
  • Apply secure-by-design principles to the Practice’s own AI systems by threat modeling agent architectures, enforcing least-privilege tool scopes and autonomy boundaries, protecting client data across context windows and retrieval stores, governing model and provider selection, and implementing controls aligned to the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications, the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications, the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, and MITRE ATLAS, while establishing the engineering standards and guardrails that govern AI-assisted delivery, including human-in-the-loop review gates, output validation, prompt and agent version control, change management, telemetry, and documented evidence of client-data handling sufficient to withstand client, contractual, and regulatory scrutiny.
  • Serve as a forward-deployed security architect on client engagements, embedding with client engineering, platform, data science, and security teams to design, review, and harden application and AI architectures and to accelerate secure adoption of AI at enterprise scale.
  • Deliver client-facing AI strategy and advisory services, including AI/ML and agentic architecture reviews, AI security program and governance assessments, AI threat modeling, secure AI reference architectures, and multi-phase roadmaps that move clients from AI pilots to governed production deployment.
  • Develop and deliver AI and AI security training and enablement for both client audiences and internal consultants, covering secure AI and agentic development practices, prompt injection and agentic attack techniques, AI governance, and effective hands-on use of AI-assisted tooling.
  • Serve as a primary technical point of contact with AI labs and model providers, working alongside Vendor Relationship Management, the Resource Management Office, Practice leadership, and the teams that own the commercial side of those relationships. Represent GuidePoint Security in technical discussions with the labs, evaluate new platform capabilities and roadmaps, and bring what we learn back into our services and tooling.
  • Lead GuidePoint Security’s technical participation in lab subject-matter-expert and partner programs (such as Anthropic’s SME network and certification tracks, and similar programs at other providers), and work with the Learning & Development team on SME training, certification pathways, and onboarding so AI expertise grows across the organization.
  • Act as the senior technical authority and mentor for AI architecture within the Practice, setting direction, reviewing designs, upskilling consultants, and partnering with Practice leadership, sales, and solutions architects to shape new service offerings, scope engagements, and support client pursuits.
  • Contribute to AI and agentic security research and marketing initiatives through activities such as speaking at industry conferences, authoring blog articles and whitepapers, delivering webinars, and contributing to open-source security tooling, while maintaining a strong desire to learn, adapt, and improve along with a rapidly-growing company, and perform other duties as assigned.

Required Experience and Education:

  • High School Diploma + 7 years of experience OR Bachelor’s Degree (BS/BA) + 3 years of experience OR Master’s Degree (MS/MA)
  • Minimum of three (3) years of experience in a security architecture, application security, software engineering, or platform engineering role with demonstrated ownership of system-level design decisions
  • Minimum of one (1) year of experience in an enterprise-level consulting or client-facing technical advisory role
  • Demonstrable hands-on experience designing and building AI agents and agentic systems (evaluated on the depth, recency, and complexity of what the candidate has actually shipped rather than years of elapsed experience), spanning agent orchestration frameworks, agent skills and prompt engineering, tool and function calling, MCP servers and tool integrations, retrieval-augmented generation, context management, and evaluation harnesses
  • Able to substantiate that AI experience in a technical interview by walking through agentic systems they have personally designed and built, the architecture and security tradeoffs they made, how they evaluated agent output quality, and where their approach failed and why
  • Proficiency building against LLM APIs and SDKs (e.g., OpenAI, Anthropic, Amazon Bedrock, Azure OpenAI) with strong development and scripting skills in Python, TypeScript/JavaScript, or a comparable language
  • Demonstrated ability to threat model and securely architect AI-native and agentic systems, including practical command of the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications and the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications
  • Working knowledge of application security assessment, threat modeling, secure code review, application architecture review, and Secure SDLC practices sufficient to architect automation that supports them
  • Proven ability to communicate architecture decisions and AI strategy to both engineering teams and executive stakeholders, to represent the organization credibly with external technology partners, and to lead by influence across technical and business audiences
  • Embraces emerging technologies, including AI tools, to work smarter, solve problems, and drive better business outcomes

Preferred Experience and Education

  • Relevant industry certifications, including AI and agentic architecture credentials such as Anthropic’s Claude Certified Architect (Foundations or Professional), comparable AI/ML and generative AI certifications from AWS, Microsoft, Google Cloud, or NVIDIA, and application security and architecture certifications such as OSWE, GWAPT, CISSP, or CCSP. GuidePoint Security supports consultants in earning these certifications after hire, so they are a plus rather than a prerequisite

jobs.title: Security Engineer
jobs.excerpt: CAST AI is an automation platform that operates cloud-native and AI infrastructure at scale.
jobs.description:
CAST AI is an automation platform that operates cloud-native and AI infrastructure at scale. By embedding autonomous decision-making directly into Kubernetes and cloud environments, CAST AI continuously optimises performance, reliability and efficiency in production.

More than 2,100 companies rely on CAST AI, including Akamai, BMW, Cisco, FICO, Hugging Face, NielsenIQ, Swisscom and TGS. We are headquartered in Miami and operate as a remote-first company across 34 countries in Europe, North America, Latin America and APAC. In January 2026, CAST AI reached unicorn status following a strategic investment from Pacific Alliance Ventures, the corporate venture arm of Shinsegae Group.

About the role

CAST AI is hiring its first dedicated Security Engineer.

Security is currently handled alongside other responsibilities by engineers across the product organisation. As the company grows, we need someone whose full-time focus is understanding the security of our platform, identifying the highest-impact risks and helping engineering teams address them.

CAST AI operates inside customers’ production environments. Customers grant the platform cloud credentials, cluster access and permission to delete, move and resize workloads. Every permission needs to be justified, every action needs to be attributable and every component needs to be assessed as part of a wider attack surface.

You will work across a multi-tenant platform spanning AWS, GCP and Azure, Kubernetes environments, microservices, CI/CD pipelines and AI agents that make autonomous decisions in production. You will help make the secure path the easiest path for engineering teams.

This is a technical, hands-on individual contributor role. You will not be expected to implement every security control yourself, but you will identify risks, define practical mitigations, guide the teams responsible for implementation and drive the most important issues through to closure.

You will report to Mantas Norvaiša and work closely with engineering teams, the Platform team and Danielius, who leads the non-technical side of compliance.

What you will do

  • Learn CAST AI’s architecture, infrastructure and engineering workflows, then identify security flaws and material risks.
  • Set up, operate and continuously tune cloud security tooling such as Wiz so it produces high-signal findings that engineering teams can act on.
  • Build threat models for the product and backend architecture, including trust boundaries, service-to-service authentication, customer-cluster access, secrets and attack paths.
  • Assess and prioritise findings using evidence, business impact and exploitability rather than treating every alert equally.
  • Present the most important risks to engineering and company leadership and build the case for addressing them.
  • Advise engineering teams on practical security improvements.
  • Drive the implementation of security controls across engineering, including production access, identity, secrets management and secure CI/CD practices.
  • Work with the relevant teams to ensure security controls are implemented, tracked and maintained.
  • Help translate compliance requirements into meaningful technical work and evidence.
  • Contribute to security standards for cloud infrastructure, Kubernetes, software supply chains and AI-enabled systems.
  • Support the development of security signals and incident-response practices while helping reduce alert noise.
  • Use scripting, prototypes or code where helpful to validate risks, automate security workflows or support engineering teams. This is not a software development role, but strong software-engineering fundamentals are important.

What you will bring

  • At least 5–6 years of professional security experience. Around 10 years or more would be ideal.
  • Hands-on experience setting up and running cloud security tooling in production, such as Wiz, Upwind or a similar platform, and turning findings into fixes.
  • Strong understanding of cloud infrastructure security across compute, networking, IAM, storage and service communication.
  • Practical experience with at least one of AWS, GCP or Azure, with the ability to reason about how cloud systems work and how they can fail.
  • Strong understanding of Kubernetes and cloud-native infrastructure.
  • Experience threat modelling real systems using STRIDE or a similar method, and the ability to lead engineering teams through the process.
  • Strong software-engineering fundamentals, including the ability to understand and reason about software architecture, distributed systems and infrastructure.
  • Ability to write or review code and automation in Go or Python.
  • Strong written and spoken English.
  • A proactive, adaptable approach and comfort working in a fast-moving environment where the security function is being built from the ground up.

Nice to have

  • Deep hands-on experience with AWS, GCP or Azure, including compute, networking and storage internals.
  • Kubernetes security experience covering RBAC, admission control, network policies and Pod Security Standards.
  • Experience hardening real production Kubernetes clusters.
  • Identity and secrets-management experience, including least-privilege IAM, workload identity and secrets rotation.
  • Detection engineering or incident-response experience, including tuning security signals and reducing false positives.
  • Experience with SOC 2, ISO 27001, FedRAMP or similar compliance frameworks.
  • Software supply-chain security experience, including SBOMs, dependency scanning, container-image scanning, signing and CI/CD security.
  • Experience securing AI and agent-based systems, including prompt injection, excessive agency and tool abuse risks.
  • Familiarity with AI coding agents and agentic development workflows.
  • Experience with Terraform and infrastructure-as-code security.
  • Security certification such as OSCP, CISSP or a comparable qualification. We value what you have built and fixed more than certifications alone.

Technology environment

  • Security: Wiz
  • Cloud and orchestration: Kubernetes, GCP, AWS, Azure
  • Infrastructure as code: Terraform
  • Programming: Go, Python
  • Databases and storage: PostgreSQL, ClickHouse, Google Cloud Storage
  • Messaging and APIs: GCP Pub/Sub, gRPC, REST
  • Observability: Grafana, VictoriaMetrics, VictoriaLogs, VictoriaTraces
  • CI/CD and GitOps: GitLab CI, Argo CD, Kargo

You do not need experience with every technology listed. We are looking for deep security judgement, strong infrastructure fundamentals and the ability to learn the rest quickly.

What you will get

  • A chance to build the first dedicated security function at a fast-growing cloud infrastructure company.
  • Direct influence over how security is designed, prioritised and implemented across the organisation.
  • Exposure to large-scale multi-cloud, Kubernetes and AI infrastructure.
  • Close collaboration with engineering and platform teams rather than security work in isolation.
  • A flexible, remote-first working environment across Europe.
  • Equity options.
  • Learning and development budget, including access to relevant courses and conferences.
  • Equipment budget and team-building support.
  • Additional time off and company events.

Hiring process

  1. Introductory conversation with Mantas Norvaiša.
  2. Security-focused threat modelling exercise. You will be given a system to analyse and model. This is similar to a system-design interview, but focused on trust boundaries, threats, attack paths and mitigations.
  3. Conversation with Danielius about compliance and cross-functional working.
  4. Culture check interview

jobs.description:
Why This Role Exists
This is a founding role — which means your ceiling is uncapped and your fingerprints will be on how an entire function works for years to come.
You'll own how CDM identifies, develops, and scales creative — video and static — built Paid Social–first, with support for our Paid Search team, so our clients grow faster than their competitors can copy them.
Here's the bet we're making: creative is the most durable lever in performance marketing. Budgets, algorithms, audiences, and targeting all converge over time — everyone eventually gets access to the same tools. The creative is what still separates the winners from everyone else. CDM believes the agencies that dominate the next decade will be the ones that treat creative strategy as a rigorous, repeatable discipline instead of a guessing game.
You will be the person who builds that discipline here.

Key Responsibilities

Who We Are
Clever Digital Marketing is a performance marketing agency helping large home improvement companies across the US and Canada grow through Paid Social, Paid Search, CRO, and strategic advising.
We manage a large portfolio of accounts, an in-house creative team, and significant monthly ad spend. As we scale, we're building a stronger creative-strategy function to help clients find new creative winners — and to turn one-off learnings into repeatable systems that compound across every account.

Skills, Knowledge and Expertise

What You'll Own
This is a senior, strategic role. You won't be editing every asset or running campaigns day-to-day. Your job is to raise the quality of the thinking, research, and strategy behind everything we produce and test.
1. Generate net-new creative. Develop original concepts, messaging angles, hooks, formats, and storytelling approaches for video and static ads — not variations on the same three ideas.
2. Find the ideas before you have them. Run customer, competitor, and market research to uncover motivations, objections, and pain points that haven't been explored yet. Mine reviews, sales calls, and customer feedback for the insight that makes an ad work.
3. Turn performance into strategy. Analyze why creative wins or loses and translate it into clear next steps. Write sharp, actionable briefs grounded in customer insight, direct-response principles, and a defined testing hypothesis — and push iteration beyond surface-level hook and footage swaps.
4. Build the system. Create CDM's creative-strategy frameworks, brief standards, testing processes, and a shared learning repository. Spot what's working in one account and determine where it can be adapted across others.
5. Level up the whole team. Coach Media Buyers and editors so stronger creative thinking becomes a department-wide capability, not something that lives with one person. Partner with CRO to align messaging, personas, offers, and landing-page experiences. Provide direction for UGC, founder-led, and spokesperson-led formats.

6. Use AI as a force multiplier. Build AI-powered workflows and tools that accelerate research, ideation, and production for the entire team — more on that below.

What We're Looking For
  • 5+ years in performance-focused creative strategy.
  • Deep understanding of Meta advertising and direct-response creative.
  • Strong direct-response copywriting and short-form storytelling skills.
  • A track record of developing concepts from customer research and performance data — not just intuition.
  • Fluency with creative metrics (Hook Rate, Hold Rate, CTR, CPL) and the judgment to weigh them against lead quality and down-funnel performance.
  • Experience across multiple brands, accounts, or verticals.
  • A structured approach to testing — hypotheses, iteration strategy, isolating variables.
  • Demonstrated ability to build systems, processes, frameworks, or knowledge bases.
  • Advanced, practical experience using AI for research, analysis, ideation, workflow design, or creative enablement.
  • The ability to explain not just what you'd test, but how you found the opportunity and why you believe it will work.
  • Strong communication, prioritization, and cross-functional collaboration skills.
  • A bias for speed — you generate learning quickly without over-engineering every test.

What "AI-First" Means to Us

We are not looking for someone who asks AI to spit out scripts and hooks.
We're looking for someone who uses AI to:
  • Analyze customer reviews, calls, and feedback at scale.
  • Identify creative patterns across many accounts at once.
  • Build and maintain shared account context.
  • Surface cross-account testing opportunities.
  • Automate recurring creative research and reporting.
  • Improve the speed and quality of briefs and production workflows.
  • Build systems that help the whole team make better creative decisions.
You bring strong, independent creative judgment. AI is how you increase the depth, speed, and scale of that judgment. Familiarity with tools like Motion, Looker Studio, Asana, Slack, and Claude is a plus.

Nice to Have

  • Lead generation or high-ticket services experience.
  • Home improvement experience.
  • CRO and landing-page testing familiarity.
  • UGC, founder-led, or spokesperson-led creative experience.
  • Hands-on familiarity with editing or design tools.

What Success Looks Like

  • CDM consistently introduces genuinely new creative ideas instead of recycling the same concepts and formats.
  • Creative iterations are more deliberate, strategic, and evidence-based.
  • Media Buyers and editors produce stronger briefs and creative recommendations on their own.
  • Learnings are captured, shared, and applied across accounts.
  • AI-supported research and creative workflows are adopted department-wide.
  • CDM has a repeatable creative-strategy engine that gets stronger with every test.

Benefits

Benefits of Working at CDM
  • Competitive base salary + performance-based bonuses
  • Flexible remote work environment with option for in-person collaboration (Vaughan, ON)
  • Group Benefits - Medical, Dental, Vision, RRSP/401k Plan w/matching, more.
  • Company-provided MacBook computer
  • Home office budget and Clever merch delivery to get you started
  • Work Abroad Policy: Need a new working environment? Our work abroad policy supports this!
  • The chance to shape and grow a high-performing Client Success team
  • A culture of performance and respect where the best work happens with extreme ownership and accountability meets collaboration.
Clever Digital Marketing values the unique skills and experiences each individual brings to the team. We are happy to provide reasonable accommodations to candidates in need of support during the recruitment and selection process. Please note that artificial intelligence (AI) may be utilized during the interview or candidate evaluation process to support the fair and efficient screening, assessment, and selection of applicants.

jobs.description:
Helsinki, Finland · Product and engineering · Full-Time · Remote

One position · Finland or Sweden · Remote-first · Rust in production, not on the roadmap

You've spent years getting good at Rust. You've also spent years explaining to employers why it matters, or writing it in a corner of a codebase nobody else touches.

Here it's the whole codebase. The gateway, the policy engine, the security pipeline. All of it.

Roder is an AI security and governance platform: a high-performance Layer 7 gateway that sits between organizations and every AI model and agent they use. Real-time threat detection, prompt injection prevention, identity and access control, data sovereignty enforcement, full audit trails. The security layer enterprises need before they can trust AI at scale.

The entire backend is Rust. Not a rewrite project, not an experiment. It's what runs in production for regulated European customers today, and it's what you'll own.

The Role in a Nutshell

  • Permanent position, starting as soon as we find the right person
  • Remote-first, work from anywhere in Finland or Sweden. We meet in person occasionally, not constantly. When we do, we expect you there.
  • Lead-level ownership. You'll shape the Rust architecture, set the standard for the codebase, and mentor engineers who join after you. If you want the lead title and the responsibility that comes with it, it's here. If you'd rather be a deep senior IC without the title, that works too.
  • Salary, competitive and based on experience. We won't win on pure salary against the big consulting factories, but we offer something they never will: a genuine stake in what we're building.
  • Equity. Every employee joins our stock option program after settling into their role. We have massive ambitions, and this is a rare chance to become a true part of Roder and share in what we build.

What You'll Be Working On

  • Owning and evolving our Rust backend: a cargo workspace powering a high-throughput, low-latency AI security gateway in production
  • Performance-critical proxy work: async Rust, Layer 7 routing, streaming, connection handling, multi-provider AI routing, rate limiting
  • Security engineering in the hot path: prompt injection detection, PII scanning, policy enforcement, output filtering, all under strict latency budgets
  • Protocol work: MCP, OAuth/OIDC, token binding, agent identity. This is where the industry is heading and we're already there.
  • Setting engineering standards: code review culture, API design, testing strategy, how we structure the workspace as the team grows
  • Driving our agentic development practices. We build with AI agents, we automate aggressively, and we expect you to push this forward, not tolerate it.

Who You Are

You must have:

  • Strong production Rust experience. You've shipped and operated real Rust systems, not just side projects. You know async Rust, you have opinions about error handling, and you can explain a design tradeoff without reaching for a framework's defaults.
  • Proven senior-level engineering experience overall. Systems that real people depend on.
  • Solid understanding of networking fundamentals: proxies, gateways, API security, protocols
  • Comfort with Kubernetes and containerized deployment
  • EU residency and eligibility to work in Finland or Sweden

You're the right fit if you:

  • Have worked on performance-sensitive services and know how to measure before optimizing
  • Care about security engineering, or want to go deep on it with real attacker-facing problems
  • Use AI tools as a natural part of how you work: not a gimmick, not a crutch, a genuine force multiplier
  • Want to set direction, not just receive it
  • Prefer shipping over meetings

This is not for you if:

  • You believe the future of software development looks like the last 10 years
  • You want a clear org chart to know whose approval you need
  • "Remote-first" to you means never meeting your teammates under any circumstances

What We Offer

Compensation & Equity

  • Competitive salary based on experience
  • Stock option program, all employees, no exceptions, starting after probation. You're not joining a payroll, you're joining the founding team in spirit.

Growth & Learning, from day one

  • Dedicated time for learning, R&D, and personal development, built into your schedule from your first week. Not an empty promise; we actively make sure it happens.

How We Work

  • Remote-first: your best work environment is your work environment
  • Occasional in-person meetups (we're a small team, it's rare but real)
  • Flat organization. Founders have deep experience across IT, software, and security. Everyone's ideas get heard and processed. No idea goes into a black hole.

Tools & Setup

  • Company laptop and equipment
  • External monitor
  • Company phone
  • Internet covered
  • Health services

About Roder

We build AI security infrastructure for organizations that can't afford to get AI governance wrong. Our platform controls, secures, and monitors every AI interaction, from prompt injection attacks to data exfiltration to compliance audit trails, through a single high-performance gateway.

We're a small, experienced team at the start of something significant. The AI governance problem is real, it's growing, and we're building the right solution at the right time.

The Process

We keep it simple and fast. We respect your time.

How to Apply: Submit an application introducing yourself. This is a key position with an exceptional stock option program rarely found elsewhere. We receive hundreds of applications, so make yours stand out.

In your message, highlight the concrete Rust systems you've built, your background, and specifically why you want this position and why your future lies at Roder. Include a tailored CV along with a GitHub profile, crates you've published, or other concrete examples of your Rust work.

Please note: We expect applications to demonstrate that you have carefully read this job description. Generic, mass-submitted applications and non-tailored CVs will not be considered.

  1. Online screening, quick survey
  2. Intro call, 30 minutes, no coding puzzles, just a conversation
  3. Technical discussion, we talk through real problems, architecture decisions, how you think
  4. Meet the team, short and human

We review applications as they come in. The position fills when we find the right person.

We welcome applicants from diverse backgrounds. If you have the experience and the mindset, we want to hear from you.

jobs.title: Software Engineer 5 – Agent Platform, AI Platform
jobs.excerpt: At Netflix, our mission is to entertain the world.
jobs.description:
At Netflix, our mission is to entertain the world. Together, we are writing the next episode - pushing the boundaries of storytelling, global fandom and making the unimaginable a reality. We are a dream team obsessed with the uncomfortable excitement of discovering what happens when you merge creativity, intuition and cutting-edge technology. Come be a part of what’s next.

Machine Learning/Artificial Intelligence powers innovation in all areas of the business, from helping members choose through personalization, to making payment processing easier. Building highly scalable and differentiated ML infrastructure is key to accelerating this innovation.


The Opportunity

Agents are one of the ways work gets done at Netflix — and the AI Platform is building the foundation they run on. The Agent Platform team owns the durable, horizontal substrate every agent at Netflix is built on, no matter which team ships it or which business it serves: the runtime agents execute in, the SDK developers build them with, the memory that lets them carry context across runs, the identity and permissioning that lets them act safely, and the tool and service interfaces they reach the rest of Netflix through.

We are a small team with outsized leverage — what we ship becomes the foundation for agents across all of Netflix. The hardest problems we work on have no vendor answer and no textbook: how a non-deterministic system earns trust at member scale and how memory and evaluation become a loop that makes agents measurably better, not just bigger.

This is a senior individual-contributor role for an engineer who wants to build that foundation hands-on — to own a core primitive end-to-end and set its technical direction, in a domain that is still being invented and where the frameworks turn over in months. The defining work is judgment about what to build and what actually moves the business — expressed in code and contracts the rest of the company depends on.

You will:

  • Design, build, and operate a core agent primitive end-to-end — the runtime, the developer SDK, the memory layer, the tool and service interfaces, or the identity and permissioning substrate. You own it as a paved path other Netflix engineers ship production agents on, including the reliability and day-2 operations that non-deterministic systems running at very high — sometimes member-facing — scale demand.
  • Build the loop that lets agents improve from their own experience. Capture each run's full reasoning-and-tool-call trajectory as structured, replayable data; turn real-world outcomes into evaluation signal; make memory compound across runs; and close the feedback loop so improved behavior ships behind eval gates and safe rollout. These are the most durable problems in the space — make them first-class platform capabilities with real contracts, not afterthoughts.
  • Build the quality and safety surfaces teams can't ship agents without — the tracing, quality signals, and guardrail hooks that tell a team whether an agent is actually any good and contain non-deterministic behavior before it reaches production.
  • Aim the hard problems at business impact. A pull toward hard technical problems is the baseline here — the differentiator is aiming it at the ones that move Netflix's business, from personalization and content to payments and the member experience. Know where an agent actually changes a member or business outcome, and let that decide what the platform takes on and in what order.
  • Set technical direction and raise the bar. Make the hard architecture calls in your area, drive cross-team technical initiatives with ML scientists, product managers, and security, compute, and data partners, and define the clean interfaces a shared foundation depends on — leading through technical credibility, not authority.
  • Iterate fast with real users. Ship, learn from how agent developers actually build, and turn that into durable platform capabilities rather than one-off fixes.

If you want the distance between "a frontier idea about how agents should work" and "the substrate every agent at Netflix runs on" to be one team, this is the role.


Minimum Qualifications

  • Significant software engineering experience (typically 8+ years), with a track record of shipping and operating production systems — not just prototypes.
  • Hands-on experience building, deploying, and operating LLM agents in production — systems that plan, call tools, observe results, and iterate — beyond chat-completion apps or demos.
  • Experience evaluating agents the rigorous way: building eval suites, tracing, and quality signals, then iterating on the results to make agents measurably better.
  • Strong fundamentals in designing and operating scalable, observable, fault-tolerant distributed systems.
  • A track record of building SDKs, APIs, or libraries that other engineers build on — you think in contracts, versioning, and developer experience, not just features.
  • Working fluency with modern agent frameworks and the tool/function-calling and MCP patterns they share — deep enough to have an opinion about where they help and where they get in the way.
  • Proficiency in Python and its packaging tooling, plus one of Java, Go, C/C++, Rust, or Zig.
  • A track record of choosing what to build by business impact, not technical interest alone — you partner closely with the teams and stakeholders you serve, and can point to outcomes that moved the business, not just systems you shipped.
  • Strong written and verbal communication; comfort with ambiguity; able to drive both 0-to-1 and 1-to-100 work; effective across a distributed (US) team.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience building memory or state systems for agents — context that compounds across runs — especially at high scale.
  • Experience with the emerging class of agent concerns: agent identity and permissioning, guardrails and safety, and cost governance for LLM and agent workloads.
  • Credibility in a relevant open-source ecosystem (agent frameworks, runtimes, evaluation, or developer tooling).
  • Familiarity with our stack — Temporal, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Kubernetes — and with large-scale build, release, CI/CD, and observability practices.

The IT Operations Manager is responsible for ensuring the effective operation, control, and governance of the organization's IT infrastructure and technology assets across the head office, retail stores, warehouses, and distribution centers. The role oversees IT asset management, incident management, equipment deployment, inventory control, and lifecycle management while ensuring IT services support business operations efficiently.

A key responsibility of this role is to establish structured processes, accurate asset records, and operational controls that enable scalable IT support for the organization's expanding retail network.

Key Responsibilities

1. IT Asset Inventory and Deployment Management

  • Manage the central inventory of all IT equipment, including computers, laptops, POS terminals, scanners, printers, networking equipment, mobile devices, and peripherals.
  • Ensure all incoming IT equipment is properly received, inspected, tagged, recorded, and stored.
  • Plan and coordinate deployment of IT equipment to new and existing retail stores, warehouses, and distribution centers.
  • Maintain complete documentation of equipment movements including receipts, transfers, deployments, returns, repairs, and disposals.
  • Conduct periodic physical inventory counts and reconcile inventory against system records.
  • Investigate and resolve inventory discrepancies promptly.
  • Ensure adequate inventory levels are maintained to support new store openings and operational requirements.

2. Retail IT Incident Management

  • Establish and manage a structured IT incident management process for all retail locations.
  • Ensure incidents are properly logged, categorized, prioritized, assigned, monitored, and resolved within agreed service levels.
  • Coordinate with internal IT teams and external vendors to resolve incidents efficiently.
  • Analyze recurring incidents and implement preventive or permanent corrective actions.
  • Produce regular reports on incident trends, root causes, response times, and service performance.
  • Continuously improve incident response procedures to minimize downtime affecting retail operations.

3. IT Asset Register Rebuild and Asset Verification Project

Lead the organization's IT Asset Register reconstruction project by:

  • Conducting a comprehensive physical inventory of all deployed IT equipment across all locations.
  • Verifying equipment ownership, location, assigned users, and operational status.
  • Reconciling physical assets against accounting records and existing IT inventories.
  • Rebuilding the complete IT Fixed Asset Register with accurate and validated information.
  • Recording asset specifications including:
    • Asset Tag
    • Serial Number
    • Model
    • Purchase Date
    • Deployment Date
    • Current Location
    • Assigned User
    • Warranty Status
    • Useful Life
    • Equipment Age
    • Current Operational Condition
  • Identify missing, obsolete, retired, or unrecorded assets and recommend appropriate corrective actions.
  • Develop standardized procedures for maintaining the accuracy of the IT Asset Register going forward.

4. IT Equipment Dispatch and Deployment System

Design and implement a controlled IT equipment dispatch process by:

  • Developing standardized workflows for requesting, approving, issuing, transferring, and returning IT equipment.
  • Implementing documentation and approval controls for all equipment movements.
  • Creating tracking mechanisms from central inventory through deployment to retail stores and distribution centers.
  • Maintaining complete traceability of every IT asset throughout its lifecycle.
  • Standardizing forms, documentation, and approval matrices for equipment dispatch.

5. IT Asset Lifecycle Management

Develop and implement a comprehensive IT Asset Lifecycle Management Program covering:

  • Procurement
  • Receiving
  • Asset Registration
  • Deployment
  • Maintenance
  • Repair
  • Transfer
  • Upgrade
  • Warranty Tracking
  • Obsolescence Monitoring
  • Retirement
  • Disposal

The manager shall:

  • Establish asset lifecycle policies and standards.
  • Monitor equipment aging against defined replacement schedules.
  • Identify obsolete or end-of-life equipment.
  • Prepare annual technology refresh and replacement plans.
  • Coordinate retirement and disposal activities in accordance with company policies.
  • Ensure retired equipment is securely sanitized, documented, and disposed of appropriately.
  • Provide management with reports on asset age profiles, replacement forecasts, and lifecycle costs.

6. IT Operations Management

  • Ensure availability of IT infrastructure supporting retail operations.
  • Coordinate preventive maintenance of IT equipment.
  • Monitor vendor performance and service contracts.
  • Support new store openings, relocations, and closures.
  • Maintain IT operational documentation, procedures, and standards.
  • Recommend improvements to IT operational processes and controls.

7. Governance, Reporting, and Compliance

  • Develop and enforce policies governing IT asset management and inventory control.
  • Ensure compliance with internal controls, audit requirements, and company policies.
  • Prepare regular management reports including:
    • IT Asset Inventory Status
    • Asset Aging Report
    • Incident Management Dashboard
    • Equipment Deployment Status
    • Inventory Variance Report
    • Asset Utilization Report
    • Technology Refresh Plan
  • Support internal and external audit activities related to IT assets and operations.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field.
  • Minimum of 5–8 years of experience in IT operations, infrastructure, or IT asset management.
  • At least 3 years of supervisory or managerial experience.
  • Experience supporting multi-site retail operations is highly preferred.
  • Experience implementing IT Asset Management (ITAM) and IT Service Management (ITSM) processes is an advantage.

Technical Competencies

  • IT Asset Management (ITAM)
  • IT Service Management (ITIL)
  • Incident Management
  • Inventory Control
  • Fixed Asset Management
  • Retail IT Operations
  • Network and Endpoint Infrastructure
  • Microsoft 365 Administration
  • Asset Tracking Systems
  • Service Desk Management
  • Project Management
  • Data Analysis and Reporting

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

  • IT asset inventory accuracy of at least 99%.
  • Completion of the enterprise-wide IT asset verification and fixed asset register rebuild within the approved project timeline.
  • 100% tracking of IT equipment movements from receipt through retirement.
  • Timely deployment of IT equipment for all scheduled store openings.
  • Achievement of incident response and resolution service level targets.
  • Reduction in recurring IT incidents through root cause analysis and corrective actions.
  • Completion of annual IT asset lifecycle reviews and technology refresh plans.
  • Zero significant audit findings related to IT asset management and inventory controls.
  • Accurate and timely reporting of asset aging, obsolescence, and replacement requirements.
  • Full implementation and adoption of standardized IT asset dispatch, lifecycle, and inventory management processes across all locations.
