jobs.excerpt: DescriptionThe Site Contracts & Budget Manager provides operational leadership for site contracting and budget negotiation activities across awarded clinical trials.
jobs.description:
Description

The Site Contracts & Budget Manager provides operational leadership for site contracting and budget

negotiation activities across awarded clinical trials. The role is primarily accountable for contracting strategy,

Clinical Trial Agreement negotiation and execution, site budget negotiations, amendments, and resolution of

complex contractual and financial issues.

Working in close partnership with the Site Budget & Proposal Manager, the role translates proposal-stage

budget assumptions into effective study- and site-level contracting and negotiation strategies. Together, the

roles provide complementary leadership across the site budget and contracting lifecycle, with distinct primary

areas of accountability.

The Site Contracts & Budget Manager serves as a key contact and escalation point for sponsors, sites, and

internal stakeholders and provides functional guidance, training, and support to Site Budget & Contracting

personnel

Requirements

More specifically, the Site Contracts and Budget Manager must:

· Lead and manage Site Budget & Contracting staff, providing direction, coaching, development,

workload oversight, and support to ensure consistent quality and delivery across assigned studies.

· Oversee site contracting and budget negotiation activities across the portfolio, ensuring appropriate

resourcing, prioritization, quality, timelines, and escalation of risks or issues.

· Provide oversight of site contracting for awarded clinical trials, including Clinical Trial Agreements,

associated financial exhibits, amendments, negotiation parameters, and country-specific requirements.

· Establish and maintain contracting strategies, standards, and negotiation approaches that support

timely site activation while balancing sponsor requirements, organizational standards, site

expectations, and contractual risk.

· Serve as functional escalation point for complex or high-risk contract and budget negotiations,

providing guidance to team members and facilitating decisions with sponsors, sites, Legal Affairs, and

other stakeholders.

· Oversee the operational implementation of study-specific site budgets, including negotiation

parameters, approval pathways, exceptions, and escalation requirements.

  • Provide site contracting expertise during proposal development, including input on country-specific contracting requirements, anticipated timelines, institutional considerations, negotiation trends, risks, and resource needs.
  • Participate and/or support bid defence meetings, client presentations, and sponsor strategy discussions when site contracting, budget negotiation, timelines, or associated risks are relevant.
  • Monitor portfolio-level contracting and budget performance, identifying emerging risks, delays, capacity constraints, quality concerns, and opportunities for improvement.
  • Own and oversee the business assets supporting Site Budget & Contracting, including contract and budget templates, negotiation tools, country intelligence, guidance documents, trackers, reference materials, and other functional resources.
  • Ensure business assets remain current, fit for purpose, consistently applied, appropriately governed, and aligned with evolving operational and business needs.
  • Oversee the integrity, consistency, and usability of Site Budget & Contracting data across applicable tools, trackers, and systems.
  • Use contracting and negotiation outcomes to strengthen institutional and country intelligence and, in partnership with the Site Budget & Proposal Manager, inform future budget assumptions and benchmarks.
  • Lead functional process improvement initiatives to improve contracting and budget negotiation quality, efficiency, consistency, scalability, and stakeholder experience.
  • Support digital transformation and automation opportunities that reduce manual activities, strengthen controls, and improve the availability and quality of contracting and budget data.
  • Establish and monitor relevant performance indicators and use operational data to identify trends, bottlenecks, and opportunities for corrective action or continuous improvement.
  • Ensure Site Budget & Contracting staff are appropriately trained and consistently apply relevant SOPs, processes, templates, tools, and quality standards.
  • Partner with senior leadership on resource and capacity planning, functional priorities, process maturity, systems and tools, quality, and continuous improvement.
  • Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, proactive risk management, knowledge sharing, and continuous improvement within the Site Budget & Contracting team.
  • Employee may be assigned to other responsibilities that do not pertain to their former description, if they have the required experience, are qualified and/or have received adequate training.

Profile

  • B.Sc. or in a relevant field of study.
  • 5+ years of experience in clinical research, clinical trial budgeting, or related financial management roles within the pharmaceutical, biotech, or CRO industry.
  • Strong negotiation and communication skills to engage with sponsors, external budget contacts, and internal stakeholders, serving as the escalation point to secure optimal study budgets.
  • Experience creating and maintaining budget templates tailored to global regions and therapeutic areas, ensuring scalability and consistency.
  • Collaborative mindset to partner with operational leads and ensure financial assumptions align with study design, operational strategies, and delivery plans.
  • Experience representing the organization in bid defense meetings and client calls, with the confidence to explain budget rationale and defend assumptions.
  • Technical proficiency to maintain pricing tools, cost databases, and budget models in collaboration with Finance and IT teams.
  • Leadership abilities to train and mentor junior specialists, provide guidance, and ensure team adherence to best practices.
  • Demonstrated success in partnering with senior team members to refine internal processes, drive efficiencies, and improve deliverables.
  • Strategic thinking to engage with leadership on process improvement initiatives, offering insights and recommendations that enhance operational excellence.
  • Good knowledge of good clinical practices, and applicable Health Canada and Food and Drug Administration (FDA) regulations/guidelines.

Our company

The work environment

At Indero, you will work with brilliant and driven colleagues. Our values are collaboration, innovation, reliability, and responsiveness. We offer a stimulating work environment and attractive advancement opportunities.

In this position, you will be eligible for the following perks:

  • Permanent full-time position
  • Flexible schedule
  • Vacation
  • Home-based position
  • Ongoing learning and development

About Indero

Formerly known as Innovaderm, Indero is a world-renowned expert and clinical research leader in dermatology. We have more than two decades of experience serving a broad range of indications, patient populations, administration routes, and drug classes, and a global footprint.

Indero is a dual-focus CRO for dermatology and rheumatology, with 25+ years’ experience in clinical research and trial delivery. Our full-service approach – which includes everything from protocol design and patient recruitment to trial monitoring and biometrics – provides biotech and pharmaceutical sponsors with the rigorous scientific foundation and tailored expertise their studies need to reach the finish line efficiently and effectively. With capabilities in North America, Europe, Asia Pacific and Latin America; vast, continuously growing relationships with investigators and patients; and a dedicated research clinic through which we design and execute our own studies, Indero is the ideal CRO partner for clinical needs at global scale.

Indero is committed to providing equitable treatment and equal opportunity to all individuals. As such, Indero will provide accommodations throughout the recruitment and selection process to applicants with disabilities, upon request.

jobs.excerpt: About the Organization: Mosaic is a national collaborative funder and field catalyst that boosts the collective power of climate, conservation, and environmental health and justice movements in the United States to achieve durable, population-scale wins.
jobs.description:
About the Organization:
Mosaic is a national collaborative funder and field catalyst that boosts the collective power of climate, conservation, and environmental health and justice movements in the United States to achieve durable, population-scale wins. Directed by a Leadership Council of diverse and representative grassroots, NGO, and philanthropic leaders from across the country, Mosaic bolsters four key pillars of infrastructure necessary for transformative movements: Strong and resilient networks and coalitions rooted in trust; a deep bench of diverse, highly skilled leaders; advocacy tools and training for large-scale mobilization; and powerful, norm-shifting narratives. (See our full strategic framework here). Mosaic has committed $32M in grant funding since 2020 to support collaborative projects and coordinated resources that are strengthening alliances, driving policy wins, shifting narratives, and galvanizing large-scale action.
Impact is at the heart of Mosaic’s mission. As one of the only national collaborative funds exclusively focused on building movement infrastructure – the connections and shared resources all movements need – Mosaic is committed to building the power necessary for lasting environmental and social change. A stable climate, clean air and water, healthy communities, and thriving natural systems all hang in the balance during this critical decade. Mosaic was created in response to a collective recognition that, although the U.S. environmental movement has achieved historic victories, the pace and scale of the challenge we face demand even more. The environmental movement will only achieve climate and environmental goals with a stronger, better-connected movement that is capable of driving and sustaining meaningful change.
Position Summary:
The Director of Communications and Strategic Initiatives reports to the Chief Executive Officer and is responsible for developing and implementing Mosaic’s external communications strategy for both fundraising and programmatic outcomes in collaboration with the development and program teams. The role also supports the CEO with overarching organizational & programmatic strategic planning, and facilitates transparency and collaboration across staff teams.

Primary Responsibilities

Communications
  • Develops and leads the annual communications strategy, ensuring alignment with the organization’s strategic plan and mission;
  • Manages and strengthens the Mosaic brand, overseeing all external communication platforms to enhance visibility and engagement;
  • Produces high-quality, funder- and field-facing materials, including annual reports, docket memos, proposal templates, research reports, and organizational overviews, in collaboration with program and development teams;
  • Supports Mosaic’s field catalyst work through targeted thought leadership and grantee communications strategy;
  • Cultivates and manages strategic partnerships with communication professionals to enhance outreach and brand positioning;
  • Supervises communications consultant contracts, budgets, tools, and licenses, ensuring efficient resource management and execution.
  • Collaborates with the development team in developing funder cultivation journeys, enhancing funder engagement and stewardship; and
  • Supports communication with the Leadership Council, ensuring transparency and alignment with organizational priorities.
Organizational Strategy
  • Collaborates with the CEO to align internal communications, fostering effective cross-departmental collaboration across development, programs, and operations;
  • Supports the development and execution of annual strategic planning, contributing to organizational growth and impact;
  • Works with the program team to track progress and impact, integrating data and storytelling to effectively communicate outcomes to funders and partners;
  • Collaborates with the program team in designing and implementing a narrative & communications grantmaking strategy, ensuring alignment with broader organizational goals;
  • Co-designs and manages key strategic initiatives, including anniversary events, funder convenings, special research projects, and other field-building activities;

The Ideal Candidate

You are a strategic, creative, and compelling communicator with the ability to translate complex ideas into clear, engaging narratives that inspire action and advance organizational goals. You bring expertise in communications strategy, brand development, and stakeholder engagement, paired with a collaborative approach to strategic planning and cross-team coordination. You are a thoughtful storyteller who connects data, insights, and impact to strengthen relationships with funders, grantees, and the broader environmental field. You are adaptable, highly organized, and skilled at managing multiple priorities and partnerships while fostering transparency, alignment, and shared purpose. Above all, you are passionate about advancing Mosaic’s mission and using communications and strategic initiatives to strengthen the environmental movement and drive lasting social and environmental change.

Specific Experience Requested:
  • 9+ years of experience in a support role with demonstrated track record of success; exposure to and interest in the environmental field, the philanthropic and/or nonprofit sector a plus
  • Interest, comfort, and strength working in a dynamic “startup” environment
  • Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills
  • Strong oral, written, and visual communications skills
  • Ability to represent the organization professionally; maintaining confidentiality and handling of sensitive matters with discretion and diplomacy
  • Excellent interpersonal skills and the ability to build relationships with stakeholders
  • Self-starter; highly motivated and resourceful team-player able to manage multiple requests and conflicting priorities under deadline in a fast-paced environment
  • Strong judgment; able to think and work independently, multi-task, prioritize, and follow through to effectively manage workflow
  • Strong organizational skills with attention to detail, accuracy, protocol, and a commitment to high quality work
  • High fluency with Microsoft Office, Google Drive and proficiency using online databases; Previous Salesforce experience a plus
  • Experience and comfort with Adobe Suite, Canva, various web CMSs, email platforms, and other communications tools.
  • Experience and comfort with minor troubleshooting for computer, printer, smartphone, or other equipment issues; request IT service and support
  • Forward-looking thinker who actively seeks opportunities and proposes solutions
  • Passion for Mosaic’s mission
  • Flexibility and sense of humor
  • Prior experience working with Mosaic required.

Workplace, Compensation & Application

Workplace & Travel: All employees work from home offices with occasional travel (1-2 times per year) for all-team in-person meetings.

Compensation: Mosaic and Multiplier provide a comprehensive compensation package, including competitive salary ($165k - $185k annual salary), excellent medical and dental benefits, retirement savings, and generous vacation and sick leave policy.
How to Apply: To apply, please visit our Applicant Portal. Applications will be accepted until position is filled. We respectfully request no follow-up calls or emails.

Mosaic is an independent operating project ofMultiplier, a nationally recognized nonprofit that accelerates impact for sustainability-focused initiatives.

Multiplier is committed to creating an inclusive, equitable, and accessible application process for all candidates. We recognize that the traditional hiring process can create barriers. If we can support your participation in the job application or interview process by providing specific assistance or accommodation, please reach out to . Requests for accommodations are confidential and will not impact your candidacy.

As the Amazon PPC Manager, you will be responsible for managing the company's advertising efforts on Amazon, setting performance goals, elaborating PPC strategies, and ensuring the successful execution of Amazon PPC campaigns to drive sales and maximize profitability.

If you have a strong background in Amazon PPC advertising combined with Amazon Brand Manager experience, exceptional leadership skills, and a passion for driving success in the E-commerce industry, we would love to hear from you.

It is a fast-growing small company that manages Amazon accounts and runs its own brand, offering eco-friendly products. The team works fully remotely, allowing for flexibility and efficiency while maintaining strong collaboration.

The company operates in an international and rapidly evolving market, providing a dynamic work environment. It encourages creativity and initiative, giving team members the opportunity to bring new ideas to life and make a real impact.

Responsibilities:

  • Develop and implement comprehensive Amazon PPC strategies across the company's brands, to increase visibility, drive sales, and achieve KPIs.

  • Analyze data and generate actionable insights to improve campaign performance, conversion rates, and customer acquisition.
  • Prepare regular performance reports, highlighting key metrics, campaign results, and recommendations for further optimization.
  • Ensure compliance with Amazon's advertising policies and guidelines, staying informed about any changes or updates in the platform.

Qualification requirements:

  • Minimum 2 years of proven experience in Amazon PPC advertising.
  • Proven experience as a Brand Manager or similar role, specifically within the Amazon FBA marketplace.
  • In-depth knowledge of Amazon PPC campaign management, including campaign types, targeting options, bid management, and keyword optimization.
  • A proven track record of successfully managing PPC month budgets over $50k and delivering strong ROI.
  • Expertise in using the Amazon Advertising platform, analytics tools, and data analysis techniques to measure and improve campaign performance.
  • Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to extract actionable insights from complex datasets.
  • Strong understanding of keyword research, competitive analysis, and audience targeting in the context of Amazon PPC advertising.
  • Advanced skills in using Google Sheets or similar tools for data analysis and reporting.
  • Self-motivated, proactive, and result-oriented, with a passion for continuous learning and keeping up-to-date with industry trends.

The working hours are based on GMT+2 time, but the company is not strict about them. They prioritize task completion over simply clocking in hours. Their approach is flexible, allowing team members to manage their time effectively while ensuring the work gets done.

Tracking & Tools

For communication and task management, the company uses:

  • Slack
  • ClickUp

Benefits:

  • Work for a market-proven, fast-growing company.

  • Supportive and collaborative work environment.
  • Opportunity to be part of something bigger, with autonomy over your work.

About Cardiac Care Alliance (CCA)

Cardiac Care Alliance is a Management Services Organization (MSO) dedicated to building a high-performance cardiovascular network. We work in close partnership with independent cardiologists to complement fee-for-service care with value-based care (VBC) models. Our mission is to improve patient access, outcomes, and experiences by delivering proactive, patient-centered care across the cardiac continuum.

Position Summary

CCA is seeking experienced Registered Nurse (RN) Care Managers to support a high-acuity population of patients with complex cardiac conditions, including congestive heart failure (CHF) and other comorbidities. This is a full-time, remote, hourly contract position focused on delivering advanced clinical support through clinical triage, care plan development, and high-risk care management, including Transitional Care Management (TCM), Principal Care Management (PCM), Complex Care Management (CCM), Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM), and other applicable clinical programs.

This role is integral to our population health initiatives — proactively supporting at-risk patients with data-informed outreach, continuity of care, and patient-centered engagement. You'll help reduce avoidable hospitalizations, support patient self-management, and contribute to better long-term cardiac outcomes.

jobs.description:
Job Type: Full-time | Location: Remote, US | Department: Innovation | Reporting to: Director, Data Center Commissioning | Work Location: #remote

IREN is a vertically integrated AI Cloud provider, delivering large-scale data centers and GPU clusters for AI training and inference. IREN’s platform is underpinned by its expansive portfolio of grid-connected land and power in renewable-rich regions across North America, Europe and APAC.

The Commissioning Subject Matter Expert sets the discipline standard for commissioning across every IREN region and site. You will write and own IREN's commissioning specifications, acceptance criteria and the standard against which the Commissioning Authority's test scripts are approved; be the technical escalation point for the campus commissioning teams; review Commissioning Authority deliverables and first-of-kind installations; and give Engineering and Procurement technical input on designs, equipment and commissioning scopes. This is a program-level, senior individual-contributor role that stays with the Director rather than with one project, and it is one of the first hires into the function: the standards you write will be applied on every IREN site, by IREN's own commissioning crews and by the Commissioning Authorities IREN engages.

Electrical covers the power chain from the medium-voltage service to the rack: 4.16–34.5 kV distribution, switchgear, transformers, protection, UPS, generators and paralleling, battery energy storage and on-site generation, busway and power distribution units, and the energization, NETA acceptance testing and load testing that prove them.

Responsibilities

  • Author and maintain IREN's commissioning specifications for the discipline: Division 1 commissioning specification content, acceptance criteria, Level 1 to Level 5 definitions and integrated systems test requirements, for new build and conversion projects and for both self-performed and general-contractor delivery.
  • Act as the technical escalation point for the campus commissioning teams; settle standard-versus-schedule questions with the Cx Project Manager and the Director, and record the decision.
  • Review the Commissioning Authority's commissioning plans, test scripts and reports for compliance with the standard; audit field execution, witness sampling and first-of-kind installations across sites.
  • Give commissioning input to Engineering on basis of design and specifications, and to Procurement on equipment, factory test requirements and Commissioning Authority scopes of work and request-for-proposal templates.
  • Lead the factory witness testing strategy for critical equipment in the discipline and approve factory acceptance test procedures.
  • Lead root-cause analysis on significant discipline failures or repeat deficiencies and turn the findings into changes to the standard.
  • Own the electrical test and energization standard: pre-energization and foreign-object inspection and release, NETA acceptance testing requirements, protection and relay testing, load-bank and transfer testing, UPS and battery testing, and the sequence from Level 3 start-up to Level 5 integrated systems testing for the power chain.
  • Track emerging standards and codes for the regions IREN builds in (ASHRAE Guideline 0, Guideline 1.6P and Standard 202, ASHRAE 90.4, NEC and NETA ATS in the United States; the Canadian Electrical Code and CSA standards in Canada) and update IREN standards accordingly.
  • Develop and deliver the discipline's technical training modules with the Training Program Lead; sit on interview panels and mentor the project commissioning leads and IREN's site commissioning crews.
  • Support the procurement and mobilization of Commissioning Authorities in new regions so that the IREN standard applies from day one.

Requirements

REQUIRED
  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical or Electrical Engineering, Controls or a related engineering field.
  • 10+ years of data center or mission-critical commissioning, start-up or engineering in the discipline, including large-scale programs and full Level 1 to Level 5 delivery.
  • Demonstrated authorship of commissioning specifications, test procedures or standards that were used across more than one project.
  • Deep knowledge of data center electrical systems: medium-voltage distribution, switchgear, transformers and protection, UPS, generators and paralleling, battery energy storage, busway and power distribution, including how they are energized, tested and accepted.
  • Working knowledge of integrated systems testing across electrical, mechanical and controls, and of electrical power monitoring systems.
  • Experience reviewing and directing third-party commissioning authorities and equipment vendors.
  • Able to travel up to 25% to IREN sites.
  • Authorized to work in the United States.
PREFERRED
  • BCxP or CCP held, plus a discipline credential such as NETA certification; PE license or chartered status.
  • Commissioning of 34.5 kV class switchgear, protection coordination, battery energy storage and on-site generation.
  • Experience standing up commissioning in a new region or with a new commissioning authority.

LOCATION & TRAVEL
  • Remote within the United States, with travel of up to 25% to IREN sites in Texas and elsewhere in North America and to the Fort Worth office. Candidates in the Dallas–Fort Worth area or within easy reach of IREN's Texas sites are preferred.

At IREN, we offer a comprehensive, market-competitive total rewards package designed to support employees’ well-being, career advancement, and financial wealth. Our offerings reflect our commitment to Proceed with Purpose while rewarding high performance and long-term growth.

The Director, Employee Relations leads Amerit's Employee Relations function, setting the strategy, standards, and operating discipline for how the organization identifies, investigates, and resolves employee relations matters across a multi-site, field-based workforce. This role owns the ER team's highest-risk work, including EEOC and other agency charge response, and oversight of complex and sensitive workplace investigations. The Director serves as the primary connection point to Legal on employee relations matters and partners closely with the Director, People Business Partners and People Business Partners (PBPs) to ensure ER and PBP work in close alignment, with clear escalation discipline, on employee matters across the business.

The ideal candidate combines deep employee relations and labor relations expertise with strong people leadership skills, sound judgment under pressure, and the ability to build scalable, defensible ER practices in a fast-paced, multi-site operational environment.

jobs.title: AI Phone - Security & Privacy Engineer
jobs.excerpt: AboutWe are reimagining the phone.  AI phones need to be proactive, intuitive, intelligent and low cost.
jobs.description:
About

We are reimagining the phone. AI phones need to be proactive, intuitive, intelligent and low cost. This is a mission critical for rest of the world to adopt intelligence.

There are over 5 billion people using everyday applications such as email, messaging, notes, tasks, and calendars, yet most are not AI-native. Our mission is to build proactive applications and devices that bring intelligence into daily conversations, coordination and workflows, with minimal prompting.

Focus: Designing and implementing the security and privacy architecture for the AI-native phone, ensuring AI agents can safely access user data, interact with applications, and execute actions across the operating system.

Unlike conventional mobile application security, this role needs to consider the additional risks introduced by AI agents having access to personal context, system services, and application-level actions.

Responsibilities

  • Design the overall security and privacy architecture for the AI-native phone.

  • Define permission models and access boundaries for AI agents interacting with user data and system services.

  • Design secure mechanisms for AI access to messages, contacts, calendars, notifications, camera, microphone, location and other sensitive information.

  • Implement appropriate sandboxing and isolation for agent execution.

  • Define authentication, authorization and access-control mechanisms for AI tools and application integrations.

  • Ensure users have control over what information AI can access and what actions it can execute.

  • Implement audit logging and user-visible activity tracking for AI access and actions.

  • Design secure storage, encryption, data retention and deletion mechanisms for personal data and memory.

  • Identify and mitigate AI-specific security risks, including prompt injection, malicious applications, data exfiltration and unauthorized tool execution.

  • Review Android permission models, privileged system access, SELinux policies and system-level security boundaries.

  • Work closely with Android/AOSP, Agent Runtime, Context & Memory and Applied ML teams to ensure security is built into the architecture rather than added later.

  • Conduct security assessments, threat modeling and penetration testing for system-level AI capabilities.

Requirements

  • Strong experience in mobile security, Android security, application security or systems security.

  • Deep understanding of Android security architecture, including application sandboxing, permissions, SELinux, Binder IPC and privileged system services.

  • Experience designing authentication, authorization and access-control systems.

  • Strong understanding of encryption, secure storage, key management and data protection.

  • Experience with security threat modeling, vulnerability assessment and penetration testing.

  • Understanding of privacy-by-design principles, data minimization and user consent.

  • Ability to work across Android platform, backend and AI agent architectures.

Nice to have

  • Experience with AOSP security customization or Android platform security.

  • Experience securing system-level applications or privileged Android services.

  • Experience with AI agent security, prompt injection, tool-use security and LLM data leakage.

  • Experience with mobile device security, Trusted Execution Environment (TEE), hardware-backed keystores and secure boot.

  • Experience with privacy engineering for products handling sensitive personal information.

  • Experience building permission and approval systems for autonomous agents.

At Tilt, we see a side of people that traditional lenders miss. Our mobile-first products and machine learning-powered credit models look beyond credit scores, using over 250 real-time financial signals to recognize real potential. With millions of customers worldwide, we're not just changing how people access financial products — we're creating a new credit system that backs the working, whatever they're working toward.

The Opportunity: Senior Software Engineer, Backend

We’re looking for Senior Backend Engineers who care about building scalable, reliable systems - and who thrive in a collaborative environment. You’ll join one of several product or infrastructure teams, each tackling challenges from decisioning to payments to APIs. Wherever you land, you’ll work on projects that are high-impact, technically challenging, and deeply rewarding.

Tilt is a remote-first company. We drive connectivity through regular company offsites. Travel for company offsites is expected at a minimum 2 times a year.

How You’ll Make an Impact

  • Design and scale backend systems that power our consumer facing products

  • Build and refine APIs that deliver instant, seamless experiences.

  • Collaborate with product, credit/finance, compliance, support, and analytics teams.

  • Contribute to technical discussions, code reviews, and roadmap planning.

  • Drive continuous improvement in code quality, security, and operational excellence.

  • Share knowledge, mentor peers, and contribute to engineering best practices.

Why You’re a Great Fit

  • 6+ years of backend engineering experience (we know careers don’t all look the same — if you’re close, let’s talk).

  • Experience with .NET (C#), or similar frameworks

  • Experience scaling consumer-facing products with significant transaction volumes

  • A collaborative problem-solver who values inclusion, feedback, and continuous learning.

  • Able to effectively leverage AI-powered development tools (e.g., Cursor, Augment, Factory) to enhance productivity, code quality, and collaboration

Don’t meet every qualification? We care about potential over your past. If you're bringing ambition and drive to what we're building, we want to hear from you.

What you'll get at Tilt

  • Virtual-first teamwork: The Tilt team is collaborating across 14 countries, 12 time zones, and counting. You’ll get started with a WFH office reimbursement.

  • Competitive pay: We're big on potential, and it's reflected in our competitive compensation packages and generous equity.

  • Complete support: Find flexible health plans at every premium level, and substantial subsidies that stand up to global standards.

  • Visibility is yours: You can count on direct exposure to our leadership team — we’re a team where good ideas travel quickly.

  • Paid global onsites: Magic happens IRL: we gather twice yearly to reconnect over shared meals or kayaking adventures. (We’ve visited Vail, San Diego, and Mexico City, to name a few.)

  • Impact is recognized: Growth opportunities follow your contributions, not rigid promotion timelines.

The Tilt Way

We're looking for people who chase excellence and impact. Those who stand behind their work, celebrating the wins and learning from the missteps equally. We foster an environment where every voice is valued and mutual respect is non-negotiable — brilliant jerks need not apply. We're in this together, working to expand access to fair credit and prove that people are incredible. When you join us, it's not just another day at the [virtual] office, you're helping millions of hardworking people reach better financial futures.

You’re pushing ahead in your career? We can get behind that. Join us in building the credit system that people deserve.

jobs.description:
Compassion & Choices is seeking an Legal Assistant to support three to six attorneys in their day-to-day litigation work and maintain Compassion's Legal Digital Office. This role reports to the Director of Litigation and sits within the Legal Advocacy & Policy department.

This is a full-time, remote position. The starting salary range is $75,000–$85,000 annually. The final salary offered will be based on relevant experience, qualifications, internal equity, and organizational considerations.

We offer excellent benefits, including employer-shared medical and dental insurance premiums; employer-paid short- and long-term disability, life, and accidental death and dismemberment insurance; flexible spending accounts for medical and dependent care; a commuter pre-tax benefit; eligibility to participate in a 401(k) with a generous 5% employer match and immediate vesting upon eligibility; paid holidays; paid time off; and personal days.

This position will primarily be responsible for:

  • Supporting up to six attorneys managing multiple active litigation matters, including all administrative tasks.
  • Maintaining and optimizing the paperless office.
  • Prioritizing competing assignments, tracking deadlines, managing complex calendars, and adjusting priorities in response to changing litigation demands.
  • Anticipating attorneys’ needs, identifying potential scheduling conflicts and workflow challenges, and taking initiative to address issues before they become urgent.
  • Managing up effectively by communicating priorities, identifying competing demands, providing timely status updates, and ensuring attorneys have the information and materials they need to meet their obligations.
  • Providing substantive support for written and oral discovery, including drafting discovery shells and initial responses and preparing exhibits for oral depositions.
  • Conducting intake and evaluation of legal requests from prospective clients, screening appropriate plaintiffs.
  • Cite checking and proofreading as needed.

Additional Responsibilities

  • Maintaining electronic case files, managing litigation documents, and identifying opportunities to improve digital workflows and operational efficiency.
  • Creating and maintaining research and memo archives for historical, contextual, and future use by Compassion Legal attorneys and partners.
  • Creating and maintaining pleading shells, templates, and sample briefs and pleadings in an organized and accessible manner.
  • Supporting organization-wide Compassion & Choices efforts as requested, including fundraising activities.

Preferred Qualifications (You Will Be a Good Fit):

Education and Experience

  • A four-year degree (B.A. or B.S.) in a field related to law, medicine, or social change, and a minimum of five years of experience in a litigation-focused legal office, law firm, or legal advocacy organization, including providing simultaneous administrative and litigation support to multiple attorneys. An equivalent combination of related experience and/or education may be considered.
  • Experience supporting four or more attorneys with competing deadlines and active litigation caseloads is strongly preferred.

Skills

  • Exceptional written communication skills, including drafting, editing, and proofreading legal correspondence and litigation documents with accuracy and attention to detail.
  • Ability to read, analyze, and interpret complex legal documents, including pleadings, motions, court orders, discovery requests, statutes, regulations, and judicial opinions.
  • Proactive problem-solving: identifying potential problems before they affect litigation deadlines or attorney workflows.
  • Independent prioritization of competing requests from multiple attorneys.
  • Sound judgment in distinguishing between matters you can resolve independently and substantive legal questions that require attorney direction.
  • Professionalism and discretion, including strict confidentiality of privileged and sensitive information.
  • Adaptability and reliability in a fast-paced litigation environment, including when responding to urgent or unexpected developments.
  • Clear, tactful communication with attorneys, clients, court personnel, colleagues, and diverse audiences.

Professional Knowledge

The successful candidate should have advanced knowledge of or experience working with:

  • Civil litigation procedures, court rules, filing requirements, discovery processes, legal document preparation, and litigation calendaring.
  • Federal and state electronic court filing systems, including PACER/CM/ECF.
  • Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook, and PowerPoint), Adobe Acrobat Pro, Westlaw, Clio, DocketBird, and comparable legal research, document management, and case management platforms.
  • Discovery support, including document collection, review, organization, Bates numbering, and production.

Travel

Must be able and willing to travel and have their own means of transportation where applicable (overnight and possible weekends). Some overnight travel may be required but likely less than 10% of total time.

Values

Must be energized by the idea of working at an organization guided by the following values:

  • Patient-directed care is our North Star.
  • Cross-functional collaboration is key to success across programs, policy, legal, clinical, volunteer, communications, development, and operations.
  • We must build an organization that scales through volunteers, partnerships, education, navigation, technology, and influence.
  • We are committed to collaborative relationships while maintaining clarity about our organizational mission, boundaries, leadership, strategic positioning, and long-term sustainability.
  • We value equity, accessibility, and cultural responsiveness.
  • We prioritize organizational learning and continuous improvement.
  • Messaging and communication of our work is a responsibility we all share.

How to Apply

A current résumé and cover letter should be submitted as one PDF document.

In your cover letter, please include the following:

  1. Explain how your personal philosophy and professional interests align with the mission of Compassion & Choices.
  2. Provide a brief summary of the experience, skills, and qualifications that make you a strong candidate for this position.
  3. Describe how your approach to collaboration and your professional values would contribute to Compassion & Choices and the work of this role.

Questions about the position may be directed to HR @ compassionandchoices.org.

About Compassion & Choices

Across the nation, Compassion & Choices works to create a society that affirms life and accepts the inevitability of death, embraces expanded options for compassionate dying, and empowers everyone to choose end-of-life care that reflects their values, priorities, and beliefs. To make this vision a reality, we improve care, expand options, and empower everyone to chart their end-of-life journey.

Compassion & Choices is committed to building a staff that reflects the diverse communities that make up our country. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and recruit, hire, train, promote, and administer personnel actions without regard to any status protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

Salary: $75,000–$85,000/year

jobs.description:
We are seeking a Remote Labor Relations Manager.

*CA and AZ based candidates highly preferred.

The Labor Relations Manager is responsible for planning, directing, and administering all labor relations activities across the organization’s multiple union-represented accounts located across various states, all of which employ hourly, non-exempt personnel under collective bargaining agreements (CBAs). As the sole incumbent in this function, the Labor Relations Manager holds end-to-end accountability for collective bargaining, contract administration, grievance and arbitration management, union relationship management, and labor law compliance across all assigned accounts and jurisdictions, and will scale this function as the organization’s union account portfolio grows. This is a remote position that requires regular multi-state travel to account locations to fulfill essential job functions.

Responsibilities:

  • Supervisory Responsibilities:

    • This position has no direct reports and is classified as an individual contributor role.
    • The Labor Relations Manager exercises significant functional authority and advisory influence over site/account managers and supervisors company-wide on labor relations matters, contract compliance, and disciplinary process.

    Duties/Responsibilities:

    • Collective Bargaining & Contract Administration: Serve as lead negotiator for new contracts, renewals, and re-openers across all union accounts; maintain a master tracking system of all CBA expiration dates, wage/benefit re-openers, and negotiation timelines; interpret and administer the terms of each CBA, advising site/account management on contractual rights, obligations, and past practice; and draft, review, and finalize contract language, side letters, and memoranda of understanding (MOUs).
    • Grievance & Dispute Resolution: Manage the grievance procedure end-to-end at all accounts, including intake, investigation, response drafting, and company representation through each step up to and including arbitration; partner with outside labor counsel on arbitration strategy and hearing representation; and track grievance trends by account to identify systemic issues or contract-language gaps requiring correction in future bargaining.
    • Union Relationship Management: Serve as the primary company liaison to all union locals and business agents representing the company’s accounts; lead or support labor-management committee meetings, information requests (RFIs), and ongoing communication between union representatives and account leadership; and monitor union organizing activity in non-represented parts of the business and advise leadership on positive employee relations strategies.
    • Compliance & Risk Management: Ensure company practices comply with the National Labor Relations Act (NLRA) and applicable state-specific labor laws in every jurisdiction in which the organization operates a union account; respond to unfair labor practice (ULP) charges, NLRB filings, and related regulatory inquiries in coordination with legal counsel; and maintain current knowledge of federal and state labor law developments and proactively communicate impacts to leadership.
    • Training & Internal Advisory: Train and coach site/account managers and frontline supervisors on contract compliance, grievance avoidance, disciplinary process under just-cause standards, and effective communication with hourly, union-represented employees; act as the internal expert resource for any labor relations question arising at any account; and develop tools, templates, and job aids so that field managers can operate consistently with contractual requirements.
    • Reporting & Strategy: Provide regular reporting to senior leadership on labor relations metrics, including grievance volume and resolution, arbitration outcomes, contract cost impacts, and upcoming negotiation timelines; develop and recommend enterprise-wide labor relations strategy, including standardization opportunities across the account portfolio; and support workforce and labor-cost planning by modeling the financial impact of proposed contract terms.
    • Performs other related duties and special projects as necessary or assigned.

Skills/Abilities:

  • Expert knowledge of labor relations principles, collective bargaining practices, and grievance/arbitration procedures.
  • Strong negotiation, conflict-resolution, and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate effectively with hourly employees, union representatives, and senior leadership.
  • Ability to interpret and apply contract language, statutes, and regulations accurately and consistently.
  • Strong organizational and time-management skills sufficient to independently manage competing deadlines across a multi-account, multi-state portfolio.
  • Ability to exercise sound, independent judgment and discretion on matters with legal and financial risk to the organization.
  • Proficiency with standard office/HRIS software and labor relations case-tracking tools.

Education and Experience:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Labor Relations, Industrial Relations, Business Administration, or a related field; equivalent professional experience may substitute for the degree requirement.
  • SHRM-SCP, SPHR, or equivalent labor relations certification preferred.
  • Minimum of seven (7) years of progressive labor relations experience, including direct experience negotiating collective bargaining agreements and managing grievance and arbitration processes.
  • Demonstrated experience independently managing labor relations for a multi-site, multi-state union portfolio as a sole practitioner, without a supporting labor relations team.

PCG is seeking an AI Solutions Analyst to support the design, delivery, and ongoing monitoring of AI-enabled solutions within state government environments. This role bridges client-facing requirements work with hands-on responsibility for how the AI system actually performs — translating policy and program needs into structured requirements, and using evaluation data to diagnose and improve system output quality.

The ideal candidate combines business analysis discipline with practical, hands-on fluency in enterprise AI — not just understanding how agentic workflows behave, but analyzing evaluation results with basic statistical reasoning and using that diagnosis to shape system behavior, within real-world constraints of performance, cost, and explainability.

This role is ideal for candidates who want to work inside how enterprise AI environments by writing the requirements, measuring the results, and closing the gap between the two.

What This Role Is Not

  • Not a data science or ML infrastructure role (no model architecture, training pipelines, or platform engineering)
  • Not a traditional business analyst role focused only on documentation
  • Not a project manager role only owning delivery execution or sprint ceremonies
  • Not a prompt-only or AI tool usage role without enterprise context understanding
  • Not a role where success is measured by prompt-writing volume — tuning here is diagnosis-led, grounded in evaluation data, not trial-and-error prompting

Key Responsibilities

Client Engagement & Requirements Facilitation

  • Support and lead client requirements sessions and discovery discussions
  • Translate policy and operational workflows into structured requirements

  • Iterate on prompts and instructions to address root causes identified through evaluation analysis
  • Identify tradeoffs related to performance, cost, token usage, and explainability
  • Partner with technical leads on tuning cycles within established review and sign-off processes

Delivery & Operations Support

  • Support broader program operations as needed — process design, cross-workstream coordination, and other work that helps scale delivery beyond a single engagement

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution
  • 4+ years of experience as a Business Analyst, Solutions Analyst, or Consultant

  • Working knowledge of basic statistics — sample sizes, error rates, false positive/negative distinction, and comfort reading distributions — sufficient to design representative evaluation test sets and interpret results
  • Hands-on experience iterating on prompts/instructions for LLM-based systems in a production or near-production setting
  • Working knowledge of AI systems, including behavior, limitations, and agentic workflows
  • Practical understanding of model selection tradeoffs, context/cost constraints, and agentic workflow limitations beyond prompt-level interaction with frontier models
  • Technical understanding of system architecture, data flows, APIs, and integrations

Preferred Qualifications

jobs.excerpt: AboutWe are reimagining the phone.  AI phones need to be proactive, intuitive, intelligent and low cost.
jobs.description:
About

We are reimagining the phone. AI phones need to be proactive, intuitive, intelligent and low cost. This is a mission critical for rest of the world to adopt intelligence.

There are over 5 billion people using everyday applications such as email, messaging, notes, tasks, and calendars, yet most are not AI-native. Our mission is to build proactive applications and devices that bring intelligence into daily conversations, coordination and workflows, with minimal prompting.

Focus: Designing and implementing the security and privacy architecture for the AI-native phone, ensuring AI agents can safely access user data, interact with applications, and execute actions across the operating system.

Unlike conventional mobile application security, this role needs to consider the additional risks introduced by AI agents having access to personal context, system services, and application-level actions.

Responsibilities

  • Design the overall security and privacy architecture for the AI-native phone.

  • Define permission models and access boundaries for AI agents interacting with user data and system services.

  • Design secure mechanisms for AI access to messages, contacts, calendars, notifications, camera, microphone, location and other sensitive information.

  • Implement appropriate sandboxing and isolation for agent execution.

  • Define authentication, authorization and access-control mechanisms for AI tools and application integrations.

  • Ensure users have control over what information AI can access and what actions it can execute.

  • Implement audit logging and user-visible activity tracking for AI access and actions.

  • Design secure storage, encryption, data retention and deletion mechanisms for personal data and memory.

  • Identify and mitigate AI-specific security risks, including prompt injection, malicious applications, data exfiltration and unauthorized tool execution.

  • Review Android permission models, privileged system access, SELinux policies and system-level security boundaries.

  • Work closely with Android/AOSP, Agent Runtime, Context & Memory and Applied ML teams to ensure security is built into the architecture rather than added later.

  • Conduct security assessments, threat modeling and penetration testing for system-level AI capabilities.

Requirements

  • Strong experience in mobile security, Android security, application security or systems security.

  • Deep understanding of Android security architecture, including application sandboxing, permissions, SELinux, Binder IPC and privileged system services.

  • Experience designing authentication, authorization and access-control systems.

  • Strong understanding of encryption, secure storage, key management and data protection.

  • Experience with security threat modeling, vulnerability assessment and penetration testing.

  • Understanding of privacy-by-design principles, data minimization and user consent.

  • Ability to work across Android platform, backend and AI agent architectures.

Nice to have

  • Experience with AOSP security customization or Android platform security.

  • Experience securing system-level applications or privileged Android services.

  • Experience with AI agent security, prompt injection, tool-use security and LLM data leakage.

  • Experience with mobile device security, Trusted Execution Environment (TEE), hardware-backed keystores and secure boot.

  • Experience with privacy engineering for products handling sensitive personal information.

  • Experience building permission and approval systems for autonomous agents.

Job Description
As a Platform Engineer, you'll build and own the software that takes our ML models from research to production: the Theia SDK that runs real-time inference at the edge, the APIs and services our customers and partners integrate with, and the cloud infrastructure behind our data and model pipelines. You'll work closely with our ML engineers and researchers, so you'll need to understand how models are trained, evaluated, and deployed, but your core focus is building reliable, well-designed systems around them.

What You'll Do

  • SDK Development: Design, build, and maintain the Theia SDK in Python and C++, delivering real-time eye-tracking inference across desktop, mobile, embedded, and XR platforms. Own packaging, performance, versioning, and the developer experience.
  • API & Backend Development: Design and implement APIs and backend services for data ingestion, model serving, licensing, and customer integrations, with a focus on clean interfaces, reliability, and security.
  • Cloud Engineering: Build and operate infrastructure on AWS, including containerized services on Kubernetes, infrastructure-as-code, CI/CD, and monitoring.
  • Full Stack: Build internal tools, dashboards, and customer-facing web interfaces that make our data and models accessible.
  • Data Science Engineering: Build and scale the pipelines that process millions of eye-tracking records for training, evaluation, and analytics. Clean, transform, validate, and analyze large tabular datasets, and build the tooling that lets our ML team explore and work with data efficiently.
  • ML Productionization: Partner with ML engineers to deploy, optimize, and monitor models in production and at the edge, including model conversion, latency and memory optimization, and inference pipelines.

Qualifications

Required

  • 2–4 years of professional software engineering experience building production systems
  • Strong Python skills, including packaging and distributing libraries
  • Working familiarity with C++ (reading, modifying, and building C++ code in a cross-platform codebase)
  • Experience designing and building APIs (REST, gRPC, or similar) and backend services
  • Hands-on experience with AWS, containers, and CI/CD
  • Experience working with large tabular datasets in pandas (data cleaning, transformation, aggregation, and performance at scale)
  • Working familiarity with machine learning: you understand the model lifecycle and have helped deploy or integrate ML models in a product
  • Strong communication skills and comfort working across engineering and research teams

Nice to Have

  • Experience building and shipping SDKs or libraries used by external developers
  • SQL and database engineering (schema design, query optimization, PostgreSQL or similar)
  • Kubernetes and infrastructure-as-code (Terraform or similar)
  • Frontend experience (React or similar)
  • Edge or on-device inference (ONNX Runtime, TensorRT, TFLite, Core ML, or similar)
  • Python compilation or distribution tooling (Nuitka, Cython, pybind11, or similar)
  • Exposure to time-series, sensor, or signal-processing data
  • Interest in VR/AR, eye tracking, or human-computer interaction
  • 1 year experience in a research setting (developing or working with ML research domains)

Why Join Us

  • Remote role with room to grow into automation, tooling, and AI-engineering work—not a pure manual-QA seat
  • Direct exposure to a novel technical stack: real-time eye-tracking, ML pipelines, SDKs, and VR/AR integrations
  • Tight feedback loop with senior engineering and leadership—the work you ship is felt across the company

How to Apply

This position reports into the engineering team. We're looking for someone who pairs solid QA fundamentals with curiosity for automation and AI-assisted workflows.

With your submission please attach:

  1. Your resume
  2. GitHub profile, portfolio, or links to relevant work (test suites, scripts, automations welcome)
  3. A short note on a bug you're proud of finding—or an automation/script that saved you or your team meaningful time

HarmonEyes is the world's only open, AI-powered eye-tracking platform that identifies and predicts a person's cognitive, emotional, and physical state based on eye movements alone. Compatible with any camera-based device, HarmonEyes provides a one-stop shop to analyze eye-tracking data, develop models, and deploy solutions to applications at scale with the Theia™ SDK. Backed by 60+ years of eye-tracking experience and born from the largest validated eye-tracking database (14 million unique records), HarmonEyes is used by the world's leading organizations in technology, aviation/automotive, healthcare, and elite performance in military and sports.

HAPPY HOWL®

Growth & Data Strategist

About Happy Howl

We started Happy Howl because we believe dogs deserve better — and better wasn’t available. Not from the legacy brands cutting corners with feed-grade ingredients, not from the fresh players who can’t survive a pantry shelf, and not from anyone willing to accept that the industry standard for pet nutrition is “good enough.”

We’re on a mission to help dogs live longer, healthier lives. Every recipe is 100% human-grade, single-source animal protein, zero preservatives, backed by real science and formulated by a PhD nutritionist who obsesses over every ingredient. Our food is shelf-stable for two years without refrigeration — real, whole-food nutrition that’s ready whenever and wherever your dog is. That combination doesn’t exist anywhere else.

But we’re more than a product. We work hand-in-hand with rescue organizations across the country because we believe every dog deserves a great meal — not just the ones who already found their forever home. Giving back isn’t a marketing campaign for us. It’s why we exist.

We’re backed by some of the most respected investors in consumer and pet, and we’re building the team that scales this brand past $100M in annual revenue. This is not a slow build. We move fast, we think big, and we hold ourselves to a standard most companies talk about but never actually live.

The people here are energetic, passionate, thoughtful, and intentional. We’re a team in every sense of the word — we win together, we solve hard problems together, and we’re building something that genuinely matters. If you want to do the best work of your career at a company that refuses to settle, Happy Howl is where you belong.

We’re headquartered in Huntingdon Valley, PA with team members across the US.

About the Role

You'll be the analytical engine behind Happy Howl's growth strategy. Working directly with the CFO, Marketing and Operations team, you'll own the customer economics analysis, model the scenarios that shape acquisition, and retention channel decisions, and bring us the story behind the numbers before we ask for it. This is a high-visibility role where your thinking directly shapes marketing spend, channel investment, and efficiency in operations.

What You’ll Do

  • Own independent scenario modeling across acquisition channels, cohorts, and customer types.
  • Conduct LTV/CAC analysis, retention curve modeling, and cohort-level customer economics reporting.
  • Translate raw performance data into a point of view, not just what happened, but what we should do about it.
  • Partner directly with founders/leadership to shape growth and marketing strategy using data as the backbone.
  • Build and maintain the analytical infrastructure (dashboards, reporting cadence) that lets the business move fast without a dedicated data team.
  • Support strategic analysis on ad spend scaling, MER thresholds, and channel-level ROI.
  • Present findings directly,with a recommendation attached, not just a chart.

What We’re Looking For

You think like a marketer and a finance person, and model like an analyst. You don't wait to be handed a question. You see something in the data, dig into it, and bring us the answer before we knew we needed to ask.

You own outcomes. When a model doesn't tie out or a trend looks off, you don't ship it and hope no one notices. You find the break, fix it, and flag it. The decisions made on your analysis are real: ad budgets, channel bets, growth strategy.

You move fast without sacrificing rigor. You can build a scenario model on a compressed timeline and still have it hold up under scrutiny.

You default to transparency. When the numbers tell a hard story, CAC creeping up, a channel underperforming, churn ticking higher, you say so clearly, with context and a recommendation, not buried in a footnote.

Nice to Have

  • SQL skills for data extraction and analysis.

  • Finance knowledge, able to read and build financial statements.

What We Offer

  • Competitive salary ($90K–$110K) plus bonus opportunity.
  • High-visibility role with direct exposure to founders and cross-functional leadership.
  • 100% remote work.
  • Real ownership over what gets investigated and why, not an execution-only analyst seat.

Lead laboratory data strategy, architecture, and migration planning for a complex pharmaceutical transformation.

FormativGroup partners with organizations to solve complex business and technology challenges through modern application, cloud, data, AI, and digital transformation solutions.

As a Laboratory Data Strategy & Architecture Lead, you will provide strategic and technical guidance for laboratory data across systems and platforms in a regulated pharmaceutical environment. You will own data strategy and roadmaps, guide mapping and conversion planning, and establish governance, quality, and integration requirements in partnership with laboratory, business, and technology stakeholders.

What You'll Work On

As Laboratory Data Strategy & Architecture Lead, you will:

  • Develop and lead laboratory data strategies, roadmaps, mapping approaches, and conversion plans aligned to business and technology objectives.
  • Define data reconciliation processes, quality standards, validation rules, and controls to support accurate and complete data migration.
  • Establish data ownership, stewardship, governance, metadata, master/reference data, and operational handover requirements.
  • Define laboratory data architecture, data models, integration patterns, interfaces, and cross-platform migration requirements.
  • Partner with laboratory systems teams, data architects, business stakeholders, and delivery teams to identify dependencies, risks, gaps, and remediation plans.
  • Provide subject matter guidance on laboratory data structures, workflows, and system transitions in regulated pharmaceutical environments.
  • Support connected analytics, reporting, and cloud data initiatives while aligning practices with applicable regulatory and compliance requirements.

What You'll Bring

You will likely be successful in this role if you have:

  • Extensive experience with laboratory systems and data in pharmaceutical or life sciences environments.
  • Demonstrated ownership of laboratory data strategy, roadmaps, data architecture, and cross-system transformation planning.
  • Direct experience with data mapping, conversion, migration planning, reconciliation, and data-quality controls.
  • Strong knowledge of data governance, stewardship, metadata management, and master/reference data practices.
  • Experience defining data models, system interfaces, integration requirements, and migration or validation standards.
  • Ability to work directly with business, laboratory, IT, and architecture stakeholders and turn complex requirements into actionable plans.
  • Working familiarity with cloud data platforms, analytics, and enterprise reporting environments.

How You Work

  • Take ownership of ambiguous data challenges and translate them into pragmatic strategies, standards, and delivery plans.
  • Communicate clearly with scientific, business, and technical stakeholders across a complex client program.
  • Balance strategic direction with hands-on analysis and careful attention to data quality, traceability, and delivery risk.

Bonus Points If You Have

  • Experience supporting large-scale laboratory system transformation or pharmaceutical data modernization programs.
  • Familiarity with GxP requirements and regulated laboratory data practices.
  • Experience with Laboratory Information Management Systems (LIMS), scientific data management, or cloud migration initiatives.

What Success Looks Like

  • A clear, stakeholder-aligned laboratory data strategy and practical roadmap are established.
  • Data ownership, architecture, mapping, conversion, reconciliation, and governance requirements are documented and actionable.
  • Migration dependencies and data-quality risks are identified early, with clear remediation and validation approaches.

jobs.description:
Job Description

The Collections Specialist oversees internal and external student accounts receivables for students navigating institutional financial obligations. Emphasizing proactive accounts receivable management and compliant collections, this role delivers exceptional, solution-oriented service to students and partners to promote student retention and fiscal responsibility across the university.

Number of Open Positions:1

Application Materials: Please submit a PDF of your resume/CV and provide at least two professional references who have served as your supervisor. Upload these files under the Documents section, located after "Links" and before "Questions" in the application. Please note that the email address you provide will serve as your account username for all future notifications. For any questions, please contact us at .

Compensation:

This is a Full-time, Non-exempt position at Grade 6, with a starting hourly range of $20.11 – $25.13. Salary ranges listed here represent a good faith and reasonable estimate of the range of possible compensation at the time of posting. Actual compensation will depend on several factors, including but not limited to, the candidate’s relevant experience and qualifications

Primary work location:

Remote: This position is classified as "Remote". The employee's home office is the primary work location and must be located in a state APU Global is registered in. The classification of this position is subject to change based on business needs, job performance, etc. If an employee changes their physical location/residence to another state, it could impact future employment.

Remote Expectation:

We expect our employees to be able to fulfill their APU Global responsibilities with minimal distractions. While remote work does offer flexibility, employees should make arrangements for regular dependent care during work hours. This is a fully remote position; however, travel may be required to meet business demands, university needs or team meetings as necessary.

Schedule:

To best accommodate our students’ needs and various schedules, candidates must be willing to work standard hours of Monday-Friday, 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM PST, with the exception of one late shift per week. This late shift (typically 9:30 AM – 6:00 PM PST) will be scheduled between Monday and Thursday, depending on the department’s needs.

Required Experience / Education

  • Christian Commitment: Vital Christian faith and lifestyle.
  • Supportive of the evangelical mission and purpose of Azusa Pacific University Global.
  • Associate’s degree.
  • Minimum 2 years previous experience in one or more of the following areas: student accounts, customer-based accounting positions (e.g. collections, loan administration), customer service, or closely related field.

Desired Experience / Education

  • Bachelor’s degree.
  • Previous experience working in higher education.
  • Knowledge of Azusa Pacific University Global policies and procedures.

Essential Functions

Internal Collections:

  • Contacting students with past due accounts to request payment.
  • Negotiating payment plans with students who are unable to pay their balance in full.
  • Working with the student accounts department to resolve any billing discrepancies or errors.
  • Maintaining accurate records of all collection activities and updating the university's student accounts database.
  • Preparing reports and analyses related to internal collections activity, and presenting findings to university leadership as needed.
  • Collaborating with other departments within the university to develop and implement policies and procedures related to student accounts receivable collections. Adherent to all federal and state regulations governing debt collection practices, including the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act (FDCPA).
  • Participating in professional development activities to stay up to date on industry best practices and regulations related to collections.

External Collections:

  • Managing relationships with external collections agencies, including monitoring performance.
  • Coordinating with the student accounts department to identify delinquent accounts and develop strategies for external collections.
  • Reviewing and approving external collections agency reports, ensuring accuracy and completeness of data.
  • Responding to inquiries from external collections agencies, students, and other stakeholders regarding collections activity.
  • Developing and implementing policies and procedures related to external collections, and ensuring compliance with industry best practices and regulations.
  • Monitoring the effectiveness of external collections strategies and recommending improvements as needed.
  • Maintaining accurate records of all external collections activity, and updating the university's student accounts database.
  • Preparing reports and analyses related to external collections activity, and presenting findings to university leadership as needed.

Student Accounts/Business Services (May Serve as Back Up)

  • Assist students with various questions regarding their accounts including but not limited to payments, holds, and refunds.
  • Run student account reports, analyze student accounts and records for accuracy and completion.
  • Contact students regarding past due accounts and provide due diligence in collecting money owed to the university.
  • Process student requests for refunds as required by federal regulations and University policies/procedures.
  • Communicate to students in a clear and concise manner, update comments and document all conversations in the appropriate area of the student management system.
  • Walk through the payment plan process with students.
  • Work with other departments (e.g. financial aid, admission, student success, military) as needed to address student related account and document inquiries

Other:

  • Participation in annual commencement may be required as determined by University needs
  • Other duties as assigned by management

Missional Expectations

All employees play a critical role in the establishment and maintenance of a robust Christian community that seeks to serve with grace the needs of all employees and students. As an APU Global employee, you are called to engage with your colleagues and all those that the university serves by modeling Christ-like character in all of your interactions. You will celebrate and honor other employees and students as being made in the image of God; be thankful, expressing gratitude to God and one another; build others up with your words; and work as an instrument of God's love seeking to heal a lost and broken world.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Exceptional customer service skills including:
    • Minimum 2 years previous experience in student financial aid, student accounts, customer-based accounting positions (e.g. collections, loan administration), or a closely related field.
    • Outstanding customer service skills including interpersonal and active listening skills along with an analytical and critical thinking ability to interpret and respond appropriately to diverse groups of people in various situations.
    • Capable of managing challenging student communications and escalations
    • Ability to communicate clearly and concisely with tact and diplomacy in all oral and written communications.
    • Ability to work effectively in a team environment and participate to get the job done, while continually focusing on the needs of the students.
    • Ability to exercise appropriate personal initiative, prioritization and accountability.
  • Knowledge of billing procedures, compliance and collection techniques
  • Computer proficiency and knowledge of or ability to learn a variety of computer applications including but not limited to standard Google Suite, Microsoft Office Suite, ERP, SIS, CRM, telephony, payment and communication systems.
  • General familiarity working in database systems including data entry, queries, and running reports.
  • Ability to accurately perform key mathematical functions (e.g. addition, subtraction, multiplication, division).
  • Demonstrated ability to work efficiently, in an organized manner and complete tasks in a fast-paced environment amidst interruptions and fluctuating workloads.
  • Ability to manage, interpret, and adapt guidelines and procedures in a complex university setting.
  • A positive, cooperative, Christ-like attitude supportive of the University and its mission.

Mental Demands

  • Ability to gather data, compile information, and prepare reports
  • Ability to investigate, analyze information, and draw conclusions
  • Ability to engage in critical thinking, exercise independent judgment, set priorities, and solve problems
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and manage confidential information

Physical Demands

This position typically includes the following physical demands. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

  • Ability to stand, walk, and sit for extended periods of time.
  • Sufficient hand, arm, and finger dexterity to operate a computer keyboard and other office equipment.
  • Visual acuity to read words and numbers.
  • Speaking and hearing ability sufficient to communicate in person or over the telephone.
  • Ability to exert up to 10 pounds of force and occasionally lift and/or move up to 15 pounds.

Technologies

  • Google Suite: Gmail, Google Docs, Google Sheets, Google Slides, Google Meets
  • Microsoft Office Suite: Microsoft Word, Microsoft Excel, Microsoft PowerPoint
  • Communication and collaboration: Slack, Zoom (or similar virtual meeting platform), Dialpad (telephony)
  • Computer Systems: Salesforce (CRM), Jenzabar J1 (ERP and SIS), Nelnet and Authorize.net (payment systems) or similar platforms

Non-discrimination Statement
