Silverback Strategies is a performance marketing agency built to help marketers grow and capitalize on change. Ad Age, Inc Magazine, The Washington Post, The Washingtonian, and The Washington Business Journal have recognized Silverback as one of the best places to work.

We hire the best and help them get better. Silverbackers are supported, challenged and inspired by their peers. Regardless of title or tenure, every Silverbacker plays a role in helping our agency get better. This is a place where you can make a difference.

What you will do:

    • Translate strategy into visuals: partner closely with our Creative Strategist to take research, hooks, and loose creative briefs and turn them into concrete visual concepts, storyboards, and finished assets
    • Produce both statics and video: design and build static ad creative and edit/produce short-form video and motion content for paid social at a consistently high craft level
    • Interpret brand guidance at any altitude: work from anything ranging from a thin one-pager to a comprehensive brand system, and reliably produce creative that's unmistakably on-brand either way
    • Navigate regulated-industry review cycles: produce creative that anticipates compliance and legal scrutiny, minimizing revision rounds and rejection risk without watering down creative quality
    • Push brands into new creative territory: identify opportunities to evolve a brand's creative expression to unlock scale and new-market growth, while staying inside brand-safety guardrails
    • Select and edit raw footage/imagery: review raw photography and video footage from shoots and select, crop, cut, and edit the strongest material into finished assets — no on-set creative direction required
    • Own asset quality and turnaround: deliver polished, client-ready work with minimal internal revision cycles so assets aren't burning days internally before they even reach the client
    • Maintain visual consistency at scale: keep creative consistent and on-brand across a high volume of ad variations, formats, and platform

What we are looking for:

    Core Experience
    • 5+ years in a hands-on creative production role — Art Director, Senior Designer, Creative Producer, or similar —with dedicated performance/paid social experience
    • A portfolio that shows range across both static design and video/motion editing, ideally for paid social specifically
    • Experience working within brand guidelines of varying depth and translating them into new creative applications
    • Experience in regulated or highly regulated industries (healthcare, finance, insurance, legal, or similar) is a strong plus, given our client base
    • Experience working in matrixed organizations with multiple stakeholders and layered approval processes

    Craft & Technical Skills
    • Expert-level proficiency in Figma (or similar) for static design and layout
    • Strong proficiency in After Effects (or similar) for motion graphics and video editing
    • Comfortable editing raw video/photo footage into finished assets: selects, cuts, pacing, captions/graphics overlays
    • Working knowledge of Adobe Creative Suite (Photoshop, Premiere, Illustrator) as needed
    • Understands platform-specific creative specs and best practices across Meta, TikTok, YouTube, Pinterest, and other paid social channels

    Creative & Strategic Judgment

    • A strong eye for what "good" looks like in modern performance advertising — thumb-stopping, polished, and effective, not just pretty
    • Understands performance/paid-social fundamentals (hooks, pacing, hierarchy, CTAs) well enough to make smart creative calls independently, without needing to run the strategy
    • Can take a loose brief or visual direction and fill in the gaps with sound creative judgment
    • High attention to detail — typos, brand misapplications, and spec errors don't make it to client review
    • Comfortable giving and receiving fast, iterative feedback in a deadline-driven environment

    Working Style
    • Thrives on speed without sacrificing polish — this role owns production timelines that need to move fast to offset long approval cycles
    • Collaborative by nature; sees the Creative Strategist as a partner, not a hand-off point
    • Self-sufficient in production; doesn't need heavy oversight to get from brief to finished asset

What success looks like:

    • Assets consistently reach client/compliance review in 1–2 internal revision rounds or fewer

    • Output balances brand safety with creative freshness — clients see growth and new territory, not just "more of the same"
    • The Strategist and Senior Performance Creative function as a true two-person creative engine, each covering what the other doesn't

What This Role Is Not:

    • Not a photo/video shoot creative director — you won't be expected to run or direct live shoots, just to select and edit from what's captured
    • Not a pure strategist — research, testing frameworks, and reporting live with the Creative Strategist, not this role

jobs.title: AI Phone - Security & Privacy Engineer
jobs.excerpt: AboutWe are reimagining the phone.  AI phones need to be proactive, intuitive, intelligent and low cost.
jobs.description:
About

We are reimagining the phone. AI phones need to be proactive, intuitive, intelligent and low cost. This is a mission critical for rest of the world to adopt intelligence.

There are over 5 billion people using everyday applications such as email, messaging, notes, tasks, and calendars, yet most are not AI-native. Our mission is to build proactive applications and devices that bring intelligence into daily conversations, coordination and workflows, with minimal prompting.

Focus: Designing and implementing the security and privacy architecture for the AI-native phone, ensuring AI agents can safely access user data, interact with applications, and execute actions across the operating system.

Unlike conventional mobile application security, this role needs to consider the additional risks introduced by AI agents having access to personal context, system services, and application-level actions.

Responsibilities

  • Design the overall security and privacy architecture for the AI-native phone.

  • Define permission models and access boundaries for AI agents interacting with user data and system services.

  • Design secure mechanisms for AI access to messages, contacts, calendars, notifications, camera, microphone, location and other sensitive information.

  • Implement appropriate sandboxing and isolation for agent execution.

  • Define authentication, authorization and access-control mechanisms for AI tools and application integrations.

  • Ensure users have control over what information AI can access and what actions it can execute.

  • Implement audit logging and user-visible activity tracking for AI access and actions.

  • Design secure storage, encryption, data retention and deletion mechanisms for personal data and memory.

  • Identify and mitigate AI-specific security risks, including prompt injection, malicious applications, data exfiltration and unauthorized tool execution.

  • Review Android permission models, privileged system access, SELinux policies and system-level security boundaries.

  • Work closely with Android/AOSP, Agent Runtime, Context & Memory and Applied ML teams to ensure security is built into the architecture rather than added later.

  • Conduct security assessments, threat modeling and penetration testing for system-level AI capabilities.

Requirements

  • Strong experience in mobile security, Android security, application security or systems security.

  • Deep understanding of Android security architecture, including application sandboxing, permissions, SELinux, Binder IPC and privileged system services.

  • Experience designing authentication, authorization and access-control systems.

  • Strong understanding of encryption, secure storage, key management and data protection.

  • Experience with security threat modeling, vulnerability assessment and penetration testing.

  • Understanding of privacy-by-design principles, data minimization and user consent.

  • Ability to work across Android platform, backend and AI agent architectures.

Nice to have

  • Experience with AOSP security customization or Android platform security.

  • Experience securing system-level applications or privileged Android services.

  • Experience with AI agent security, prompt injection, tool-use security and LLM data leakage.

  • Experience with mobile device security, Trusted Execution Environment (TEE), hardware-backed keystores and secure boot.

  • Experience with privacy engineering for products handling sensitive personal information.

  • Experience building permission and approval systems for autonomous agents.

jobs.description:
Reporting directly to the COO, the Manager, Strategic Operations serves as a force multiplier for the leadership team, ensuring priorities translate into disciplined execution. This role is responsible for maintaining work management platforms, operational playbooks, financial and IT systems. The Manager, Strategic Operations will help build and sustain the operational backbone of the company. You will also work closely with the COO on internal communications, board and investor materials and core organizational workflows. This role requires exceptional attention to detail, strong judgment, and a commitment to high professional standards.

About Epistemix

The most consequential decisions in public health, life sciences, insurance, and enterprise strategy share a common problem: they involve human behavior, network effects, and downstream effects that cannot be safely tested before action is taken. Traditional analytical techniques built on historical data were not built for this. Epistemix was.

We build simulation and data-driven modeling tools that let leaders visualize how strategies will unfold across populations and systems before they commit resources. By clarifying which variables drive outcomes, where leverage exists, and how they interact, we help organizations move from uncertainty to conviction. Getting these decisions right means faster interventions, better-allocated resources, and measurable improvements in human and economic outcomes. We exist to make that possible.

Our platform gives organizations access to realistic, high-resolution population data and the modeling infrastructure to run scenario planning at scale. Together, these capabilities let decision-makers stress-test strategies in a controlled environment before deploying them in the real world across healthcare, consumer industries, insurance, and government. We are approaching our Series B and actively building the team that will define what comes next.

Responsibilities

Operational Infrastructure

  • Organizational Systems: Support the COO in designing and maintaining internal systems that enable the organization to operate effectively. This includes shaping the structure of internal resources, playbooks, and working frameworks so that teams have clear guidance, consistent information, and easy access to the tools they need to execute.

  • Institutional Knowledge: Maintain key internal resources so critical information, decisions, and processes remain visible, searchable, and easy for teams to navigate as the company grows.

  • Execution & Change Management: Partner with the COO to lead internal initiatives, introducing improved ways of working, and supporting teams as new systems or operational practices are implemented. Review and refine internal resources, documentation, and operational frameworks to ensure they are consistent, practical, and aligned with the organization’s evolving needs.

Technology Operations

  • Technology Operations: Oversee the day-to-day operational management of company technology systems, including employee access, licensing, and basic infrastructure coordination. This role will ensure team members have the tools and access they need to work effectively while maintaining appropriate controls as individuals join, transition within, or exit the organization.

  • IT Vendor Management: Manage vendor relationships, prioritize requests, and ensure timely resolution of technology issues while maintaining high standards for responsiveness, reliability, and service quality.

  • Technology Stewardship: Help ensure the organization maintains reliable and well-managed technology systems by coordinating data protection practices, backups, and continuity safeguards. This role will help ensure the company’s information assets remain secure, organized, and protected.

Financial Operations

  • Financial Alignment: Serve as a key operational partner to the COO in maintaining financial visibility across the organization. Coordinate closely with the accounting team to track priorities, monitor open items, and ensure financial processes and operational decisions remain aligned.

  • Budget Discipline: Assist the COO in supporting the organization’s commitment to disciplined financial management by monitoring spending across teams and ensuring financial practices remain consistent with company priorities.

  • Expense & Travel Oversight: Oversee the company’s expense and travel processes to ensure they operate smoothly and in line with company standards. Maintain clear records, coordinate approvals where appropriate, and help ensure spending remains transparent, organized, and aligned with company expectations.

Leadership Operations & Strategic Coordination

  • Board Meeting Coordination: Support the COO in coordinating the operational rhythm of the enterprise, leadership team and board engagement cycles. Help ensure materials, updates, and deliverables are organized, timely, and aligned with company priorities. Respond to inquiries from board members and investors in a timely and professional manner.

  • Leadership Time Prioritization: Help maintain focus by supporting the coordination of leadership priorities and schedules. Ensure leadership time is directed toward the most important work, while maintaining clarity around competing demands and commitments.

  • Events & Organizational Milestones: Coordinate the planning and execution of key company moments including leadership offsites, company gatherings, and industry events. Ensure events are thoughtfully organized and aligned with the company’s broader strategic and cultural objectives.

  • Special Projects: Support high-priority initiatives led by the COO and leadership team by stepping in to advance urgent or complex workstreams, gathering information across teams, and ensuring important initiatives continue to move forward.

Qualifications

  • Bachelors Degree or equivalent experience

  • 5+ years of experience in Strategic Operations, Business Ops, or a high-level operational support role in a high-growth startup preferred.

  • Demonstrated ability to lead complex projects and drive team adoption.

  • Experience in software implementations and organizational change management.

  • Comfort managing hardware logistics, software licenses, and basic troubleshooting.

  • 2+ years of experience within a Series A or Series B stage company preferred.

  • Deep experience in building complex databases, interconnected wikis, and project management hubs in Notion or similar software.

  • Comfortable with accounting, budget tracking, and platforms like Ramp.

Why Join Epistemix?

By joining Epistemix, you will become part of a collaborative and rapidly growing team that values curiosity and creativity. We are fully remote, with team members in the United States and Europe. Benefits include:

  • Equity & Incentives – Participation in our stock option program.

  • Meaningful Impact – Apply your creative talents to revolutionize data-driven decision-making and make a real-world difference.

This is a remote position open to applicants located in the United States. Candidates must possess the legal right to work in their intended work location, as we are currently unable to sponsor or transfer employment visas for any country, including the United States.

jobs.title: Staff Engineer
jobs.excerpt: About WonderlyWonderly is a closed-loop, end-to-end system that self-improves on our customers’ revenue.
jobs.description:
About Wonderly

Wonderly is a closed-loop, end-to-end system that self-improves on our customers’ revenue. We serve the home service industry ($1.3T), and can consistently double a new customer’s revenue within 90 days. We make all of our AI and software completely free - and only get paid when our customers make real money. We’re here helping real small businesses make a life, pay for their children’s college tuition, and live the American dream.

Pre-AI SaaS sold tools. AI companies claim they sell outcomes - task done, call answered, lead booked, ticket resolved - but calls or leads aren’t the outcomes that ultimately matter. Revenue is what ultimately matters, and today, none of the AI companies actually promise revenue. Wonderly changes that.

Our 70-person team (mostly in PDE) spent over a year building in stealth; our thesis is that - if you actually want to control the end result (revenue) of a business and deploy AI fast/cheaply, you can’t just build the sexy part (agents), you must also build the unsexy parts and own everything end to end: the system of record layer and the application layer. We built from scratch every software a home service business needs - replacing ServiceTitan, Squarespace, Ringcentral, Jobber, Square, Hubspot, and a dozen others applications. And we built every agent necessary - AI marketing, AI receptionist, AI voice, AI sales outreach, AI sales coaching, AI follow-ups, AI 3D design, AI finance, AI quoting, AI collections, and more - all embedded inside our own system with native data access. As a result, we can deploy dozens of production-ready Agents to our customers in under 24 hours with no FDEs, no integrations, and no data cleaning work.

We are the most outcome driven business model in the business because we’ve proven our system and AI Agents actually work in driving the end result - revenue. We are not trying to sell our customers a dream - each of our 10+ core AI Agents help improve our customers’ revenue by 5-20%.

Wonderly already has PMF and has gone from 0 → 1 (we are happy to share more over a call), with very clear moat and deep industry knowledge that took a team of 70 hardcore A-players 18 months to build (we are at least 2 years ahead of anyone else in the space). We believe Wonderly has the potential to be a $100B - $1T outcome. The market is massive: home service businesses across North America (a $1.3T market). We’ve raised over $50M from top-tier investors, have $20M a year in free cashflow from another product line (Motion), and all that money gets pumped into Wonderly.

Token maxxing

So you’ve been token maxxing and spending $4,000 a month on AI subscriptions. You’re vibe coding to the max, and sleeping barely 5 hours a day. You’ve embraced the polyphasic sleep cycle, so you can wake up in the middle of the night and press ‘Enter’ a couple times (I think that’s called harness engineering these days). And at the end of it, what exactly have you shipped? Have you made anyone’s life better?

If you are focused on technology purely for the sake of technology, then this is not the company for you. If you cannot tie your technology to real, obvious, business results, then this is not the company for you. In a world of slop factories, Wonderly had a radical idea: the purpose of software is to make someone’s life better. And in return, they pay you money.

Crazy, I know.

We are ruthlessly focused on helping small business owners in middle America put food on the table, send their children to college, and live the American Dream. And our customers love us for it.

Wonderly gives Main Street the AI agents, capital, and growth team they need to scale, and charges nothing for any of it. We only get paid when our customers make real money. No surprise fees or gotchas.

Most marketing agencies will charge you a monthly fee on top of the marketing dollars you’d have to spend, and at the end of all of that they can’t even guarantee revenue to you. Wonderly flips all that on its head. Running a small business is hard enough - you shouldn’t have to worry about whether your marketing dollars are cost effective or not on top of that.

We provide the entire system of record, all the annoying backoffice business applications (no more stitching together ServiceTitan, House Call Pro, RingCentral, Squarespace, Docusign, Square, and a dozen others and praying they work well together). As a result, we can deploy dozens of production-ready AI Agents to our customers in under 30 minutes with no FDEs, no integrations, and no data cleaning work.

We are the most outcome driven business model in the business because we’ve proven our system and AI Agents work. We are not trying to sell our customers a dream - we deliver real revenue and profit to our customers. All of our software and AI Agents are free - as I said above, we only charge a percent of revenue we deliver for our customers. Each of our 10+ core AI Agents help improve their revenue by 5-20%.

Wonderly already has PMF and has gone from 0 → 1 (we are happy to share more over a call), with very clear moat and deep industry knowledge that took a team of 70 hardcore A-players 18 months of stealth to build. We believe Wonderly has the potential to be a $100B - $1T outcome. The market is massive: home service businesses across North America (a $2T market). We’ve raised over $50M from top-tier investors, have $20M a year in free cashflow from another product line (Motion), and all that money gets pumped into Wonderly.

Who You Are

You are a technologist at heart.

  • Your dream vacation is tinkering and building something new. Every couple months you have a new side project. If you do not tinker, you cannot have taste.

  • You are someone who keeps up with technology for fun. If I pulled up your youtube feed, it would be littered with tech talks.

  • You explore new ways of building purely for the craft.

  • You’re able to work startup hours because work is fun. This is the type of career someone would have to pay you to not do.

You’re someone who’s thought deeply about engineering strategy. You have strong opinions about the SDLC, and how it changes in the age of AI.

Above all, you’re deeply practical. The world is a messy place. You work with the world how it is, not how it should be.

The Role

Wonderly is building the first enterprise grade dark software factory. We have 50 internal tools (and growing) built this way, and we are rapidly improving our own development methods based on feedback from this development process. We are extremely reluctant to use external vendors; with our internal tools factory, we have replaced ~50 vendors (and more will be replaced soon). We do this for three main reasons:

1. Margin

Software is entering a low-margin era. Most of our customers’ margins are only 30-40%, and as a result, we cannot pay frivolously for vendors that we could easily replicate in-house ourselves.

With AI, the cost of building – and yes, maintaining – these tools in-house has dramatically decreased. Every dollar that we can save is a dollar more we can invest on behalf of our customers.

2. Operational excellence

Stitching together well known tools can quickly bootstrap you to an MVP in terms of business and engineering processes, but as you scale, you’ll find yourself tied down to the lowest common denominator of what each of these tools allow you to do. As a result, you’ll naturally adopt sub-optimal processes, and this will drive down your operational excellence.

Every operational mistake costs our customers real money. We cannot afford for this to happen. As we rapidly scale, we must have maximum flexibility to choose the best process first, and build the tooling to enable that process after the fact.

3. Software revolution

As AI continues to eat software and its production lifecycle, we need to have a semi-production environment to push the boundaries. We need a place where we can experiment without risking customer outages. I say semi-production because everything can work in a toy sandbox environment. Our internal tools on the other hand have real customers, real traffic, and numerous edge cases. It is complex enough to give a real sense of whether this will work without immediately putting our end customers at risk.

Many of the architectural and AI coding decisions we took in production were first started in our internal tools test bed.

Your role is the ultimate culmination of both the tinkering in internal tools and the maturity of actual production. We need both to co-evolve with each other. We’re looking for someone who is bringing technical excellence (real money is on the line here!) first and foremost, but can also peer into the future for what’s coming and position Wonderly for the AI native era.

You are capable of holding two opposing view points simultaneously: AI is going to change everything, and yet, most of what it produces today continues to be slop.

And your answer to the above paradox is ultimately going to be your roadmap in this company.

Compensation & Eligibility

  • Base Salary: $337,500

  • Equity: $396,000

  • Bonus: $135,000

We do not discriminate based on gender identity, race, ancestry, disability, religion, sexual orientation, pregnancy status, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. We welcome and encourage all qualified candidates to apply for our job openings.

jobs.title: Senior Project Manager
jobs.excerpt: Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous!
jobs.description:
Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous!

Our agentic platform helps finance and operations teams worldwide remove manual work from their core business processes, so work runs end-to-end with greater control and significant productivity gains.

Today, over 550 enterprise customers use BLP across 1,300+ deployed projects. In the processes we automate, customers achieve productivity improvements of 5 to 10 times.

To date, BLP remains majority employee-owned, with Goldman Sachs holding a minority stake as a growth investor. Our success is driven by deep expertise in technology and business processes, a superior product with strong product-market fit, reflected in an expanding customer base that includes Fortune 500 companies.

BLP is one of Switzerland's fastest-growing SaaS scale-ups; we are now entering our next phase of growth. From our headquarters on Zürich's Bahnhofstrasse, we're expanding globally, with a growing presence across Europe and North America.

Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard.

Location

This is a full-time position based in Munich or Cologne. Following a comprehensive onboarding period at our HQ in central Zurich (minimum one month), you will work from your home location, with regular visits to customers across the DACH region.

Team collaboration matters a lot to us. You will regularly spend time with the team in person, in Zurich and at our hubs, for team days, all-hands and offsites. These visits are financially supported by blp.

Your Mission

You get customers live. Hands on, end to end, and fast.

As a Senior Project Manager, you make large, global blp transformations happen. These programs touch finance, procurement and supply chain at once, run across multiple ERP systems and legal entities, and roll out country by country. Your job is to orchestrate all of it and get the customer live: the first go-live above all, because that is where credibility is won or lost, and then wave after wave with the same discipline. You run the steering committee, you lead a blp team on each engagement, and you do that across several engagements at once.

At both levels, scope is the single biggest lever on whether a project goes live on time. Protecting it is a daily job, not a contract clause. You escalate early and precisely rather than absorbing problems until they become critical.

You will not be alone with the technical side. Integrations Engineers handle the connection into the ERP, Technical Project Managers handle the harder solution design, and our Consultants take over the automation work after go-live. On our largest strategic accounts a Client Partner carries the relationship and the commercial number, so your attention goes to delivery quality.

We have done this many times, so you are not inventing the approach each time. A proven onboarding method and a strong toolkit are what let you carry your own customers from early on.

Your Career Path in Project Management

This is the path most of our delivery leadership came through, and we hire at every step of it. We place you according to your experience and the size of the programs you have delivered, and we are explicit about what the next step requires.

  • Project Manager: You get customers live end to end, several in parallel: guided onboarding for commercial customers, leading enterprise projects yourself, or a workstream on our largest programs. Typically you bring 2+ years in consulting, implementation or project management.

  • Senior Project Manager: You make large, global transformations happen: multiple ERPs, entities and countries, the steering committee, and a blp team on each engagement. Typically you bring 5+ years delivering complex, multi-country programs.

  • Next steps: Lead a delivery team, or move into Consulting and from there towards our Client Partner role on strategic accounts.

Moves into Consulting or Customer Success Engineering are open at every level, and many of our people make them.

Key Responsibilities

  • Run implementations end to end: kick-off, scope, planning, configuration, testing and go-live.

  • Manage several customers in parallel at different stages, and keep every one of them on date.

  • Work with customers on their processes, and flag early where a process assumption will not hold.

  • Coordinate the specialists on your projects: Integrations Engineers, Technical Project Managers and AI Automation Specialists.

  • Own scope actively. Recognize a change request for what it is and handle it deliberately.

  • Keep the project inside its budget, and raise it early when the effort is drifting.

  • Hand over cleanly at go-live to our Consultants and support organization.

In addition, as a Senior Project Manager

  • Own the delivery outcome of global programs from kick-off to the last go-live: plan, scope, dependencies and date.

  • Drive the first go-live relentlessly, then run wave planning across ERPs, entities and countries.

  • Run the steering committee and own the decisions that come out of it.

  • Write and execute the recovery plan when a program is off track.

  • Lead the blp team on each engagement and coach the Project Managers working on your programs.

What We're Really Looking For

The following key attributes ensure success in this role:

  • Scope Discipline – You notice when a project is quietly growing, and you raise it rather than absorbing it.

  • Ownership & Autonomy – You take initiative, move things forward, and deliver end to end without being chased.

  • Escalation Judgment – You escalate early, to the right person, with a proposal rather than a problem.

  • Client Confidence – You are comfortable running a meeting with a customer's finance or IT lead in it.

  • Four-Language Fluency – Technology, process, data and people. You speak each well enough to spot where a roadblock really sits.

  • Structured Under Pressure – When a project goes sideways you get sharper and more organized, not louder.

What You Bring

  • 4+ years of experience delivering complex projects: management consulting, enterprise software implementation, or large-scale transformation delivery.

  • Proven track record running multi-country or multi-entity programs with senior client stakeholders, and steering a committee that includes client executives.

  • Experience leading a delivery team rather than only a plan.

  • Strong analytical and communication skills. You can translate a business need into something a technical team can act on.

  • Fluent in German and English, spoken and written.

  • Bonus points for ERP implementation experience, finance or supply chain processes, or AI-driven SaaS.

Benefits

  • High ownership environment – you shape your projects, outcomes, and career path.

  • Impact at scale – your work powers automation across global enterprises.

  • Cross-functional exposure – work with engineers, data scientists, and business leaders daily.

  • Real growth – fast-paced environment, steep learning curve, and structured career progression.

  • Employee ownership – be part of a majority employee-owned company with a best-in-class stock option program.

  • Amazing team – become part of a driven and collaborative group of innovators.

  • Technology exposure – be at the forefront of AI and enjoy continuous learning opportunities.

  • Visits & offsites – paid visits and stays at our HQ in Zurich, including collaborative team offsites.

Ready to build the future of ERP automation? Join us and own your impact.

  • Identity and Access Management (IAM): Drive automation within the IAM infrastructure, focusing on automated role assignment, least-privilege policy enforcement, and audit-friendly logging of authentication and authorization events.

  • Enterprise Data Engineering: Architect and engineer robust data platforms for IT, ensuring efficient collection, normalization, and secure storage of high-volume enterprise data for reporting, audit, and advanced analytics.

jobs.description:
Who are we and why should you join us?

BetterHelp is on a mission to remove the traditional barriers to therapy and make mental health care more accessible to everyone. Founded in 2013, we are now the world’s largest online therapy service, providing affordable and convenient therapy across the globe. Our network of over 30,000 licensed therapists has helped millions of people take ownership of their mental health and change their lives forever. And we’re not stopping there – as the unmet need for mental health services continues to grow, BetterHelp is committed to being part of the solution.

As the Principal Product Manager, Network Economics at BetterHelp, you’ll join a diverse team of licensed clinicians, engineers, product pros, creatives, marketers, and business leaders who share a passion for expanding access to therapy. And as a mental health company, we take employee mental health just as seriously as we do our mission. We deeply invest in our team’s well-being and professional development, because we know that business and individual growth go hand-in-hand. At BetterHelp, you’ll carve your own path, make an immediate impact, and be challenged every day – with a supportive community behind you the whole way.

What are we looking for?

BetterHelp is looking for a principal-level individual contributor to own therapist compensation and incentives: the economic mechanisms that determine whether a client who needs care can find the right therapist, in their state, under their plan, as soon as possible. We match hundreds of thousands of clients to licensed therapists across every state and a growing set of insurance plans. How quickly that match happens comes down to the strength, size, and variety of our therapist population, and how quickly we can shift it toward the plans and states where clients are waiting.

This individual will own the mechanisms that drive that supply pool, compensation rates, structure, and incentives, as a product and be accountable for the business outcome, not just the shipped feature. That means close collaboration with cross functional stakeholders, deriving defensible answers to how much therapist capacity we actually need and where, and experiments that tell us how the network responds when we change what it earns.

It’s an exciting opportunity for someone who is deeply analytical and does their best work in ambiguity: able to take a problem where the data is incomplete and the stakeholders don’t yet agree, and still reach an effective outcome with the organization behind it. The problems here sit where product, economics, and clinical operations meet, all while making a difference in the lives of people seeking mental health care.

What will you do?

  • Own the incentive system that moves therapist availability toward where clients actually need it, designed to be targeted, measurable, and reversible
  • Own the structure and clarity of the compensation model itself: what a therapist can predict about their earnings, and what the model rewards them for
  • Define what “well supplied” means for a network like ours, and build the tools and features that close the gap
  • Build a compelling and sustainable earnings proposition for therapists, and use controlled rollouts and rigorous measurement to learn what actually moves availability before we commit to it, all within the realities of a licensed, independent clinical workforce
  • Incentivize the specific behaviors that create client access, including therapist availability, match acceptance, and continuity of care
  • Analyze and quantify the impact of every change we make, then draw conclusions and plan next steps based on actual data
  • Partner closely with matching, eligibility, member experience, therapist experience, and provider acquisition. Your systems and theirs depend on each other
  • Work cross-functionally with finance, clinical, legal, marketing, data science, and operations, who have a stake in nearly everything this role touches, to get a change designed, approved, launched, and measured
  • Participate in setting the strategy and long-term direction for the organization, both within and beyond the context of product
  • Own KPI’s and be obsessed about them
  • In a nutshell: Diagnose, model, design, test, measure, decide, systematize

What will you NOT do?

  • You will NOT worry about "runway", "cash left", or "how much time we have until the next round". We have the startup DNA but we're fully backed and funded, all the way to success.
  • You will NOT be confined to your "job". You will get involved in product, marketing, business strategy, and almost everything we do.
  • You will NOT be bogged down by office politics, ego, or bad attitude. Only positive, pleasure-to-work-with people are allowed here!
  • You will NOT get yourself burned out. We work hard but we believe in maintaining a sustainable work/life balance. Really.

Can I work remotely?

Yes. We operate on PST and candidates in any time zone are welcome to apply. We ask employees to travel to our San Jose, CA office up to three times per year plus one company-wide offsite to collaborate in person and strengthen working relationships. Travel expenses are covered and reasonable accommodations are made for those under unique circumstances who cannot travel.

Requirements

  • 8-10 years experience in a product role with proven success through measurable impact and increasing responsibilities, including experience owning pricing, incentives, payouts, or supply-side economics in a two-sided marketplace
  • Super analytical: you can build the model, defend it in a room with data science, and explain it to a CFO without losing either audience
  • Deep understanding of unit and business economics, and a proven ability to balance business, clinical, and technical considerations in a product decision
  • You know which decisions to test cheaply and which ones you only get to make once, and you can tell the difference under time pressure
  • Strong understanding of marketplace dynamics and two-sided marketplace business models
  • Sound judgment in ambiguity. You can tell when the evidence is good enough to act on and when the right move is to dig deeper, and you can explain which call you’re making and why
  • A track record of driving cross-functional decisions to a conclusion without authority over the people who have to agree
  • Excellent written communication. Much of this role is making a quantitative argument that an executive audience can act on
  • Excellent organizational and leadership skills, strong attention to detail, able to work independently

Bonus (Great to have, but not required):

  • Experience with supply-side economics in a marketplace where supply is labor: ride-hail, delivery, or a professional services marketplace
  • Experience compensating an independent contractor workforce, and familiarity with the constraints that come with it
  • Experience in healthcare, insurance, or another business where eligibility and payer rules shape who can serve whom
  • Fluency with experimentation and causal inference where clean randomization isn’t always available

Benefits

  • Remote work with regular in-person bonding experiences sponsored by the company
  • Competitive compensation
  • Holistic perks program (including free therapy, employee wellness, and more)
  • Excellent health, dental, and vision coverage
  • 401k benefits with employer matching contribution
  • The chance to build something that changes lives – and that people love
  • Any piece of hardware or software that will make you happy and productive
  • An awesome community of co-workers

The base salary range for this position is $210,000 - $250,000. In addition to the base salary, this position is eligible for a performance bonus and the extensive benefits listed here (subject to eligibility requirements): Teladoc Health Benefits 2026. The Company

Industrial Technology Group (ITG) is an operating platform of The Heico Companies, LLC, overseeing 11 independent manufacturing companies which produce a wide array of equipment and products serving multiple industries and end users. ITG’s independent business model fosters entrepreneurship and growth and allows professional development at all levels.

ITG harbors a philosophy of developing close customer engagement, providing prompt, responsive service to meet our customer's changing needs, while striving to be leaders within our respective industries. Equipment and products are marketed domestically through a direct sales force, manufacturer's representatives and an established network of independent dealers. Internationally, ITG sells in more than 60 countries through an independent distributor network, company sales representatives, licensees and agents. Our portfolio of companies is diverse and has a solid management base, product/market niches and efficient manufacturing capabilities.

Position Summary

The Manufacturing Engineer develops and implements optimal, cost-effective manufacturing processes in alignment with product specifications and quality standards. This remote-based role requires approximately 75% travel to support manufacturing sites, where the engineer works directly on the shop floor to analyze equipment layout, workflow, assembly methods, and workforce utilization to drive efficiency and reduce waste. As a high-visibility position with exposure across multiple levels of the organization, the Manufacturing Engineer plays a key role in supporting the growth strategy of the Industrial Technologies Group and its Business Units.

  • Analyzes and plans work force utilization, space requirements, workflow, and designs layout of equipment and workspace for maximum efficiency.
  • Develops, evaluates, and improves manufacturing methods, utilizing knowledge of product design, materials and parts, fabrication processes, tooling and production equipment capabilities, assembly methods, and quality control standards.
  • Collaborate with planning and design staff concerning product design and tooling to ensure efficient production methods.
  • Works with vendors to determine product specifications and arrange for purchase of equipment, materials, or parts, and evaluates products according to specifications and quality standards.
  • Estimates production times, staffing requirements, and related costs to provide information for management
  • Coordinate with management, engineering, and other staff regarding manufacturing capabilities, production schedules, and other considerations to facilitate production processes.
  • Conducts Value Stream Analysis, manufacturing process flow redesigns, time and motion studies as part of the planning process.
  • Applies statistical methods to estimate future manufacturing requirements and capture potential efficiencies.
  • Leads plant employees in conceptualizing, planning, implementing, and sustaining continuous improvements by utilizing Lean Manufacturing tools.

Job Requirements

  • Bachelor of Science in Mechanical/Manufacturing engineering required.
  • 3-5+ years’ work experience in a manufacturing facility in an engineering role with proven track record of delivering results. Strong internship experience will be considered in place of.
  • Proven ability to see facility projects through to completion, on time and within budget.
  • Able to effectively carry out a vision and collaborate with Production, Materials and Quality teams.
  • AutoCAD/Solid works experience required. Experience designing manufactured parts and developing comprehensive production floor layouts is preferred.
  • Technically proficient in applicable programs related to process improvement & MS Office.
  • Ability to present in a clear and concise manner within all layers of the organization.
  • Strong analytical, organization and communication skills.
  • A high energy team player with a go-getter attitude.
  • This role supports projects across multiple business units nationally, requiring 75% travel

Candidates must be authorized to work in the United States without the need for current or future visa sponsorship.

Work Environment

A Manufacturing Engineer works in a fast-paced production setting, balancing time on the shop floor with analytical planning. The role involves close collaboration with operators, maintenance, quality, and leadership to improve safety, efficiency, and performance. The environment can be loud, dirty, and subject to varying temperatures, requiring appropriate protective equipment and adaptability.

Physical Demands

This position requires frequent standing and walking on the production floor, with occasional bending, stooping, and reaching. The role may involve lifting and carrying materials or equipment up to 40 pounds and working around moving machinery. Employees must be able to tolerate varying temperatures, noise levels, and industrial conditions while wearing required personal protective equipment. Clear vision, including the ability to distinguish between colors, and strong attention to detail are essential.

Compensation & Benefits:
Estimated salary range: $75,000 – $90,000 annually.

This position is eligible for the company’s full benefits package, including medical insurance, life insurance, short-term and long-term disability coverage, paid vacation and sick leave, and paid holidays.

Key Competencies

  • Data Gathering and Analytics - Collecting, consolidating, and using relevant information; recognizing important information; tracing possible causes of problems, and searching for practical data/solutions.
  • Attention to Detail - Taking responsibility for a thorough and detailed method of working.
  • Planning and Organizing – Setting priorities and defining actions, time, and resources needed to achieve predefined goals.
  • Communication Skills - Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to effectively deliver and reinforce consistent messages at all levels. Excellent listening skills.
  • Problem Solving - Having the ability to identify problems and issues of varying complexities and to find effective solutions with few guidelines.
  • Teamwork - Working as a productive member of a cohesive group toward a common goal and contributing to team development and effective team dynamics.
  • Continuous Learning - Actively and continuously gaining insight of strengths and weaknesses to identify the relevant areas that need further development (with regard to skills and knowledge) and acting upon it.

This role may be a fit for you if:

  • You write with judgment, not just accuracy. You can take a complicated file, determine what actually happened, and state a clear, complete, well-supported position under a deadline.

  • You solve problems at the root. You love digging beneath the surface to identify root causes and aren't afraid to roll up your sleeves to resolve complex edge cases while mentoring others to do the same.

  • You build and maintain operational rigor. You thrive in a remote environment, bringing organization, accountability, and process design to ensure compliance deadlines are met without exception.

What you’ll actually do:

  • Lead Escalation Operations: Oversee the end-to-end investigation and de-escalation framework for critical customer complaints, acting as the final point of escalation for complex issues.

  • Own DOI and Insurance Carrier Responses: Manage carrier audits and state regulatory complaint workflows; author, review, and finalize official correspondence to state departments of insurance, carrier partners, and consumers.

  • Complaint Log & Compliance Controls: Own the complaint log and the workflows behind it, keeping records accurate and audit-ready for market conduct examinations and state data calls, and meeting statutory deadlines and internal SLAs.

  • Carrier Relationship & Claims Support: Serve as the primary operational liaison for carrier partners during high-stakes claims investigations, regulatory inquiries, and information audits.

  • Team Guidance & Coaching: Provide operational guidance, quality oversight, and subject-matter expertise to team members handling customer service, compliance, and claims support.

What we’re looking for:

  • 5+ years of insurance experience, including 3+ years in state insurance and regulatory compliance.

  • 2+ years in a team lead, managerial, or supervisory role preferred.

jobs.description:
About Featherless

is building the world's most reliable open-model inference platform.

Backed by AMD, Airbus Ventures, 500 Global, Kickstart Ventures, HF0 Residency, Panache Ventures, and Oakseed Ventures, we're a well-funded team of researchers and engineers on a mission to democratize AI through performance and accessibility.

Our cloud provides instant access to 40,000+ open-source AI models and the research innovations powering next-generation efficiency, reliability, and model optimization.

About the Role

We're hiring our first Sales Engineer to pair directly with our founding Account Executive in North America. You are the technical half of a two-person deal team: the AE owns the commercial motion, you own the technical win.

Our buyers are developers, ML engineers, and CTOs, and they don't buy on slides. They buy when someone credible sits with them, looks at their workload, and shows them that open models on Featherless are faster, cheaper, and more reliable than what they're running today. That's your job — hands on keyboard, in the customer's stack, from first technical call through production rollout.

Because you're the first SE here, you'll build the function as you go: the demo environment, the POC playbook, the benchmark harness, the security answers, the migration guides. Every deal you win should make the next one easier to win.

If you like being the person who can actually answer the hard question in the room — and want the technical foundation of a Series A GTM engine to be yours — this is for you.

What You'll Own Immediately

  • Partner with the founding AE as the named technical owner on every active opportunity in North America

  • Run technical discovery: map each prospect's models, workloads, latency and throughput targets, spend, and constraints

  • Design and drive POCs and benchmarks that prove Featherless against the incumbent — closed-model APIs, another inference provider, or self-managed GPUs

  • Build the demo environment and reusable technical collateral that the whole GTM team sells with

  • Own technical objection handling end-to-end: performance, reliability, cost modeling, security, and data handling

  • Be the field's voice into product and engineering — you'll know what we're losing on before anyone else does

Core Responsibilities

  • Lead technical calls tailored to each buyer's stack: architecture reviews, live demos, and working code against their real use case

  • Build migration paths off closed-model APIs and onto open weights — model selection, evaluation, prompt and output parity, cutover plan

  • Run benchmarks and produce the throughput, latency, and cost-per-token analysis that anchors the business case the AE builds

  • Scope and execute POCs with clear technical success criteria, then hold the customer and us to them

  • Write the technical sections of proposals, RFP responses, and security questionnaires; keep a reusable answer library so we never write the same answer twice

  • Support onboarding and first production workloads, then hand off cleanly and stay available for expansion

  • Feed structured field input to product and engineering — feature gaps, model coverage requests, reliability issues, competitive intel

  • Build and maintain the technical assets that scale the team: demo apps, notebooks, reference architectures, integration guides, internal enablement for BDRs and future AEs

  • Represent Featherless technically at conferences, meetups, and developer events

  • Keep POC and technical-stage detail current in HubSpot so forecasting reflects technical reality, not optimism

What You Bring

  • 3–6 years in pre-sales engineering, solutions architecture, or a forward-deployed / customer-facing engineering role — at a GPU cloud, inference provider, MLOps platform, AI/developer tooling company, or cloud infrastructure vendor

  • Genuinely hands-on: you write Python comfortably and build your own demos rather than requesting them

  • Working knowledge of modern LLM inference — serving stacks (vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM or similar), OpenAI-compatible APIs, quantization, LoRA and fine-tune serving, batching and KV cache behavior, and what actually drives tokens/sec and cost

  • Practical familiarity with the open-model ecosystem: Hugging Face, the major open weight families, and how teams evaluate one model against another

  • Comfortable with containers, Kubernetes, and cloud networking and security fundamentals

  • Credible with both audiences in the same meeting — the ML engineer who wants the numbers and the CTO who wants the risk and cost story

  • Strong written communication: your benchmark writeups and architecture docs should be good enough to forward to a buyer's CEO

  • Entrepreneurial and self-directed — comfortable being the first SE, with no playbook and no one to escalate the technical answer to

  • Use AI tools heavily in your own workflow to research, prototype, and move faster

Nice to have: experience selling or building on AMD GPUs / ROCm; exposure to enterprise security and compliance review; open-source contributions or public technical writing; experience as the first technical hire on a GTM team.

Why Featherless

  • Build the sales engineering function at a company in one of the fastest-moving spaces in AI

  • Work as a true pair with the founding AE, and directly with the CRO and founders — small team, no layers, immediate impact

  • Real technical depth: 40,000+ open models and an in-house research team shipping inference and optimization work you'll get to sell

  • Be part of a small, high-performing team making open weight AI accessible to everyone

  • Competitive base + variable tied to the team's number, plus equity

Compensation Range: $150K - $190K

About Menlo

Menlo Research is an Applied R&D lab building Asimov, an open-source humanoid robot platform, and the full software stack that powers it. Our mission is to make humanoid labor economically viable, turning software into physical labor at scale. We build across the full stack: hardware architecture, locomotion, autonomy, simulation, and infrastructure. We move fast, ship to real robots, and open-source everything we can. If you want your work to matter beyond a paper or a demo, this is the place.

The Role

We are looking for a Researcher, Manipulation to give Asimov hands that can do real work. We recently ported our RL stack from locomotion to manipulation, taking Asimov from walking to flipping, and you will drive what comes next: grasping, dexterous and contact-rich tasks, and the kind of whole-body coordination where an arm, a torso, and two legs have to solve one problem together. You will get skills onto real hardware and keep pushing until they hold up outside a controlled setup.

What You'll Do

  • Design, train, and ship reinforcement learning policies for manipulation, grasping, and dexterous, contact-rich tasks on Asimov

  • Build on our locomotion-to-manipulation RL work and extend it toward whole-body manipulation, where balance and reaching are one problem

  • Own the sim2real pipeline for manipulation, using our zero-shot sim2real approach so skills transfer to hardware cleanly

  • Design rewards, training environments, and randomization strategies in MuJoCo for contact-heavy tasks that are hard to simulate well

  • Close the loop with real telemetry from real arms and hands, then feed failures back into the next policy

  • Collaborate closely with locomotion, controls, and hardware researchers, since a humanoid manipulates with its whole body

  • Open-source what you can and share what you learn with the community building on Asimov

What We Look For

  • Deep hands-on experience with reinforcement learning or learning-based methods for manipulation, grasping, or dexterous control

  • A track record of getting manipulation policies onto real robots, not only into papers or simulators

  • Strong command of a physics simulator such as MuJoCo, Isaac, or similar, including contact modeling, reward shaping, and domain randomization

  • Fluency in Python and modern RL tooling, and comfort in a ROS2-based control stack

  • A bias for shipping: you would rather watch a policy fumble a real object this week than perfect it in sim next month

  • Clear thinking about why contact-rich tasks fail, and how to close the gap

Nice to Have

  • Published work in manipulation, dexterous control, grasping, or imitation learning

  • Experience with tactile sensing, force control, or teleoperation and demonstration data

  • Experience with whole-body control that spans locomotion and manipulation

  • Contributions to open-source robotics or RL projects

Why Join Menlo

You will own manipulation for a humanoid that thousands of developers are building on in the open. Your skills will ship to real robots and real hands, not slides, and the community will see them work. If you want your research to reach into the physical world and pick things up, this is the place.

A Note on AI

You don't need deep AI expertise for every role, but we do expect everyone at Menlo to be intellectually curious, drawn to tinkering and discovery, and excited to use AI as a real collaborator in their work. For some roles, AI fluency is a core requirement. When that's the case, we'll say so explicitly in the qualifications. People who thrive here don't treat AI as a novelty. They use it to think better, and make their work easier for others to build on.

Equal Opportunity and Accommodations

We hire talented people from a wide range of backgrounds. If you're excited about a role but don't meet every bullet, we still encourage you to apply. Menlo Research is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of any legally protected characteristic. Menlo provides reasonable accommodations during the application process. If you need one, please let your recruiter know.

jobs.excerpt: About MFAN The Military Family Advisory Network (MFAN) is a national nonprofit organization that conducts rigorous research, develops responsive programs, and brings together military families, government, nonprofit, and private-sector partners to drive meaningful change.
jobs.description:
About MFAN

The Military Family Advisory Network (MFAN) is a national nonprofit organization that conducts rigorous research, develops responsive programs, and brings together military families, government, nonprofit, and private-sector partners to drive meaningful change. MFAN is entering an important period of growth and transformation as we implement a new strategic plan, strengthen our national positioning, expand the reach of our research and programs, and prepare for a rebrand and website redesign. 

The Opportunity

MFAN seeks a seasoned, strategic Director of Communications to lead an integrated, enterprise-wide communications function. This is not solely a content-production or media-relations role. The Director will establish a multi-channel communications plan, systems, standards, and team practices that enable MFAN to communicate with greater clarity, consistency, and influence as the organization grows. 

Reporting initially to the Chief Executive Officer, the Director will translate complex research, program impact, policy priorities, and the lived experiences of military families into compelling communications for diverse audiences. The Director of Communications will be counted on to delegate and lead a team, while managing a budget and discerning when it is appropriate to bring in outside support for specialized, tactical elements. The Director will be MFAN's senior communications advisor, lead major organizational initiatives, and manage staff, contractors, agencies, budgets, and workflows. The ideal candidate is both a strong strategist and an excellent operator: someone who can set the direction, build the plan, guide others, and step in personally when the moment requires it. 

This is a consequential role; the Director of Communications must have excellent judgement and understand the content, stakeholders, and environment that MFAN operates in. A growth mentality is a must.

What Success Looks like in the First Year

  • Build and begin implementing a multiyear communications strategy aligned with MFAN's 2027–2030 strategic plan and organizational goals. 
  • Create an integrated editorial and campaign-planning system that aligns research, programs, government relations, advancement, events, and executive communications. 
  • Strengthen MFAN's national visibility and reputation as a trusted, nonpartisan source of military family insight and solutions. 
  • Develop a disciplined approach to translating MFAN's data, evidence, and impact into accessible narratives for families, funders, policymakers, partners, media, and the public. 
  • Assess and strengthen the communications team structure, vendor portfolio, workflows, measures of success, and quality-control practices. 
  • In coordination with leaders across the organization, develop and implement the personnel, technology, and systems infrastructure needed to advance strategic priorities, align resources with the budget, and strengthen organizational efficiency, productivity, and quality—not just for the communications area, but for the full organization. 
  • Lead communications planning and execution for MFAN's rebrand and website redesign, in close partnership with executive leadership and external specialists. 

Position Type / Hours of Work

  • Full-Time, Exempt Position
  • Hours: Standard hours of operation are 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. ET on Monday–Thursday and 8 a.m. to 2 p.m. ET on Fridays, unless otherwise approved by the department lead. There will be occasions when extended hours are required due to events, travel, meetings, or other requirements.
  • Location: Remote. As this is a fully remote position, candidates are expected to have a dedicated workspace and access to high-speed internet. This position is limited to a candidate living in the 48 contiguous states and must have regular availability during Eastern Time business hours.
  • Travel: Travel is required for conferences, partner meetings, MFAN events, and staff retreats (monthly travel should be expected).  

Duties & Responsibilities

Enterprise Communications Strategy and Leadership 

  • Develop and own an integrated communications strategy that advances MFAN's mission, strategic plan, reputation, growth, and impact. 
  • Serve as a senior advisor to the CEO and executive leadership team on messaging, organizational positioning, reputation, emerging issues, and communications opportunities. 
  • Establish clear annual priorities, audience strategies, campaign plans, performance measures, decision rights, and cross-functional workflows. 
  • Design, implement, and maintain organization-wide communications efforts and operating rhythms in close coordination with research, programs, fundraising, government relations, and events leaders, ensuring that priorities are aligned and work moves forward with clear ownership and accountability. 
  • Lead through organizational change, helping staff understand and consistently communicate MFAN's evolving strategy, identity, priorities, and value. 

Brand, Messaging, and Digital Transformation 

  • Steward MFAN's brand and ensure consistent use of its voice, messages, narrative, and visual identity across the organization. 
  • Lead communications strategy and internal coordination for MFAN's rebrand and website redesign, including audience needs, content architecture, editorial standards, launch planning, and adoption. 
  • Maintain a reliable source of approved messages, evidence, proof points, and organizational language for use across communications, fundraising, partnerships, and public engagement. 
  • Oversee MFAN's website, email, social media, digital campaigns, and other external channels, using data to improve reach, engagement, and conversion. 

Research Translation, Thought Leadership, and Storytelling 

  • Partner closely with research and impact leaders to translate complex findings into clear, accurate, timely, and actionable communications without compromising rigor. 
  • Develop thought-leadership strategies that position MFAN and its subject-matter experts for media commentary, speaking opportunities, op-eds, convenings, and other influential platforms. 
  • Create a balanced narrative approach that combines credible data, program outcomes, partner contributions, and the lived experiences of military families. 
  • Guide communications for major research releases, national events, program launches, and rapid-response moments. 

Media, Executive, and Public Communications 

  • Build and sustain relationships with national, military, policy, trade, and local media; identify timely opportunities and develop proactive pitches. 
  • Prepare the CEO and other subject-matter experts for interviews, speeches, panels, testimony, and high-visibility engagements. 
  • Draft or oversee executive communications, public statements, talking points, opinion pieces, presentations, and sensitive organizational messages. 
  • Develop practical issues-management and crisis communication protocols and lead communications when rapid coordination is required. 

Advancement, Partner, and Program Communications 

  • Partner with advancement to ensure donor and corporate-partner communications are compelling, accurate, consistent, and aligned with MFAN's broader narrative. 
  • Support the development of cases for support, proposals, stewardship materials, sponsorship campaigns, reports, and other high-value communications while maintaining clear ownership between communications and fundraising. 
  • Collaborate with programs and government relations to reach military families, partners, policymakers, and community stakeholders with audience-specific communications. 
  • Lead communications planning for partner campaigns while protecting MFAN's credibility, nonpartisan voice, and brand standards. 

Team, Operations, and Performance 

  • Lead, coach, and develop communications staff while creating clear expectations, accountability, and opportunities for growth. 
  • Select and manage agencies, consultants, designers, producers, freelancers, and other vendors; oversee scopes, timelines, budgets, quality, and results. 
  • Build repeatable systems for intake, prioritization, editorial planning, production, review, approval, asset management, and performance reporting. 
  • Use analytics and audience insight to evaluate results, communicate progress, and continuously improve strategy and execution. 
  • Manage the communications budget and make thoughtful decisions about internal capacity, external support, and resource allocation. 

Required Experience & Skills

  • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university.
  • At least eight years of progressively responsible experience in strategic communications, public relations, marketing, journalism, public affairs, or a related field, including meaningful experience leading a communications function or major portfolio. 
  • Demonstrated success developing and executing integrated communications strategies tied to organizational priorities and measurable outcomes. 
  • Demonstrated ability to manage multiple complex priorities, adapt quickly to changing needs, and deliver polished, high-quality work in a fast-paced environment. 
  • A collaborative, no-ego leadership style and the ability to build trust and accountability across functions in a remote organization. 
  • Experience leading staff and managing consultants, agencies, vendors, budgets, and simultaneous high-stakes projects. 
  • Experience leading a significant brand, messaging, website, or organizational-positioning initiative through planning, stakeholder alignment, implementation, and adoption. 
  • Exceptional writing, editing, message-development, and storytelling skills across executive, media, digital, donor, partner, and public-facing formats. 
  • Strong record of translating complex information, research, or policy into accessible and compelling content while protecting accuracy and nuance. 
  • Sound judgment and the ability to advise senior leaders, navigate sensitive issues, manage competing perspectives, and make decisions in a fast-moving environment. 
  • Commitment to MFAN's mission, nonpartisan approach, and responsibility to represent military families with accuracy, dignity, and respect. 

Preferred Skills

  • Experience in a national nonprofit, research, policy, public affairs, association, or other mission-driven organization. 
  • Experience communicating research findings or supporting advocacy, public policy, or systems-change efforts. 
  • Familiarity with military and veteran communities, military family policy, or the national-security ecosystem. Military affiliation is welcomed but not required. 
  • Experience supporting fundraising, corporate partnerships, sponsorships, or cause-marketing initiatives. 
  • Experience with modern content management, email, social media, project management, and analytics platforms. Familiarity with specific software is less important than the ability to select and use tools strategically. 

Benefits

We’re proud to offer a comprehensive and people-centered benefits package designed to support your well-being both in and out of work:

  • Health & Wellness: QSEHRA (Qualified Small Employer Health Reimbursement Arrangement) to help cover your health insurance and medical expenses.
  • Technology Allotment: MFAN offers monthly technology reimbursement or stipend.
  • Time to Recharge: Generous vacation days, sick leave, and compassionate leave—because life happens.
  • Summer Fridays: Enjoy shortened hours on Fridays during the summer months.
  • 401K: Available immediately upon hire with a 3% employer match.

We believe in flexibility, care, and supporting our team with meaningful benefits that promote balance and sustainability.

Working Conditions

The work environment described here is representative of those an employee encounter while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable

individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. The qualified employee will work in a

dynamic home office setting, and interact with staff and consultants, and therefore may be subjected to

interruptions throughout the workday. The position will require some flexible hours, and when

applicable, local and national travel will be required.

Location & Work Authorization

This position is open only to candidates who are legally authorized to work in the United States and who will perform all work from within the United States. MFAN does not sponsor employment visas or assume sponsorship of existing employment visas, now or in the future.

Equal Employment Opportunity Statement

MFAN is an equal employment opportunity employer. Employment decisions are made based on qualifications, merit, and organizational needs. MFAN does not discriminate against employees or applicants in any aspect of employment and prohibits harassment of any kind, in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local laws.

This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation, and training.

Salary: $115,000-$145,000
