jobs.title: Senior Financial Analyst
jobs.excerpt: ITHAKA’s mission is to expand access to knowledge and education around the world.
jobs.description:
ITHAKA’s mission is to expand access to knowledge and education around the world. Our services — JSTOR, Portico, and Ithaka S+R — enable people everywhere to learn, to grow, and to overcome barriers to education. In carrying out our mission, as employees we feel a deep responsibility to members of our community and to each other, and we are committed to building and sustaining a culture where everyone can thrive.

The Role

ITHAKA is seeking a Senior Financial Analyst to serve as a strategic finance partner for cost support and analysis in our product and shared services areas of JSTOR, JSTOR Stewardship, Portico, and Ithaka S+R.

This is a high-impact individual contributor role for a systems-oriented finance professional who thrives in a SaaS and hybrid revenue environment. The Senior Financial Analyst operates independently across complex, multiproduct analysis, and plays a central role in forecasting, long-range planning, and financial systems optimization.

This role goes beyond reporting. It is about designing clear financial narratives, strengthening planning infrastructure, and ensuring our financial systems—particularly Workday Adaptive Planning and Acumatica—generate reliable, scalable insights that support executive decision-making. This role reports directly to the Director of Financial Planning & Analysis and collaborates closely with Product leadership and key stakeholders across Enterprise Operations, including the Office of the COO, Finance, Legal, and Work Life & Culture.

Responsibilities

Strategic financial partnership

  • Serve as the primary finance partner to senior product and functional leaders.
  • Maintain our cost allocation model and lead the analysis of cost impacts from our product and functional areas to our four business units (JSTOR, JSTOR Stewardship, Portico, and Ithaka S+R). Translate cost structure analysis into actionable insights.
  • Identify financial risks, structural margin drivers, and resource tradeoffs.
  • Support evaluation of new initiatives, pricing changes, and portfolio investments.

Forecasting & Planning

  • Lead regular and rolling forecasts for complex, multientity areas.
  • Lead preparation of monthly and quarterly financial review materials for executive leadership, including variance analysis and forward-looking risk assessment.
  • Contribute to long-range planning and scenario modeling.
  • Design and maintain our cost allocation model, which includes working with budget owners on updating allocation drivers, updating the data and explaining variances to business unit leaders.
  • Ensure assumptions are documented, defensible, and aligned across the portfolio.
  • Manage the non-payroll cost budget, and maintain software, cloud, and other purchase order details in the planning system to ensure an accurate forecast.
  • Manage the headcount and payroll budget and maintain open positions for accurate forecasting.

Systems & Infrastructure

  • Serve as a power user of Workday Adaptive Planning, ensuring models, versions, allocations, and reporting structures are clean and scalable.
  • Serve as a power user of Databricks and Tableau ensuring ongoing support and enhancement of the allocated product line financial results dashboards.
  • Partner closely with Accounting to ensure integrity of data flows from Acumatica (ERP) into Adaptive.
  • Improve data architecture and dimensional consistency across systems.
  • Identify opportunities to automate manual processes and improve forecasting accuracy.
  • Strengthen reporting governance and system documentation.
  • Ensure forecast integrity through rigorous assumption validation, reconciliation to actuals, and alignment with accounting standards.
  • Elevate reporting from static output to decision-support tools.

Process Improvement & Innovation

  • Identify and drive enhancements to forecasting workflows, allocation methodologies, and reporting structures.
  • Leverage AI, automation and analytical tools to improve efficiency and scalability.
  • Contribute to modernization of FP&A practices, including integration of new technologies and AI in current processes.

Experience and Skills

  • 7+ years of progressive FP&A or strategic finance experience
  • Advanced proficiency in Workday Adaptive Planning (model building, reporting, version control, allocations)
  • Strong working knowledge of Acumatica ERP and financial data structures
  • Experience in SaaS or hybrid subscription and services business models preferred
  • Advanced Google Suite, Microsoft 365, and BI capabilities (Power BI/Tableau)
  • Proven advanced financial modeling and scenario planning skills
  • Ability to synthesize complex financial information into clear executive-ready narratives
  • Strong cross-functional communication skills
  • Familiarity with automation, AI-assisted analysis, or advanced analytics tools a plus

Work Authorization and Sponsorship

ITHAKA is not currently considering candidates who require any type of immigration sponsorship (additional work authorization or permanent work authorization) to work in the United States.

Compensation and Benefits

At ITHAKA we believe in openness and fair pay. Part of living those values is our commitment to clarity about salary ranges, so candidates know what to expect. The starting salary for this position ranges from $76,320 - $95,400 per year. Starting pay may vary with job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. At present, our total compensation package for benefits-eligible employees includes medical, dental, and vision plans, an employer-paid 10% retirement contribution, paid parental and caregiver leave, 22 days of paid time off, 11 paid holidays, up to 12 sick days, wellness benefits, and more. Please note that ITHAKA, at its discretion, may make changes to its benefits programs from time to time.

Work for ITHAKA

We are committed to our organizational values of belonging, evidence, speed, teamwork, and trust. We take seriously the need for everyone to feel welcome. Belonging is one of our core values, and it shows in our vibrant culture. People from a wide range of backgrounds work at ITHAKA, and we believe that unique perspectives help us realize new insights and build better solutions.

We want to work with people who are passionate about ideas like these and who wish to contribute their perspectives and talents to ITHAKA’s mission. We enthusiastically welcome applications from people of all backgrounds and credentials. We want to hear your story and include your perspective in the transformative work we aim to do.

Learn more about Working at ITHAKA.

Apply Now

Although ITHAKA has physical offices in New York and Ann Arbor, Michigan, our employees are distributed across the continental United States. At this time, we’re not considering candidates who are unable to work and reside in the continental U.S.

Candidates may apply by submitting an application online through our career site, if you have any questions about your application, please contact us at . ITHAKA is committed to providing reasonable accommodations, if there’s anything we can do to accommodate any portion of the application or hiring process, please contact us at .

We are proud to be an Equal Opportunity employer. All qualified applicants receive consideration for employment without regard to identity or other status protected by law. We invite you to read our Equal Employment Opportunity Statement. ITHAKA cares about your privacy, learn more about our Applicant Privacy Notice.

Your car and your home are your most important assets, yet the experience of owning them is stuck in the 90s. Every part of the journey — buy/sell, insurance, maintenance, repairs — is fragmented, complicated, and expensive.

Jerry.ai is building the first app to manage it all. We started with car insurance in 2019, became one of the top 3 brokers in the U.S., then added driving insights, diagnostics, and a repair marketplace.

Why We’re Hiring

Our Data Science & Analytics team has been a force multiplier and accelerant to our business that has helped us reach these pivotal milestones in spite of headwinds and within a highly competitive market. They are a team of former McKinsey, BCG and Bain consultants who drive data & insights, and inform decision-making across every corner of our business. They are analytical powerhouses and first principles problem solvers who push forward our most important initiatives across product, growth, tech, and operations.

Every business unit has a Data Science team member embedded within it — someone who doesn't just run analyses and build dashboards, but shapes what questions we should ask, what data to pull, what conclusions to draw, what decisions to make, and then drives our teams towards our next goal: go from 5M to 50M customers and become a $10B business in the next 4 years.

As our business continues to expand, there is growing demand for more Data Science team members. We are hiring 2-3 people to drive impact in these areas:

  • Growth Marketing

  • Product Development

  • Strategic Partnerships

On leveling: You may see job ads for this role at different job levels. Our priority is finding the right people, we can be flexible with job title/leveling.

Why You Will (Or Won't) Like Working Here

  • No slides: If you've worked in consulting, you know what it feels like to be up at 3am reformatting a deck. That doesn't exist here. The only work that gets done at Jerry is work that will materially change the trajectory of our business — an important product, a new growth channel, a key metric, a critical partner relationship, etc.

  • No corporate fluff: The Data Science & Analytics team is 14 insatiable learners who care deeply about solving difficult problems and making a tangible impact. Every person owns a critical domain. There is no bloat, unnecessary meetings, or waiting for approvals.

  • Hands-on: This is not a pure strategy role, you will also own execution. Your day-to-day will be surfacing analytical insights, driving decisions, and seeing them through end-to-end.

What You'll Own

You'll sit on our central Data Science & Analytics team but you’ll be embedded in one of Jerry's core business areas — growth, product, AI and automation, strategic partnerships — and own the analytical function for that business unit end-to-end.

  • Define the right problems: Before any analysis, understand what business question it's answering and what decision it will inform. Push back if the question is flawed.

  • Data and insights: Define metrics, build reports, run analyses, design experiments, and surface data insights that move your team's key metrics.

  • Drive outcomes: Bring recommendations to your counterparts in product, growth, finance or operations, tell them what's happening and why, and what next steps should be.

Who You Are

  • First principles thinker: You break ambiguous problems into clear hypotheses before touching data. You're analytically strong (comfortable with SQL or Python) but your instinct is to ask "what are we trying to solve here?" before jumping to "what should I build?"

  • Direct communicator: You can walk a skeptical stakeholder through a complex finding and get buy-in quickly. You write clearly, speak precisely, and don't bury the lede.

  • Owner: You act like your name is on the door. If something is broken, you feel responsible for fixing it, even if it’s outside of your swim lane.

What You'll Bring

  • 2+ years of experience at a consulting firm, investment bank, or high-growth technology company.

  • Strong analytical skills; ability to pull, structure, and interpret data independently.

  • Track record of owning ambiguous problems and delivering impact.

  • Clear, persuasive communicator who can influence decisions at the leadership level.

SQL (Clickhouse), Metabase, Python, Jupyter Hub, GitHub.

Why We’re Hiring

Jerry is expanding into several new markets at the same time. Capital allocation is now one of the most consequential decisions we make: each dollar committed to a new product line, a marketing channel, or a headcount is a dollar not available elsewhere.

We are hiring a Strategic Finance Manager, reporting to our VP of Finance, to build the analysis those decisions rest on. You will own the operating model and the planning cycle, partner with functional leaders across the company, and work closely with the CFO and the founders.

What You’ll Own

The operating core is the model, the planning cadence, and the spend discipline the company runs on. Alongside it, you are the analytical partner on new opportunities — the products, verticals, channels and partnerships we are deciding whether to back. And over your first year or two, as our newer products scale and the audience for our numbers widens beyond the people who already know the business, the reporting itself has to reach a standard that holds up to outside diligence.

Own the operating model and forecast cycle:

  • Own Jerry’s driver-based operating model for the base business and expand it as we launch new insurance products and business lines.

  • Run the annual budget and long-range planning process end to end — cadence, assumptions, stakeholder inputs, and the consolidated plan the executive team commits to.

  • Own the monthly and quarterly forecast cycle and variance analysis: Once Accounting closes the books, explain what moved against plan and prior period, why it moved, and what it means for the forecast.

  • Write the executive narrative: Translate the financial results into clear business insights for the CFO, the founders, the board, and our investors, at a standard that survives external diligence.

  • Lead monthly business reviews: Work with functional leaders and turn what the numbers show into the business decisions that need to be made.

  • Support the team in evaluating and implementing a planning system: Assess the options, make the recommendation, and own the rollout.

Build the financial case for new opportunities

  • Build the financial model for new product, vertical, channel or partnership: Size the market, model the economics, evaluate capital commitment and return profile.

  • Read results back against the case: Once something is live, compare the actual economics to what we underwrote and carry the lesson into the next decision. Monitor product and channel economics including CAC and payback, policy retention and lifetime value, contribution margin etc.

  • Support corporate development: Capital markets and investor workstreams through diligence, modeling, and transaction analysis as the need arises.

  • Frame build, buy or partner decisions: help refine the frameworks we use to compare the options and the return profile of each.

Underwrite vendor spend:

  • Build the business case before a commitment is made, support negotiation on terms, and give budget owners the visibility to manage their own numbers.

  • Picks the right question: No one hands you the workstream. You decide which analysis will actually change a decision, and leave the rest alone.

  • Direct communicator: You form a view, communicate it directly, and revise it when the evidence changes.

  • Executive-ready output: What you produce can go in front of the founders or the board without a rewrite — clear, precise, and honest about what the numbers do and do not show.

  • Owner: You take ownership of outcomes and are comfortable building process where none exists yet.

jobs.title: Strategic Project Manager
jobs.excerpt: Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous!
jobs.description:
Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous!

Our agentic platform helps finance and operations teams worldwide remove manual work from their core business processes, so work runs end-to-end with greater control and significant productivity gains.

Today, over 550 enterprise customers use BLP across 1,300+ deployed projects. In the processes we automate, customers achieve productivity improvements of 5 to 10 times.

To date, BLP remains majority employee-owned, with Goldman Sachs holding a minority stake as a growth investor. Our success is driven by deep expertise in technology and business processes, a superior product with strong product-market fit, reflected in an expanding customer base that includes Fortune 500 companies.

BLP is one of Switzerland's fastest-growing SaaS scale-ups; we are now entering our next phase of growth. From our headquarters on Zürich's Bahnhofstrasse, we're expanding globally, with a growing presence across Europe and North America.

Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard.

Location

This is a full-time position based in Munich or Cologne. Following a comprehensive onboarding period at our HQ in central Zurich (minimum one month), you will work from your home location, with regular visits to customers across the DACH region.

Team collaboration matters a lot to us. You will regularly spend time with the team in person, in Zurich and at our hubs, for team days, all-hands and offsites. These visits are financially supported by blp.

Your Mission

You get customers live. Hands on, end to end, and fast.

As a Senior Project Manager, you make large, global blp transformations happen. These programs touch finance, procurement and supply chain at once, run across multiple ERP systems and legal entities, and roll out country by country. Your job is to orchestrate all of it and get the customer live: the first go-live above all, because that is where credibility is won or lost, and then wave after wave with the same discipline. You run the steering committee, you lead a blp team on each engagement, and you do that across several engagements at once.

At both levels, scope is the single biggest lever on whether a project goes live on time. Protecting it is a daily job, not a contract clause. You escalate early and precisely rather than absorbing problems until they become critical.

You will not be alone with the technical side. Integrations Engineers handle the connection into the ERP, Technical Project Managers handle the harder solution design, and our Consultants take over the automation work after go-live. On our largest strategic accounts a Client Partner carries the relationship and the commercial number, so your attention goes to delivery quality.

We have done this many times, so you are not inventing the approach each time. A proven onboarding method and a strong toolkit are what let you carry your own customers from early on.

Your Career Path in Project Management

This is the path most of our delivery leadership came through, and we hire at every step of it. We place you according to your experience and the size of the programs you have delivered, and we are explicit about what the next step requires.

  • Project Manager: You get customers live end to end, several in parallel: guided onboarding for commercial customers, leading enterprise projects yourself, or a workstream on our largest programs. Typically you bring 2+ years in consulting, implementation or project management.

  • Senior Project Manager: You make large, global transformations happen: multiple ERPs, entities and countries, the steering committee, and a blp team on each engagement. Typically you bring 5+ years delivering complex, multi-country programs.

  • Next steps: Lead a delivery team, or move into Consulting and from there towards our Client Partner role on strategic accounts.

Moves into Consulting or Customer Success Engineering are open at every level, and many of our people make them.

Key Responsibilities

  • Run implementations end to end: kick-off, scope, planning, configuration, testing and go-live.

  • Manage several customers in parallel at different stages, and keep every one of them on date.

  • Work with customers on their processes, and flag early where a process assumption will not hold.

  • Coordinate the specialists on your projects: Integrations Engineers, Technical Project Managers and AI Automation Specialists.

  • Own scope actively. Recognize a change request for what it is and handle it deliberately.

  • Keep the project inside its budget, and raise it early when the effort is drifting.

  • Hand over cleanly at go-live to our Consultants and support organization.

In addition, as a Senior Project Manager

  • Own the delivery outcome of global programs from kick-off to the last go-live: plan, scope, dependencies and date.

  • Drive the first go-live relentlessly, then run wave planning across ERPs, entities and countries.

  • Run the steering committee and own the decisions that come out of it.

  • Write and execute the recovery plan when a program is off track.

  • Lead the blp team on each engagement and coach the Project Managers working on your programs.

What We're Really Looking For

The following key attributes ensure success in this role:

  • Scope Discipline – You notice when a project is quietly growing, and you raise it rather than absorbing it.

  • Ownership & Autonomy – You take initiative, move things forward, and deliver end to end without being chased.

  • Escalation Judgment – You escalate early, to the right person, with a proposal rather than a problem.

  • Client Confidence – You are comfortable running a meeting with a customer's finance or IT lead in it.

  • Four-Language Fluency – Technology, process, data and people. You speak each well enough to spot where a roadblock really sits.

  • Structured Under Pressure – When a project goes sideways you get sharper and more organized, not louder.

What You Bring

  • 6 + years of experience delivering complex projects: management consulting, enterprise software implementation, or large-scale transformation delivery.

  • Proven track record running multi-country or multi-entity programs with senior client stakeholders, and steering a committee that includes client executives.

  • Experience leading a delivery team rather than only a plan.

  • Strong analytical and communication skills. You can translate a business need into something a technical team can act on.

  • Fluent in German and English, spoken and written.

  • Bonus points for ERP implementation experience, finance or supply chain processes, or AI-driven SaaS.

Benefits

  • High ownership environment – you shape your projects, outcomes, and career path.

  • Impact at scale – your work powers automation across global enterprises.

  • Cross-functional exposure – work with engineers, data scientists, and business leaders daily.

  • Real growth – fast-paced environment, steep learning curve, and structured career progression.

  • Employee ownership – be part of a majority employee-owned company with a best-in-class stock option program.

  • Amazing team – become part of a driven and collaborative group of innovators.

  • Technology exposure – be at the forefront of AI and enjoy continuous learning opportunities.

  • Visits & offsites – paid visits and stays at our HQ in Zurich, including collaborative team offsites.

Ready to build the future of ERP automation? Join us and own your impact.

Learn more about blp and our values at .

  • Develop and execute Computer System Validation (CSV) protocols for Emerson DeltaV automation systems.
  • Draft detailed test scripts to validate DeltaV batch recipes, automation sequences, control logic, and system configurations.

  • Verify DeltaV batch recipes, including unit procedures, operations, phases, and recipe parameters.
  • Develop test scenarios to verify automation control logic, interlocks, permissives, alarms, setpoints, and process sequences.
  • Perform positive and negative testing to ensure automation systems function according to approved specifications.

We’re hiring a Physician Liaison to own the ground game: getting into pediatric practices across the market, earning the trust of the physicians and the front desk, and turning that into referrals.

You’ll work a target list of pediatric practices, get past the door, get in front of the physician, and give them a reason to send us their next patient with anxiety, ADHD, or obesity.

We have a strong playbook from California and you’ll get it on day one. Clinical presentations with our own physicians activate new providers better than almost anything else we do. Layering touches inside a tight window is what makes a clinic activate. Expect the playbook to change as we learn Texas. The target list, the pitch, and the sequence will all move, and we want someone who treats that as normal and tells us straight what they are seeing in the field.

You’ll report to our Head of GTM today, and to our Growth General Manager once that role is in seat.

What success looks like in year one:

  • 200 referring clinics across Dallas–Fort Worth, actively sending patients

  • Hundreds of individual referring providers inside those clinics

  • Referral volume growing quarter over quarter across your territory

  • Relationships stable enough that a clinic keeps referring when you’re not standing in the lobby

What you’ll own

  • Activate new clinics Work a target list across Dallas and Fort Worth. Prospect cold, get past the front desk, book the meeting, and turn practices into referring partners. Run the territory like it’s your own book of business.

  • Run in-services Get in front of a whole practice, physicians and staff together, and teach them what Clarity treats, who to send, and how to send them. You deliver these yourself.

  • Grow the clinics you win The first referral is the start of the account. Build relationships with physicians, medical assistants, office managers, and referral coordinators until Clarity is the default place they send these patients.

  • Set up clinical presentations Find the practices worth a physician-led presentation, get them scheduled, and get our medical advisors and clinicians in the room. You build the opportunity, they deliver the content.

  • Document your work Log every account, contact, visit, and outcome in the CRM the same day it happens, following our field team’s conventions. Keep account records current, including who the referring providers are, where each practice stands, and what the next step is. Your records are how we decide where to spend the next dollar and the next rep, so they need to be complete and accurate rather than close enough.

  • Bring the market back to the team You’ll have a better read than anyone here on what lands with a Texas pediatrician. Bring it back on a regular cadence: what’s working, what objections you’re hearing, which materials fall flat, and what we should change. In a new market, why a clinic said no is worth as much to us as the ones that said yes.

What we’re looking for

  • 2+ years in healthcare sales or provider relations You’ve called on physician practices and grown referrals. Pediatrics or behavioral health is a plus. A track record of hitting or beating a number is what we will look for first.

  • A clinical background is a real advantage If you are a nurse, an MA, or came up on the care delivery side and moved into sales, you will be more credible in these rooms and we will weight that heavily.

  • You work fast and you carry a lot at once You’d rather get through twenty practices than perfect one. Hearing no all week doesn’t wear you down.

  • You can walk into a room cold The front desk is the hardest door in this job. It is a learnable skill, but you have to want to do it.

  • You can present to a full practice In-services mean standing in front of a room of physicians and staff and holding their attention for fifteen minutes.

  • You’re disciplined about documentation You keep a CRM current without being asked, and you’ve worked in Salesforce, Zoho, or something like them.

  • You learn fast and take coaching We’ll teach you the clinical material and the playbook. You need to pick it up quickly, run it the way we ask, and tell us where it breaks.

  • Based in Dallas–Fort Worth Valid driver’s license, clean driving record, and reliable transportation. You’ll be driving the metroplex every day, with one to three trips a year to the SF Bay Area for onboarding and team on-sites.

Compensation, equity & location

  • Total on-target earnings of $112,000 to $128,000, made up of:

  • Base salary of $70,000 to 80,000

  • On-target variable compensation of $42,000 to $48,000 tied to referral growth in your territory. Variable is paid quarterly, and pay is set individually based on track record; there is no cap on the variable compensation

  • Guaranteed variable payout in your first full quarter while you ramp and build the territory

  • Equity in an early-stage, well-funded company

  • Mileage reimbursed at the IRS standard rate

  • Medical, dental, vision, and ancillary benefits, plus 401(k)

  • Paid holidays and flexible PTO

  • Full-time W-2, based in Dallas–Fort Worth, four to five days per week in the field

  • Reports to our Growth General Manager

  • Candidates must be authorized to work in the US without the need for company sponsorship

jobs.excerpt: About MenloMenlo Research is an Applied R&D lab building Asimov, an open-source humanoid robot platform, and the full software stack that powers it.
jobs.description:
About Menlo

Menlo Research is an Applied R&D lab building Asimov, an open-source humanoid robot platform, and the full software stack that powers it. Our mission is to make humanoid labor economically viable, turning software into physical labor at scale. We build across the full stack: hardware architecture, locomotion, autonomy, simulation, and infrastructure. We move fast, ship to real robots, and open-source everything we can. If you want your work to matter beyond a paper or a demo, this is the place.

The Role

We are looking for a Researcher, Locomotion to push Asimov from walking to running, recovering, and moving through the real world with the confidence of something alive. Asimov 0 was built to learn locomotion and Asimov 1 to learn whole-body control, and you will own the policies that make that motion robust on real hardware. You will not stop at a clip in simulation. You will get your work onto a physical biped and keep pushing until it holds up under contact, disturbance, and terrain we did not train for.

What You'll Do

  • Design, train, and ship reinforcement learning policies for bipedal and whole-body locomotion on Asimov

  • Own the sim2real pipeline end to end, building on our zero-shot sim2real work so a first run on hardware is never really a first run

  • Push balance, gait, and recovery behavior past the demo stage into something that survives pushes, slips, and uneven ground

  • Build and refine reward design, domain randomization, and training environments in MuJoCo

  • Close the loop between simulation and hardware with real telemetry from real robots, then feed what breaks back into the next policy

  • Work shoulder to shoulder with hardware, controls, and manipulation researchers, since whole-body control does not respect team boundaries

  • Open-source what you can and write up what you learn so the community can build on it

What We Look For

  • Deep hands-on experience with reinforcement learning for continuous control, legged locomotion, or whole-body control

  • A track record of getting learned policies onto real robots, not only into papers or simulators

  • Strong command of a physics simulator such as MuJoCo, Isaac, or similar, including reward shaping and domain randomization

  • Fluency in Python and modern RL tooling, and comfort in a ROS2-based control stack

  • A bias for shipping: you would rather see a policy stumble on real hardware this week than look perfect in sim next month

  • Clear thinking about why a policy fails, not just whether it does

Nice to Have

  • Published work in locomotion, legged robotics, or sim2real transfer

  • Experience with model predictive control or classical locomotion methods alongside learning-based approaches

  • Contributions to open-source robotics or RL projects

  • Experience bringing up new hardware and debugging the messy gap between a model and a motor

Why Join Menlo

You will own locomotion for a humanoid that thousands of developers are building on in the open. Your policies will ship to real robots, not slides, and the community will see them walk. If you want your research to leave the lab and stand up on its own two feet, this is the place.

A Note on AI

You don't need deep AI expertise for every role, but we do expect everyone at Menlo to be intellectually curious, drawn to tinkering and discovery, and excited to use AI as a real collaborator in their work. For some roles, AI fluency is a core requirement. When that's the case, we'll say so explicitly in the qualifications. People who thrive here don't treat AI as a novelty. They use it to think better, and make their work easier for others to build on.

Equal Opportunity and Accommodations

We hire talented people from a wide range of backgrounds. If you're excited about a role but don't meet every bullet, we still encourage you to apply. Menlo Research is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of any legally protected characteristic. Menlo provides reasonable accommodations during the application process. If you need one, please let your recruiter know.

micro1 is engaging Enrolled Agents and CPAs who actively prepare individual returns to participate in a project supporting a customer. Scope of Work

  1. Prepare complete federal individual returns (Form 1040) from scratch under TY2025 rules, working through the worksheets, phase-outs, limitations, and carryovers by hand.
  2. Write clear, concise preparer notes explaining how each figure on the return was derived, so that every number can be traced and reproduced.
  3. Build realistic, self-contained tax scenarios involving complex returns, including self-employment, partnership and S-corporation K-1s, investments, and credits, specifying facts, dates, filing status, and expected results.
  4. Review and evaluate AI-generated returns and computations for accuracy and completeness, flagging errors by severity (critical, secondary, minor).

  6. Experts and Adjudicators: strengthen and audit scenarios and reviews, and resolve disputed outcomes (see levels below).

Required Qualifications (all levels)

  1. Active EA or CPA who currently prepares individual (1040) returns.
  2. 3+ tax seasons on complex returns (Schedule C, K-1s, investments, credits), not mainly W-2 returns.
  3. Fluency in TY2025 rules.
  4. Ability to compute a full return by hand (worksheets, phase-outs, carryovers) and explain each number in clear written notes.
  5. Strong written communication, with an emphasis on clarity, objectivity, and reproducibility.

Levels

  1. Contributor: Meets the required qualifications above.
  2. Expert: 5+ tax seasons. Able to audit and strengthen scenarios, making a task harder without making it vague. Trainer, reviewer, or QC background preferred. A careful, independent preparer who builds the return from scratch.

Jerry is expanding into several new markets at the same time. Capital allocation is now one of the most consequential decisions we make: each dollar committed to a new product line, a marketing channel, or a headcount is a dollar not available elsewhere.

We are hiring a Strategic Finance Manager, reporting to our VP of Finance, to build the analysis those decisions rest on. You will own the operating model and the planning cycle, partner with functional leaders across the company, and work closely with the CFO and the founders.

What You’ll Own

The operating core is the model, the planning cadence, and the spend discipline the company runs on. Claroty is a global leader in cyber-physical systems (CPS) protection, dedicated to securing the critical infrastructure that keeps the world running. We’re a fast-growing, award-winning team where innovation meets purpose—and we want you to help us define the future of cybersecurity.

About the Role:

As a Technical Account Manager (TAM), you will serve as a strategic technical partner to our enterprise customers, ensuring successful deployment, adoption, and ongoing value realization from Claroty’s platform. You will bridge the gap between customers and internal teams, driving technical alignment, proactive optimization, and long-term relationship success. This is a high-impact, customer-facing role ideal for a strong networking professional who thrives at the intersection of technology, strategy, and customer engagement.

  • Partner with customers to plan, design, deploy, and configure Claroty’s solutions to meet their technical and business objectives while driving measurable value.
  • Serve as the primary technical point of contact for customers, owning all technical requirements and ensuring alignment with best practices.
  • Provide ongoing technical guidance, architecture recommendations, and optimization strategies to maximize product adoption and performance.
  • Proactively identify risks, gaps, and opportunities for improvement across customer environments.
  • Translate customer feedback, industry trends, and field insights into actionable recommendations for Product, Engineering, and Customer Success teams.
  • Develop technical artifacts, documentation, playbooks, and best practices to streamline deployments and enhance service delivery.
  • Support escalations and complex technical scenarios in partnership with Support and R&D teams.
  • Drive executive-level technical conversations and present strategic roadmaps aligned with customers’ cybersecurity and operational objectives.
  • Travel up to 30% to support on-site engagements, workshops, and strategic meetings.

Requirements

What you need to succeed in this role:

  • 3-5 years of experience in Professional Services, Technical Account Management, Network Engineering, or similar customer-facing technical roles.
  • Deep knowledge of IT networking; prior experience as a Network Architect is highly beneficial.
  • Strong understanding of networking standards and protocols, including TCP/IP, routing, switching, DNS, DHCP, and segmentation principles.
  • Experience with Operational Technology (OT) environments and industrial networks – a strong advantage.
  • Solid understanding of cybersecurity principles and secure network architecture.

About Claroty

Claroty empowers organizations to protect the mission-critical infrastructure that underpins modern life. The AI-powered Claroty Platform serves as the single source of operational truth, providing the deepest visibility and broadest protection across cyber-physical systems (CPS), leveraging five core solutions: asset inventory, exposure management, network protection, secure access, and threat detection. Claroty helps organizations operationalize CPS protection through a programmatic approach designed to reduce risk, maintain operational integrity, and meet compliance–whether in the cloud with Claroty xDome or on-premise with Claroty Continuous Threat Detection (CTD). Claroty is deployed by hundreds of organizations at thousands of sites globally. The company is headquartered in New York City and has a presence in Europe, Asia-Pacific, and Latin America. To learn more, visit.

Claroty is widely recognized as the industry leader in CPS protection, backed by the world’s largest investment firms and industrial automation vendors. About Menlo
Menlo Research is an Applied R&D lab building Asimov, an open-source humanoid robot platform, and the full software stack that powers it. Our mission is to make humanoid labor economically viable, turning software into physical labor at scale. We build across the full stack: hardware architecture, locomotion, autonomy, simulation, and infrastructure. We move fast, ship to real robots, and open-source everything we can. If you want your work to matter beyond a paper or a demo, this is the place.

The Role
We are hiring a Designer to own how Menlo looks and feels across our website, our communications, and everything in between. Menlo builds in public, and the brand is a big part of why people love Asimov. Every launch, research post, careers page, and community moment is a chance to show the world what we are building. We want one designer who can own that whole surface, from the marketing site to the social asset that goes out an hour before a demo.
This is a broad, hands-on design role for someone who moves fast and has real range. You will shape the brand system, design the pages, and turn around the comms assets, all while keeping Menlo and Asimov looking sharp and consistent.
If you want to own the look of a company people are already watching, this is it.

What You'll Do

  • Own the visual design of and its surfaces, from marketing and launch pages to the careers page and shop touchpoints, working with engineering to ship them to production

  • Design communications assets across every launch, including social posts, announcement art, research post graphics, video thumbnails, and event and IRL collateral

  • Build and maintain the Menlo brand system, including typography, color, and reusable components and templates, so the whole team can move fast and stay on brand

  • Keep Menlo and Asimov visually consistent across the website, docs, community channels, and partner materials

  • Design decks, one-pagers, and collateral for sales, partnerships, and hiring

  • Design for the build in public motion across Discord, the forum, streams, and community moments

  • Turn rough ideas into finished work quickly, often on launch-day timelines

What We Look For

  • A strong portfolio that spans brand, web, and communications design, not just one of the three

  • Real range, from setting up a brand system to designing a marketing site to shipping fast-turn social assets

  • Comfort owning brand at an early company, where you set the bar rather than inherit it

  • Fluency in Figma and a sharp eye for layout, type, and detail

  • Web design sensibility, including responsive thinking and a smooth handoff or collaboration with engineers

  • Taste for a technical, developer-facing aesthetic that feels clean and confident, never corporate

  • Self-direction and speed, with a bias for shipping

Nice to Have

  • Front-end skills such as HTML, CSS, Tailwind, or React and Next.js, enough to ship your own designs to production

  • Motion design or video editing for launches and social

  • Illustration or 3D skills, such as Blender, for robots and hardware

  • Photography or art direction for product and team shoots

  • Experience at a hardware, robotics, developer tools, or open source brand

Why Join Menlo
Your work will be the first thing the world sees of Menlo. You will own how the brand shows up across the website, our launches, and the community, with the freedom to set the bar rather than follow a template. The range is real: one day a brand system, the next a launch page, the next the asset that ships minutes before a demo. If you want to shape how a company people already watch looks and feels, this is where it happens.

A Note on AI

You don't need deep AI expertise for every role, but we do expect everyone at Menlo to be intellectually curious, drawn to tinkering and discovery, and excited to use AI as a real collaborator in their work. For some roles, AI fluency is a core requirement. When that's the case, we'll say so explicitly in the qualifications. People who thrive here don't treat AI as a novelty. They use it to think better, and make their work easier for others to build on.

Equal Opportunity and Accommodations

We hire talented people from a wide range of backgrounds. If you're excited about a role but don't meet every bullet, we still encourage you to apply. jobs.description:
The PCB Design Specialist designs and develops complex detailed layouts of printed circuit boards. Collaborates in developing state-of-the-art designs of new or modified, RF printed circuit boards. Establishes design standards and configurations. Works from preliminary schematics, part lists and basic description of the board function, configuration and arrangement as defined by engineering. May perform the checking of design layouts and detailed drawings. This position is remote. Legal authorization to work in the US is required.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Create PCB/PCBA design using Altium software with input from both mechanical and electrical
  • Create schematics and modify as directed by engineers.
  • Able to create library symbols/ footprint/3D drawing for component used
  • Study PCB design trends and processes and then evaluate and implement those processes that apply to Ezurio.
  • Conduct design feasibility studies to evaluate the PCB design goals for packaging, cost, manufacturing, and system performance.
  • Perform complex and difficult CAD and CAE tasks requiring extensive skill and knowledge of equipment capabilities, applications techniques and design limitations.
  • Ensure PCBs are designed to observe the principle of design for test (DFT) and design for manufacturability (DFM).
  • Propose PCB design trade-offs to the engineering design team for resolution and implementation.
  • Communicate with fabrication vendors for quotations and purchase requisitions also responsible to engineering questions (EQ) from PCB fabricators.
  • Understands the requirements for a quality design and strives to achieve the requirements before releasing the product to manufacturing.
  • Understands the impedance control requirement of the different electrical bus interfaces and RF circuits, familiar with the basic rule of thumb to achieve SI (Signal Integrity) during the routing.
  • Understands the driving of PCB technology and process trends and their application to Ezurio's designs.
  • Coordinate with Engineering, Test, Quality, and Manufacturing during the PCB design and fabrication process.
  • Resolve PCB design issues with fabrication and manufacturing vendors.
  • Participate and provide input into the PCB design specifications and standards with respect to product design, electrical design, manufacturing and various regulatory agency requirements to determine design trade-offs necessary to meet design goals and produce high quality PCB's at the lowest cost and within schedule.

REQUIREMENTS

  • Demonstrate proficient hands-on use of Altium Designer for PCB layout, library management, and PCB design release. Experience with Cadence or Mentor PCB design tools is a plus.
  • Ability of using Mechanical CAD tools like Solidwork/AutoCad is preferred.
  • Must demonstrate an ability to read schematics
  • Proficient working knowledge of PCB design best practices and applicable IPC standards, including IPC-2221, IPC-7351, IPC-A-600, and IPC-6012. Knowledge of IPC-A-610 is also preferred.
  • Demonstrated strong and effective verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills

EDUCATION/EXPERIENCE

  • Bachelors or Technical Degree and a minimum of 5 years related experience required
  • Experience in RF Circuit PCB design is preferred

Darkroom is the leading next-generation growth marketing firm engineering the brands of tomorrow. Founded in 2017, we set out to redefine what a modern agency could be, by replacing the inertia of legacy advertising behemoths with a model built for speed, intelligence, and measurable impact.

Every engagement feeds into our proprietary data infrastructure, enabling a continuous feedback loop that accelerates growth, improves margins, and compounds results across our client portfolio.

What began as a boutique design studio has evolved into one of the fastest-growing private companies in America (Inc. 5000) and among the most effective performance media agencies of the 2020s (Varos). Our founders were recognized by Forbes 30 Under 30 for advancing the intersection of technology, marketing, and advertising, cementing Darkroom’s role as a defining player in the future of media innovation.

About the role

We are looking for a deeply technical Senior Retention Specialist to own the CRM build for a high-growth consumer technology client. You will architect and implement the flows and automations that carry the program, own the segmentation logic behind them, and hold the channel KPIs that determine whether any of it lands in the inbox.

You are standing this program up from the ground, not inheriting it. The list starts near 20,000 and scales rapidly behind a significant acquisition investment — which puts real pressure on deliverability, list hygiene, and data hygiene from day one. Volume ramps to 40–60 emails a month, and increasingly granular segmentation is what generates that output. Automation is the core of the program: lead capture, welcome series, and the first-conversion funnel first, then subscription activation, loyalty, repeat purchase, and win-back. You will work in an enterprise-grade platform — Braze, Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Iterable, , or comparable.

You are the person who knows the platform better than anyone else on the team. When something does not fire, does not render, or does not deliver, you find out why.

Working hours: PST (mandatory). This role includes monthly travel to San Francisco.

You should apply if this sounds like you

You are hands-on in the ESP every day and you like it there. You enjoy building a journey with real conditional logic, and you get genuine satisfaction from tracking down why one segment stopped converting.

  • 3–5+ years of hands-on lifecycle, CRM, or email marketing execution, with deep expertise in at least one enterprise-grade ESP — Braze, Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Iterable, , or comparable.

  • You have built complex, event-triggered journeys from scratch: multi-branch logic, wait steps, conditional splits, holdouts, and cross-channel orchestration across email, SMS, push, and in-app.

  • You are fluent in advanced segmentation — behavioral and product-event based, computed attributes, dynamic and personalized content — and you have scaled a program where segmentation drove a real increase in send volume.

  • You have built the funnel that matters here: lead capture forms and opt-in logic, welcome series, first-conversion sequences, and subscription activation journeys.

  • You have implemented loyalty, rewards, and win-back programs, and you treat driving repeat purchase and long-term value as a core outcome rather than a nice-to-have.

  • You own deliverability as a discipline: domain warming and authentication (SPF, DKIM, DMARC, BIMI), sending reputation, list hygiene, sunset policies, and what to do when a list grows very fast.

  • You own the channel KPIs — open, click, click-to-open, conversion, deliverability, bounce, spam complaints, unsubscribe — and you can diagnose a drop in any of them.

  • You are comfortable with HTML and CSS for email, and you know how to build templates and modules that render correctly across clients. Liquid, Handlebars, AMPscript, or a similar templating language is a strong plus.

  • You understand data flows into the ESP: API-based events, webhooks, ETL or CDP integrations, and product event streams. You can hold a technical conversation with a client's engineering team.

  • You are a systematic troubleshooter — you isolate variables, you check the data before the theory, and you document what you find.

  • You design and execute proper tests: A/B and multivariate, with honest reads on significance.

  • Excellent written communication and the ability to explain a technical problem to a non-technical audience clearly and without condescension.

A day in the life

  • Build and QA the flows, automations, and campaigns that run your client's program — from lead capture and welcome through activation, loyalty, repeat purchase, and win-back.

  • Implement the segmentation and audience logic behind the calendar, and build the dynamic content that makes personalization work at volume.

  • Own the technical setup and health of the client's ESP instance: integrations, data feeds, event tracking, templates, and modules.

  • Monitor and own channel performance and deliverability, escalating and fixing issues before they affect the program.

  • Troubleshoot anything that misfires — a flow that does not trigger, a segment that under-populates, a template that breaks in Outlook — and document the fix.

  • QA every build end to end before launch: logic, rendering, links, personalization, suppression.

  • Design and run the testing roadmap with your Associate Director, and report results honestly.

  • Partner with the Copy & Content Specialist to get copy and creative into the build accurately and on schedule.

  • Build and maintain the reporting your Associate Director needs for client KPI reviews.

What It's Like to Work at Darkroom

Darkroom is not a typical agency. We are looking for A players who want to build something great. We move fast, think deeply, and expect every team member to bring insight and rigor to everything they touch. We hold a high bar for performance, creativity, and ownership — but we also support each other relentlessly. No egos, no red tape — just world-class talent building something remarkable.

We believe in autonomy with accountability, truth over comfort, and outcomes over optics.

  • Unlimited PTO + US holidays: Rebooting is part of the work. Take the time you need to stay sharp.

  • Remote-First Culture: Many roles are fully remote. Employees based in or near our New York or Lisbon HQs are expected to work hybrid with weekly in-office time. Hub locations include the Brazil and Spain.

  • Health & Wellness: Company-sponsored medical, dental, and vision coverage.

  • Finances, growth, and retirement: Darkroom offers a robust 401(k) program with company match and profit-sharing opportunities to help you save and grow as the company grows.

  • Parental Leave: Flexible parental leave to support new parents during this important transition.

  • Growth: Our interdisciplinary model gives every Darkroomer exposure far beyond their core role. Grow your skills, expand your influence, and stay at the forefront of the industry.

  • Compensation: The base salary range for this role is $60,000-$80,000 per year. This range represents the anticipated minimum and maximum for this position and applies to candidates based in New York, including New York City, in compliance with the New York State Pay Transparency Law and the New York City Salary Transparency Law. Actual compensation within this range will be determined based on experience, skills, and qualifications.

Equal Opportunity Statement

Darkroom is an equal opportunity workplace - we are dedicated to equal employment opportunities regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national orientation, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity, or Veteran status. We also consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with legal requirements.

Coupa makes margins multiply through its community-generated AI and industry-leading total spend management platform for businesses large and small. Coupa AI is informed by trillions of dollars of direct and indirect spend data across a global network of 10M+ buyers and suppliers. We empower you with the ability to predict, prescribe, and automate smarter, more profitable business decisions to improve operating margins.

Why join Coupa?

  • Pioneering Technology: At Coupa, we're at the forefront of innovation, leveraging the latest technology to empower our customers with greater efficiency and visibility in their spend.
  • Collaborative Culture: We value collaboration and teamwork, and our culture is driven by transparency, openness, and a shared commitment to excellence.
  • Global Impact: Join a company where your work has a global, measurable impact on our clients, the business, and each other.
Learn more on Life at Coupa blog and hear from our employees about their experiences working at Coupa.

The Impact of a Sr Security Engineer at Coupa:

Coupa's Security Engineers keep our enterprise, product, platform, and customer data safe. As a Senior Security Engineer, you'll take ownership of complex, ambiguous security problems end to end — building cloud security controls, setting engineering standards, and partnering closely with Engineering, IT, and Compliance to ship durable, automated security tooling rather than one-off fixes. You'll set the technical standard for how the team remediates and automates, and you'll be a go-to resource other engineers turn to when a finding needs real root-cause analysis instead of a quick workaround.

What You'll Do:

  • Design and implement multi-cloud security controls across Coupa's cloud environment, including VPC segmentation, security groups/NACLs, IAM policy design using least-privilege and permission boundaries, and Organizations/SCPs for guardrails at scale.
  • Build policy as code and IaC security guardrails and wire them into CI/CD as pre-merge and pre-deploy gates rather than after-the-fact reviews.
  • Harden containerized workloads and Kubernetes clusters — image scanning, admission control, pod security standards, network policies, and container/workload runtime detection.
  • Own vulnerability analysis of application packages, container images, and third-party dependencies; triage findings by exploitability and business impact rather than CVSS score alone.
  • Design and implement remediations (not just report findings) including secure code fixes, cloud configuration changes, and IAM policy adjustments using least-privilege principles.
  • Support incident response and forensics as a technical contributor — log analysis, root-cause investigation, and remediation validation using cloud-native and EDR tooling.
  • Partner with the Risk & Compliance team to provide technical evidence and control validation for audit frameworks (SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI-DSS, FedRAMP).
  • Support and mentor other security engineers — reviewing designs and remediation plans, sharing root-cause analysis techniques, and helping less experienced teammates work through complex or ambiguous findings.
  • Participate in the on-call/incident rotation and help continuously improve remediation and response runbooks.

What You Will Bring to Coupa:

  • 5+ years of experience in security engineering or cloud operations, with a track record of independently owning complex assessments from scoping through remediation.
  • Practical experience with cloud security fundamentals (AWS, GCP, or Azure) — IAM, networking, and common misconfiguration classes — sufficient to both find and fix cloud findings.
  • Strong scripting/automation skills in Python, Bash, or JavaScript, with experience building or extending internal security tooling.
  • Experience with dependency/container vulnerability scanning tools and integrating them into CI/CD pipelines.
  • Working knowledge of common compliance frameworks (SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI-DSS, FedRAMP) and what auditable evidence looks like.
  • Critical thinking and root-cause analysis skills — comfortable digging past a scanner's output to understand and explain why a vulnerability exists.
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills for translating technical findings into remediation guidance for engineers and risk context for stakeholders.
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Relevant certifications a plus: CISSP, CCSP, CISA, or AWS/GCP security certifications.

About the Role

Together AI runs one of the largest GPU fleets in the world. The Infra Agent Systems team builds the software systems that power and automate that infrastructure.

We develop production AI agents that diagnose hardware failures, investigate incidents, correlate signals across the fleet, and automate operational workflows. Alongside these agents, we build the platform they run on, including knowledge graphs, retrieval systems, orchestration frameworks, and developer tooling.

You’ll work across two areas:

Infrastructure Agent Systems — Build production AI agents that help operate our GPU fleet by diagnosing failures, investigating incidents, gathering evidence from live systems, and assisting with remediation. These agents are used every day by our infrastructure and datacenter teams through APIs, CLI, dashboards, and Slack.

Core Agent Platform — Build the platform that powers these agents, including knowledge graphs, search and retrieval, orchestration, evaluation, and the tooling that enables agents to reason, act, and continuously improve.

We’re working on something that hasn’t really been done before: building knowledge graphs and self-improving AI agents that understand, operate, and continuously improve large-scale AI infrastructure.

This is an opportunity to work at the intersection of AI agents, distributed systems, infrastructure, and automation, solving challenging engineering problems with real production impact. There’s an enormous amount to build, learn, and shape as we define the future of autonomous infrastructure.

responsible for delivering the software but also for operating and supporting it in production.

Why this Role

You’ll work on two hard problems at the same time: making AI agents trustworthy enough to operate production infrastructure, and building the knowledge, retrieval, and distributed systems that make those agents effective.

You’ll have the opportunity to build foundational systems from the ground up, work on infrastructure at massive scale, and help define how self-improving AI agents operate real-world AI infrastructure.

Remote based in India


Responsibilities

  • Design and build production AI agent systems that diagnose, investigate, and remediate infrastructure issues across one of the world’s largest GPU fleets.
  • Build the distributed services, orchestration framework, knowledge graph, and retrieval systems that power infrastructure agents.
  • Develop fleet intelligence systems that combine telemetry, infrastructure state, operational knowledge, and historical incidents to help agents make better decisions.
  • Integrate with observability, incident management, ticketing, fleet inventory, source control, chat, and internal infrastructure systems through well-designed APIs.
  • Own services end to end, including architecture, implementation, testing, deployment, observability, and production operations.
  • Improve agent performance through evaluations, retrieval improvements, better tools, and production feedback loops.
  • Turn what agents learn in production into reliable, reviewed software and automation.

Requirements

  • 5+ years of experience building production backend systems, distributed systems, or infrastructure platforms.
  • Strong systems design skills and experience owning significant systems from design through production.
  • Depth in at least one of the following:
    • AI agent systems, orchestration, tool use, evaluation, or grounding
    • Knowledge graphs or graph data modeling
    • Search, retrieval, ranking, RAG, or semantic search systems
  • Strong backend engineering experience, including API design, service boundaries, data modeling, and integrations across complex systems.
  • Experience with Kubernetes, GitOps such as ArgoCD, infrastructure-as-code, and cloud platforms.
  • Comfortable working across languages such as Go, TypeScript, Python, or Rust.

Experience in the following is a plus:

  • GPU infrastructure, datacenters, bare-metal systems, hardware failure modes, BMC/IPMI, or cluster schedulers
  • Graph databases
  • Event-driven systems and messaging platforms such as NATS or Kafka
  • Observability platforms such as Prometheus and Grafana
  • Building evaluation frameworks or improving the quality and reliability of LLM-powered systems

About Together AI

Together AI is a research-driven artificial intelligence company. We believe open and transparent AI systems will drive innovation and create the best outcomes for society, and together we are on a mission to significantly lower the cost of modern AI systems by co-designing software, hardware, algorithms, and models. We have contributed to leading open-source research, models, and datasets to advance the frontier of AI, and our team has been behind technological advancement such as FlashAttention, Hyena, FlexGen, and RedPajama. We invite you to join a passionate group of researchers and engineers in our journey in building the next generation AI infrastructure.

Equal Opportunity

jobs.description:
Why We Exist

Your car and your home are your most important assets, yet the experience of owning them is stuck in the 90s. Every part of the journey — buy/sell, insurance, maintenance, repairs — is fragmented, complicated, and expensive.

Jerry.ai is building the first app to manage it all. We started with car insurance in 2019, became one of the top 3 brokers in the U.S., then added driving insights, diagnostics, and a repair marketplace.

We've reached 5M+ customers, raised $240M+, scaled revenue 70X, and became profitable in early 2024. We're now expanding into adjacent verticals (e.g. home, motorcycle, RV, etc) to become the one-stop-shop for all your physical assets.

Why We’re Hiring

Our Business Operations & Analytics team has been a force multiplier and accelerant to our business that has helped us reach these pivotal milestones in spite of headwinds and within a highly competitive market. They are a team of former McKinsey, BCG and Bain consultants who drive data & insights, and inform decision-making across every corner of our business. They are analytical powerhouses and first principles problem solvers who push forward our most important initiatives across product, growth, tech, and operations.

Every business unit has a Business Operations & Analytics team member embedded within it — someone who doesn't just run analyses and build dashboards, but shapes what questions we should ask, what data to pull, what conclusions to draw, what decisions to make, and then drives our teams towards our next goal: go from 5M to 50M customers and become a $10B business in the next 4 years.

As our business continues to expand, there is growing demand for more Business Operations & Analytics team members. We are hiring 2-3 people to drive impact in these areas:

  • Growth Marketing

  • Product Development

  • Strategic Partnerships

On leveling: You may see job ads for this role at different job levels. Our priority is finding the right people, we can be flexible with job title/leveling.

Why You Will (Or Won't) Like Working Here

  • No slides: If you've worked in consulting, you know what it feels like to be up at 3am reformatting a deck. That doesn't exist here. The only work that gets done at Jerry is work that will materially change the trajectory of our business — an important product, a new growth channel, a key metric, a critical partner relationship, etc.

  • No corporate fluff: The Business Operations & Analytics team is 14 insatiable learners who care deeply about solving difficult problems and making a tangible impact. Every person owns a critical domain. There is no bloat, unnecessary meetings, or waiting for approvals.

  • Hands-on: This is not a pure strategy role, you will also own execution. Your day-to-day will be surfacing analytical insights, driving decisions, and seeing them through end-to-end.

What You'll Own

You'll sit on our central Business Operations & Analytics team but you’ll be embedded in one of Jerry's core business areas — growth, product, AI and automation, strategic partnerships — and own the analytical function for that business unit end-to-end.

  • Define the right problems: Before any analysis, understand what business question it's answering and what decision it will inform. Push back if the question is flawed.

  • Data and insights: Define metrics, build reports, run analyses, design experiments, and surface data insights that move your team's key metrics.

  • Drive outcomes: Bring recommendations to your counterparts in product, growth, finance or operations, tell them what's happening and why, and what next steps should be.

Who You Are

  • First principles thinker: You break ambiguous problems into clear hypotheses before touching data. You're analytically strong (comfortable with SQL or Python) but your instinct is to ask "what are we trying to solve here?" before jumping to "what should I build?"

  • Direct communicator: You can walk a skeptical stakeholder through a complex finding and get buy-in quickly. You write clearly, speak precisely, and don't bury the lede.

  • Owner: You act like your name is on the door. If something is broken, you feel responsible for fixing it, even if it’s outside of your swim lane.

What You'll Bring

  • 2+ years of experience at a consulting firm, investment bank, or high-growth technology company.

Within 3 to 6 months, you’ll have a repeatable pipeline engine with reliable reporting on sourced and influenced pipeline and how efficiently budget turns into pipeline.

About vCluster Labs

We're the #1 platform for AI infrastructure, trusted by the world's fastest-growing AI cloud builders. We're a venture-backed startup that's raised over $28M from top-tier investors including Khosla Ventures (first investor in OpenAI, GitLab, Stripe, and DoorDash), and we're in a hyper-growth phase looking for motivated people to join our team. Our headquarters are in San Francisco (Salesforce Tower), but our team is distributed around the globe with a remote-first culture.

We give AI Cloud providers and AI factories a hyperscaler-like experience on their own GPU infrastructure. Our platform runs the full stack an operator needs, from bare metal provisioning and node lifecycle management up through managed Kubernetes, Slurm, Ray, and inference clusters, so they can turn raw GPUs into cluster products they can sell in days instead of spending 12+ months building it themselves. Today we power over 100,000 GPUs and 1 million CPUs across 50+ AI clouds and Fortune 500 companies, backed by a team of 40+ infrastructure engineers who build alongside our customers rather than just shipping them software.

We're the company behind vCluster, the open source technology for tenant isolation on Kubernetes, with 11,000+ GitHub stars and 40M+ tenant clusters created since 2021. Open source is part of our DNA. At KubeCon North America 2025, we launched our Infrastructure Tenancy Platform for AI, a Kubernetes-native framework built for running AI, ML, and GPU-intensive workloads anywhere, with an NVIDIA-validated reference architecture for DGX systems.

Benefits

We offer the following benefits:

  • Competitive Salary: We offer a competitive compensation package, including equity.

  • Premium Insurance: Health, dental, vision, and life Insurance, including plans for you and eligible dependents (benefits vary depending on country).

  • Flexible Working Schedule: You have a doctor’s appointment or need to head to the supermarket to get groceries at 2pm? We won’t have an issue with that. To us, results matter more than clocking in and out at the same time every day.

  • Workplace Flexibility: We’re very flexible about where you work. We know things can change in life and we’re happy to adjust the work environment for you along the way.

Culture & Values

At vCluster Labs, we value and stand for:

  1. Make it Happen: We have a relentless bias for action and the grit to push through obstacles. We do whatever it takes to figure it out, put in the work, and ruthlessly prioritize the actions that drive measurable impact for the business.

  2. Own the Outcome: We understand that our responsibility doesn't end when a task is checked off; it ends when the value is delivered. We connect our daily individual actions to the broader success of the company and our customers.

  3. Create Wow: We measure success by the experience we generate, both inside and outside the company. For our customers, this means impressive speed and intuitive experiences. For our team, this means going the extra mile to support one another and to continuously drive each other to new heights.

  4. Open Source, Open Mind: We are actively contributing to and maintaining open-source projects. Internally, we foster meritocracy — the strongest ideas win, no matter who or where they come from.

  5. Build Tomorrow’s Standards, Intentionally: We don't just ship software; we define the state-of-the-art of tomorrow. We are fearless in tearing down old approaches to build something better, but we are disciplined in how we do it because we know our users rely on our technology to run mission-critical infrastructure platforms.

jobs.title: AI Phone - Security & Privacy Engineer
jobs.excerpt: AboutWe are reimagining the phone.  AI phones need to be proactive, intuitive, intelligent and low cost.
jobs.description:
About

We are reimagining the phone. AI phones need to be proactive, intuitive, intelligent and low cost. This is a mission critical for rest of the world to adopt intelligence.

There are over 5 billion people using everyday applications such as email, messaging, notes, tasks, and calendars, yet most are not AI-native. Our mission is to build proactive applications and devices that bring intelligence into daily conversations, coordination and workflows, with minimal prompting.

Focus: Designing and implementing the security and privacy architecture for the AI-native phone, ensuring AI agents can safely access user data, interact with applications, and execute actions across the operating system.

Unlike conventional mobile application security, this role needs to consider the additional risks introduced by AI agents having access to personal context, system services, and application-level actions.

Responsibilities

  • Design the overall security and privacy architecture for the AI-native phone.

  • Define permission models and access boundaries for AI agents interacting with user data and system services.

  • Design secure mechanisms for AI access to messages, contacts, calendars, notifications, camera, microphone, location and other sensitive information.

  • Implement appropriate sandboxing and isolation for agent execution.

  • Define authentication, authorization and access-control mechanisms for AI tools and application integrations.

  • Ensure users have control over what information AI can access and what actions it can execute.

  • Implement audit logging and user-visible activity tracking for AI access and actions.

  • Design secure storage, encryption, data retention and deletion mechanisms for personal data and memory.

  • Identify and mitigate AI-specific security risks, including prompt injection, malicious applications, data exfiltration and unauthorized tool execution.

  • Review Android permission models, privileged system access, SELinux policies and system-level security boundaries.

  • Work closely with Android/AOSP, Agent Runtime, Context & Memory and Applied ML teams to ensure security is built into the architecture rather than added later.

  • Conduct security assessments, threat modeling and penetration testing for system-level AI capabilities.

Requirements

  • Strong experience in mobile security, Android security, application security or systems security.

  • Deep understanding of Android security architecture, including application sandboxing, permissions, SELinux, Binder IPC and privileged system services.

  • Experience designing authentication, authorization and access-control systems.

  • Strong understanding of encryption, secure storage, key management and data protection.

  • Experience with security threat modeling, vulnerability assessment and penetration testing.

  • Understanding of privacy-by-design principles, data minimization and user consent.

  • Ability to work across Android platform, backend and AI agent architectures.

Nice to have

  • Experience with AOSP security customization or Android platform security.

  • Experience securing system-level applications or privileged Android services.

  • Experience with AI agent security, prompt injection, tool-use security and LLM data leakage.

  • Experience with mobile device security, Trusted Execution Environment (TEE), hardware-backed keystores and secure boot.

  • Experience with privacy engineering for products handling sensitive personal information.

  • Experience building permission and approval systems for autonomous agents.

You get customers live. Hands on, end to end, and fast.

About the Role

Join a lean team at an early-stage biotech company developing AI tools for peptide and protein design. You will connect computational design, experimental validation, and platform operations, closing the loop from sequence generation to kinetics data and model improvements.

What You'll Do

  • Improve discrete diffusion and folding models for peptide and protein design, including model architecture and reasoning capabilities.

  • Operate an inference platform at scale and analyze usage patterns, including signups, churn, and customer segments.

  • Write, debug, and maintain production protocols for liquid-handling robots and plate automation.

  • Design and run BLI and SPR assays, fit kinetic curves, perform quality control, and diagnose assay failure modes.

  • Manage screening instruments and write precise protocols for external laboratory partners.

  • Use receptor biology, structure, and scoring to evaluate designs and make platform outputs useful to scientists.

  • Iterate on designed sequences using experimental kinetics data to improve models and subsequent designs.

What We're Looking For

  • Typically 3 to 11 years of relevant experience, including hands-on wet-lab work and experience across biology, bioinformatics, and machine learning.

  • Experience building or operating protein or biological models, such as discrete diffusion models, protein language models, or structure prediction systems, in a design-make-test workflow.

  • Practical experience with tools such as ESM or ProtT5 and sequence design methods such as RFdiffusion or BindCraft.

  • Hands-on proficiency writing and debugging methods for Hamilton, Tecan, Opentrons, or equivalent liquid-handling platforms.

  • Experience independently designing BLI or SPR assays, fitting kinetic curves, extracting binding parameters, and diagnosing assay artifacts.

  • Python or equivalent scripting skills for automation and kinetic data analysis, plus an understanding of protein structure, receptor biology, and scoring.

  • Ability to troubleshoot instruments and protocols quickly, operate inference systems or refine model architectures, and explain scientific workflows clearly.

  • Experience in biotech or scientific software customer-facing roles, including user conversion, customer success, or solutions engineering, is relevant. Familiarity with scientific platform usage and customer buying processes is also valuable.

Compensation & Benefits

Full-time base salary is $80,000 to $200,000 annually, depending on experience, with equity and deal-contingent upside. A consulting engagement may be available at $3,000 to $5,000 per month. Visa sponsorship is not available.

Hybrid in New York, with increased on-site presence expected as internal screening operations are established.
