Position Summary

Element Solutions is looking for an analytical and critical thinking Data Engineer. The Data Engineer is responsible for designing, developing, implementing, and maintaining scalable data pipelines and data solutions that support customer and organizational needs. This role leverages Snowflake and Apache Airflow to build and manage data integration workflows, optimize data processing, and ensure data quality, reliability, and accessibility.

The Data Engineer works collaboratively with senior engineers, software developers, data analysts, and other project stakeholders to translate technical and business requirements into effective data solutions. This position requires hands-on experience with cloud-based data platforms, workflow orchestration, SQL development, automation, and data pipeline monitoring. The ideal candidate can independently manage routine engineering tasks, troubleshoot technical issues, and contribute to the continuous improvement of data infrastructure and engineering practices.

Key Responsibilities

    Data Pipeline Development and Management

  • Design, build, and maintain reliable, scalable ETL/ELT pipelines for ingesting, transforming, and delivering data.

  • Develop Apache Airflow DAGs to orchestrate pipeline tasks, schedules, dependencies, and data-processing workflows.

  • Integrate data from sources such as databases, APIs, and files, applying appropriate transformations and preserving data consistency.

  • Develop SQL transformations and Snowflake data structures to support downstream data use.

  • Build reusable pipeline components and automate recurring processes to improve maintainability and reduce manual effort.

  • Support pipeline configuration and deployments across development, test, and production environments.

    • Snowflake Development and Optimization

  • Develop and maintain Snowflake database objects, including schemas, tables, and views.

  • Implement data loading and transformation processes using Snowflake capabilities and the organization’s approved integration tools.

  • Optimize SQL queries and Snowflake workloads by evaluating query performance, warehouse sizing and utilization, and cost.

  • Apply appropriate Snowflake data modeling and performance optimization techniques, including clustering when beneficial for the workload.

  • Implement and maintain Snowflake roles and permissions in accordance with organizational and customer security requirements.

    • Workflow Orchestration and Automation

  • Configure Airflow schedules, task dependencies, retries, timeouts, and failure handling to support reliable data workflows.

  • Monitor workflow runs, investigate failures, and implement corrective actions to prevent recurring issues.

  • Configure alerts and operational logging to support timely detection and troubleshooting of pipeline issues.

  • Develop Python scripts and automation to support pipeline operations; use SQL where appropriate for data transformations.

  • Maintain workflow and operational documentation, including dependencies, recovery steps, and troubleshooting guidance.

    • Data Quality, Testing, and Security

  • Develop and maintain automated data validation checks and tests to assess accuracy, completeness, consistency, and integrity.

  • Investigate and resolve data-quality issues, documenting their causes and corrective actions.

  • Follow established data governance, privacy, security, and access-management requirements when handling data.

  • Document data lineage and transformation logic to support traceability and maintainability.

  • Follow established procedures for error handling and data recovery, and support compliance with applicable customer, organizational, and regulatory requirements.

    • Collaboration and Continuous Improvement

  • Work with technical teams and stakeholders to clarify data requirements and deliver practical engineering solutions.

  • Participate in code reviews, technical design discussions, and development planning.

  • Contribute to shared engineering practices for version control, automated testing, and CI/CD.

  • Identify and propose improvements to the reliability, scalability, maintainability, and cost efficiency of data solutions.

  • Share knowledge with teammates and provide technical guidance when appropriate.

  • Perform other related duties as assigned.

Minimum Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Data Engineering, Information Systems, Software Engineering, or Associates degree plus two years' experience.

  • At least 3 years of professional experience in data engineering, data integration, ETL/ELT development, or a related technical field.

  • At least 3 years of hands-on experience with Snowflake and Apache Airflow in data engineering or data pipeline development.

  • Strong proficiency in SQL, including query development, data transformation, and performance optimization.

  • Experience developing, scheduling, monitoring, and troubleshooting data pipelines using Apache Airflow.

  • Experience designing and maintaining data structures, transformations, and workflows in Snowflake.

  • Proficiency in Python or a comparable scripting language for automation and data processing.

  • Understanding of relational databases, data modeling, data integration patterns, and data quality practices.

  • Experience with version control tools such as Git and collaborative software development practices.

  • Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills.

  • Ability to work independently on assigned engineering tasks while collaborating effectively with technical teams and stakeholders.

  • Must live in the Continental US.

  • Be either a US citizen or Permanent Resident due to the work we do.

  • Depending on agency requirements, you may need to possess or obtain a Public Trust designation or security clearance. Regardless of the specific requirement, all positions require the successful completion of a background check, background investigation, and the standard onboarding process.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience supporting data engineering solutions in a government contracting, healthcare CMS (Center of Medicare & Medicaid) or in the health industry, or other regulated environment.

  • Experience with cloud platforms such as AWS, Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud Platform.

  • Familiarity with cloud-based storage services and data ingestion tools.

jobs.excerpt: About Patronus AIPatronus AI is a frontier lab developing simulation research and infrastructure to accelerate progress toward human-aligned AGI.
jobs.description:
About Patronus AI

Patronus AI is a frontier lab developing simulation research and infrastructure to accelerate progress toward human-aligned AGI. We are on a mission to simulate all of the world’s intelligence.

We are the team behind some of the earliest and most influential research in AI evaluation likeFinanceBench, Lynx,SimpleSafetyTests,CopyrightCatcher,Humanity’s Last Exam, and more. We are formerly AI researchers and engineers from companies like Meta AI, Amazon AGI, and Google. Our customers include foundation model labs and Fortune 500 enterprises like Adobe. We are backed by top-tier investors like Lightspeed Venture Partners, Notable Capital, Stanford University, Noam Brown, Gokul Rajaram, and more.

At a glance

  • Engagement: Independent contractor, fully remote. Live screen-share sessions with our researchers plus short asynchronous write-ups.
  • Pay: $150 per hour. The trial session is paid.
  • Commitment: About 10 hours per week, 1 to 3 months to start, with extension for strong performers.
  • Start: Rolling
  • Location: Remote, any country, with a few hours of overlap with US or EU working hours.

The role

You'll work live with our research team on production-style reliability scenarios in a sandboxed stack: Kubernetes, Prometheus and Grafana, a log system, Helm and Terraform, and CI/CD. You solve the scenario the way you would on call, explain your reasoning as you go, tell us where the scenario doesn't match real operations, and help define what a correct resolution looks like.

Each session starts from a scenario we provide. You investigate it on a shared screen, fix or mitigate it, and then write a short note on how you approached it. Your work becomes evaluation and training data for frontier models.

You don't need an AI background. You do need to be the kind of engineer who reads the dashboard before touching the config, and who can say out loud why a tempting fix is the wrong one.

Areas we're hiring for

Each area is defined by the systems you run, so you should fit exactly one. If you work across two, apply under the one where you spend most of your time.

  • Incident response and on-call. Engineers on a production rotation who triage alerts, read metrics, logs and traces, find root cause, mitigate, roll back and write the post-mortem. Typical titles: Site Reliability Engineer, Production Engineer, On-Call Engineer, Platform Engineer.
  • Platform and infrastructure. Engineers who own clusters, deploy pipelines and infrastructure as code: Kubernetes, Helm, Terraform, CI/CD, networking and capacity. Typical titles: Infrastructure Engineer, DevOps Engineer, Platform Engineer, Cloud Engineer.
  • Observability. Engineers who build and tune the monitoring itself: Prometheus and PromQL, Grafana dashboards and alert rules, Loki or ELK, OpenTelemetry tracing, SLOs and error budgets. Typical titles: Observability Engineer, Monitoring Engineer, Site Reliability Engineer (Observability).

What you'll do

  • Work through incident, debugging and infrastructure-change scenarios live with a researcher: reading dashboards and logs, writing PromQL and LogQL, fixing Helm and Kubernetes configuration, rolling back bad deploys and writing post-mortems.
  • Explain your reasoning as you work, including the fixes you considered and rejected.
  • Review scenarios we have drafted and say plainly what is unrealistic, too easy or underspecified.
  • Help write the acceptance criteria for each scenario, including the tempting wrong moves an engineer under pressure might make.
  • Write short notes after each session on how you approached the problem and what you verified.
  • Work in reviewer feedback within agreed turnaround times, and flag guideline gaps or edge cases you run into.

Who we're looking for

Required

  • 3+ years running production systems in at least one of the areas above, including time on an on-call rotation within the last two years. You did the work yourself; managing the team is not enough.
  • Hands-on with Kubernetes, Prometheus and Grafana (or Datadog or New Relic), a log stack such as Loki, ELK or Splunk, infrastructure as code such as Terraform and Helm, and a CI/CD system.
  • Comfortable in Python, Go or Bash and at reading unfamiliar codebases.
  • Able to explain your reasoning out loud while you work, in clear professional English.
  • Reliable availability for scheduled live sessions and the habit of showing the evidence behind every conclusion.

Nice to have

  • Experience writing runbooks, post-mortems, SLO definitions or incident training material.
  • Familiarity with how AI coding agents fail on operations work.

Our standards

  • All solutions, write-ups and reviews are your own work. LLM-generated code or text is not permitted.
  • Scenarios and solutions must be original. Nothing may be copied from published or easily searchable sources.
  • Never include code, configuration, runbooks or incident details from a current or former employer or client, or anything covered by an NDA. All systems and scenarios are fictional, and all work is your own.
  • Quality is judged on correctness, clarity of reasoning and reviewer agreement, not on speed or volume.

How hiring works

  • Short AI interview and resume review
  • One paid trial session, scored against a fixed quality checklist
  • Onboarding and your first project

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer
jobs.excerpt: We are an AI-first company building innovative agentic frameworks, the systems that let LLM-driven agents research, plan, and act reliably in production.
jobs.description:
We are an AI-first company building innovative agentic frameworks, the systems that let LLM-driven agents research, plan, and act reliably in production. That means orchestrating multi-step workflows with retries, skips, and parallel execution; keeping long-running work persistent and observable; and serving per-tenant retrieval at scale. This isn't about wrapping an LLM in an API call, it's the hard backend engineering that makes agents dependable.

Our stack is Python (FastAPI) on AWS, with Terraform. We hire on engineering depth and judgment, not on a keyword count, and we work in whichever language you're strongest in during the interview (more below). As a Senior Engineer, you will own backend services and the orchestration layer on top of them, from design through deployment, operation, and the on-call that follows.

Our team is based in Tehran and pays salaries monthly in USD.

What You Will Do:

  • Design, build, and own backend services and the agent-orchestration layer end to end.

  • Build resilient systems that stay correct under load and degrade gracefully when a model, tool, or dependency fails.

  • Ensure operational excellence by making long-running, multi-step work observable and debuggable in production.

  • Shape technical direction through rigorous code reviews, mentorship, and pushing back on specifications when they misalign with engineering reality.

  • Drive the full software development lifecycle, translating ambiguous requirements into durable architectures and actionable technical plans.

What We Are Looking For:

  • 5+ years building and operating production backend systems, with deep ownership of at least one non-trivial service you can talk through end to end.

  • Deep fluency in your primary backend language, and the ability to pick up a new one fast. We work in Python; if it is not your daily language today, we expect you to ramp quickly.

  • Strong systems fundamentals — concurrency, data modeling, and failure modes — and the judgment to choose the right abstraction rather than the cleverest one.

  • Sound reasoning under ambiguity: you ask the clarifying question first, make the trade-offs explicit, and adapt when the constraints change.

  • Solid grasp of infrastructure and operations, including message brokers (Kafka, RabbitMQ), SQL and NoSQL stores, and running services in containers with an orchestrator (Kubernetes, ECS, Nomad, or similar).

  • Professional written English, enabling you to write crisp design documents and align stakeholders on complex technical trade-offs.

Even Better:

  • AWS (especially ECS) and Terraform, or comparable cloud and Infrastructure-as-Code experience.

  • Hands-on work with LLM, agentic, or RAG systems (LangChain, CrewAI, OpenAI/Anthropic SDKs, Hugging Face) and a real grasp of how non-deterministic agent steps differ from ordinary functions.

  • A recognized-bar engineering background, owned open-source work, or another verifiable standout signal.

How We Hire:

We use a deliberate, transparent two-stage process designed to see how you think and build:

  • 1. A 120-minute conversation focusing on your background and a collaborative system-design exercise and cultural fit..

  • 2. A 120-minute live technical session involving code review, live coding, and a self-review.

You may complete the technical session in your strongest language (Python, Go, Java, Kotlin, PHP, or TypeScript/Node.js). Web search is encouraged; AI assistants are not used. We want to see your fundamental engineering judgment.

What We Offer:

  • Competitive USD-based salary and a comprehensive benefits package.

  • Hybrid work flexibility with hours that support deep work.

  • The opportunity to work at the frontier of agentic AI, tackling hard problems with high ownership.

  • A highly educated, agile senior team that values pragmatism, learning, and continuous improvement.

If you would rather be judged on how you think than on a buzzword list, we would like to talk!

jobs.description:
As the global leader in high-speed connectivity, Ciena builds the critical infrastructure powering the AI era. We’re a technology company shaping the future of networking, guided by innovation, integrity, and collaboration. Through development opportunities, meaningful work, and flexibility, Ciena supports growth and well-being—on and off the job. Connect with a career that matters.


Ciena is seeking an experienced, analytical, and results-oriented professional to drive transportation optimization, network design support, and cost reduction initiatives across its global Service Logistics operations.

This role will focus on improving the efficiency, cost-effectiveness, and performance of Ciena's global service logistics network, with particular emphasis on international transportation, cross-border distribution, carrier and routing optimization, and logistics cost visibility. The successful candidate will help evaluate how inventory and replacement equipment move across global distribution centers, forward stocking locations (FSLs), and customer sites, identifying opportunities to reduce transportation and operating costs while maintaining or improving service-level commitments.

Working closely with Service Logistics, Service Parts Planning, Global Trade, Finance, and third-party logistics providers (3PLs), this individual will develop fact-based recommendations, strengthen foundational logistics processes and analytical capabilities, and drive optimization initiatives from analysis through implementation.

The position will also support broader Service Supply Chain cost-reduction programs and special projects, including RMA deflection, repair cost optimization, and operational process improvement.

Key Responsibilities

International Transportation & Logistics Optimization

  • Analyze and optimize domestic and international transportation flows across Ciena's global Service Supply Chain, including distribution center-to-FSL, FSL-to-customer, interfacility, and reverse logistics movements.
  • Identify opportunities to reduce transportation costs through carrier and service-level selection, route optimization, shipment consolidation, distribution strategies, and improved utilization of existing logistics infrastructure.
  • Evaluate international transportation lanes, transit times, freight rates, shipping modes, and service capabilities to identify cost-effective solutions that support customer delivery commitments.
  • Partner with Global Trade and logistics providers to assess cross-border shipping requirements, customs clearance considerations, importer/exporter of record (IOR/EOR) arrangements, and other trade-related factors affecting transportation cost, feasibility, and execution.
  • Analyze transportation performance, routing exceptions, expedited shipments, and cost drivers to identify recurring inefficiencies and develop corrective actions.

Service Logistics Network Design & Cost Optimization

  • Support global Service Logistics network design and optimization initiatives, evaluating transportation strategies, distribution alternatives, FSL configurations, and associated cost, service, and operational tradeoffs.
  • Develop transportation and logistics cost models to compare network design scenarios, including centralized versus distributed fulfillment, alternate stocking locations, carrier options, and service-level configurations.
  • Evaluate supplier rate structures, transportation pricing, accessorial charges, and other logistics cost components to identify savings opportunities and support commercially informed network decisions.
  • Partner with internal stakeholders and logistics providers to translate network analysis into actionable recommendations, business cases, and implementation plans.

Logistics Spend Visibility, Analytics & Process Improvement

  • Help establish the foundational logistics spend visibility and Spend Cube capabilities required to analyze freight, transportation, duty/VAT, and related expenses across carriers, lanes, regions, and service levels.
  • Develop and improve logistics cost forecasting, actual-cost tracking, performance reporting, and analytical models to support financial planning, cost reduction, and operational decision-making.
  • Analyze large and fragmented data sets, reconcile information across supplier and internal systems, and identify opportunities to improve data accuracy, transparency, and usability.
  • Support the development and documentation of foundational Service Logistics processes and standards, including process mapping, routing and carrier standards, global trade-lane visibility, and operational playbooks, to improve consistency and enable future optimization.

Cost Reduction Initiatives & Special Projects

  • Lead or support assigned Service Supply Chain cost-reduction initiatives, developing business cases, establishing baselines, coordinating cross-functional actions, and tracking results through implementation and realized savings.
  • Drive the RMA FastTrack program by partnering with Technical Support, Product Quality, Repair Operations, and other stakeholders to identify opportunities to prevent avoidable returns and reduce unnecessary repair, transportation, and inventory expense.
  • Analyze repair reason codes, event codes, NFF, CNR, and related repair outcomes to identify systemic cost drivers, improve data integrity, and support corrective actions and process improvements.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Logistics, Transportation, Business, Operations, Industrial Engineering, Analytics, or a related field.
  • 5+ years of relevant professional experience in supply chain, transportation, logistics, distribution operations, network optimization, or related functions.
  • Strong working knowledge of international transportation and logistics, including cross-border distribution, freight movement, transportation service levels, carrier operations, and associated cost drivers.
  • Demonstrated experience analyzing transportation networks, logistics costs, operational performance, or distribution strategies to develop actionable business recommendations.
  • Strong analytical, quantitative, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to evaluate complex operational and financial tradeoffs.
  • Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Excel and experience with data visualization or business intelligence tools such as Power BI.
  • Experience working with large or fragmented data sets and reconciling information across multiple systems, suppliers, or operational processes.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently manage analytical workstreams, lead cross-functional initiatives, and drive projects from analysis through implementation.
  • Strong communication, organizational, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to translate complex findings into clear recommendations for operational and leadership teams.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in service parts logistics, aftermarket supply chains, advanced replacement, reverse logistics, or time-critical service delivery networks.
  • Familiarity with international trade and customs processes, Incoterms, IOR/EOR requirements, and cross-border shipping considerations.
  • Experience with 3PL operations, carrier rate structures, freight cost modeling, transportation management systems (TMS), or logistics procurement analysis.
  • Knowledge of FSL network optimization, inventory deployment strategies, transportation serviceability, and service-level cost tradeoffs.
  • Experience with SQL, Python, Java, or similar data analytics and automation tools.
  • Experience with Lean, Six Sigma, or other structured continuous-improvement methodologies.
  • Experience with cost-reduction business cases, savings measurement, forecasting, spend analysis, or operational performance modeling.

jobs.title: Manager, Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM)
jobs.excerpt: About the TeamDoorDash’s Global Governance, Risk and Compliance (GRC) team helps the business scale securely through practical risk-based decisions, reliable controls and clear accountability.
jobs.description:
About the Team

DoorDash’s Global Governance, Risk and Compliance (GRC) team helps the business scale securely through practical risk-based decisions, reliable controls and clear accountability. Our third-party risk program protects the systems and data behind our marketplace across DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM) Manager to lead a technically rigorous global program and shape its AI-native future. You will own the vendor security risk lifecycle, lead complex assessments of integrations with our most critical systems and data, and develop a team that makes clear, evidence-based risk decisions. You will also set the vision and build practical agentic workflows that improve how we gather evidence, assess risk, and follow through on remediation.

Reporting to the Global Head of GRC, you will serve as their US-based deputy and provide GRC leadership and escalation coverage during US business hours. You will directly manage TPRM analysts together with other US-based GRC team members assigned to your organization.

This role combines hands-on technical judgment, program ownership and people leadership. You will be based in the United States, preferably within the Eastern or Central timezones, with core working hours aligned to US business needs and clear handoffs with global colleagues.

What you will do

  • Run the day-to-day TPRM program operations from vendor discovery and risk tiering through due diligence, onboarding, continuous monitoring, remediation and exit. Maintain a reliable vendor inventory, policies, assessment standards, and service levels across DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo, covering cloud, SaaS, business process outsourcing (BPO), and other critical suppliers.
  • Lead assessments of vendors connected to crown jewel systems, including identity platforms, production cloud, source code and CI/CD, and sensitive-data platforms. Examine architecture, data flows, permissions, and control evidence. Use structured threat modeling to identify realistic compromise paths and define testable requirements for access, isolation, secrets, encryption, logging and revocation.
  • Turn findings into accountable risk decisions. Agree mitigation plans and security contract terms with vendors, Legal, Privacy, Procurement, and system owners. Verify remediation, document residual risk acceptance with accountable business owners and review dates, and confirm access removal and data handling at termination. Address critical supplier dependencies, concentration risk, recovery capabilities, and exit readiness.
  • Set the vision for an AI-native TPRM function. Build a prioritized roadmap for applying AI and automation across the vendor lifecycle, with clear outcomes, dependencies, and ownership. Evaluate what to configure, buy, or build, and align delivery with Security Engineering, IT, and platform owners.
  • Build and pilot agentic workflows with the team to gather and reconcile evidence, identify control gaps, draft assessments, and coordinate follow-up. Scale the use cases that demonstrate better quality, coverage or turnaround. Use approved tools, APIs, and engineering partnerships, with evidence traceability, evaluations, data protection, appropriate access controls and human approval for consequential actions.
  • Own the TPRM framework for third-party AI and agentic services. Assess model and data providers, connectors, tool permissions, training-data use, retention, subprocessors, prompt injection, and data exfiltration. Set onboarding and monitoring requirements that respond to material changes in models, integrations, and vendor practices.
  • Hire, coach, and directly manage TPRM professionals and other US-based GRC direct reports. Own goals, workload, performance reviews, career development, and succession planning. Raise the team’s technical assessment and automation skills, working with functional leads to align priorities across GRC disciplines.
  • Provide US-hours GRC coverage and escalation support in partnership with the Global Head of GRC. Lead stakeholder discussions, resolve operational escalations, and coordinate GRC input to vendor incidents, audits, and urgent business decisions. Exercise agreed delegated authority, route risk acceptance to accountable owners, and maintain clear decisions and handoffs with global leadership.
  • Make risk and program performance visible to leadership and auditors. Report critical-system exposure, overdue remediation, exception aging, assessment quality, and review turnaround. Measure how AI and automation improve coverage or reduce effort, and translate material risks into business impact to guide priorities and investment.

What you bring

  • 6+ years of progressive experience in technical third-party risk, security risk, or security engineering, including substantial hands-on experience leading complex vendor assessments and ownership of a TPRM program. A track record of improving risk practices in a technology environment.
  • Experience leading distributed teams and coordinating delivery across different GRC specialties.
  • Deep experience assessing enterprise integrations and their failure modes. You can examine SAML/OIDC federation, OAuth scopes and tokens, SCIM provisioning, APIs, service accounts, cloud IAM, network boundaries, and data flows, then turn findings into practical integration requirements and verified remediation.
  • Strong assurance and control-testing skills. You can evaluate SOC 2 Type II scope, exceptions, subservice organizations, and customer responsibilities; interpret penetration tests and ISO 27001 or PCI DSS evidence where relevant; and validate whether the evidence covers the service, integration, and data use being proposed.
  • An AI-native working approach: you actively use AI to improve your work and have built or piloted AI-assisted workflows. You can articulate a vision for agentic TPRM, identify useful applications, and explain how you evaluate outputs, handle failures, and protect sensitive information.
  • Experience implementing or improving TPRM/GRC platforms and workflow automation, with practical knowledge of APIs and integration patterns. You can define requirements, work with structured data, and partner with engineers on delivery. Python, SQL, low-code orchestration, and production-scale agentic experience are advantages.
  • Hands-on knowledge of cloud and SaaS security, privileged supplier or BPO access, data protection, incident response, and recovery. You can apply security frameworks and threat modeling to a vendor’s actual deployment and assess AI-specific risks such as data use, tool permissions, and prompt injection.
  • Sound judgment and executive communication, with experience representing a security or GRC leader, making decisions within delegated authority, and resolving difficult risk tradeoffs. You can earn credibility with engineers, Legal, Procurement, and business leaders while managing urgent US-hours escalations.

Compensation

The successful candidate’s starting pay will fall within the pay range listed below and is determined based on job-related factors including, but not limited to, skills, experience, qualifications, work location, and market conditions. Base salary is localized according to an employee’s work location. Ranges are market-dependent and may be modified in the future.

In addition to base salary, the compensation for this role includes opportunities for equity grants. Talk to your recruiter for more information.

DoorDash cares about you and your overall well-being. That’s why we offer a comprehensive benefits package to all regular employees, which includes a 401(k) plan with employer matching, 16 weeks of paid parental leave, wellness benefits, commuter benefits match, paid time off and paid sick leave in compliance with applicable laws (e.g. Colorado Healthy Families and Workplaces Act). DoorDash also offers medical, dental, and vision benefits, 11 paid holidays, disability and basic life insurance, family-forming assistance, and a mental health program, among others.

To learn more about our benefits, visit our careers page here.

About DoorDash

At DoorDash, our mission to empower local economies shapes how our team members move quickly, learn, and reiterate in order to make impactful decisions that display empathy for our range of users—from Dashers to merchant partners to consumers. jobs.description:
Description:

We are seeking an experienced Principal Consultant to provide senior technical leadership across transmission planning, interconnection, reliability, utility operations, and regulatory compliance. This role combines advanced power system engineering with project leadership, client advisory responsibilities, and the development of technical staff.

As a Principal Consultant, you will lead complex, multidisciplinary engagements; guide engineering studies and deliverables; and help clients address planning, interconnection, operational, and compliance challenges. You will serve as a trusted advisor to utilities, system operators, government organizations, and other industry stakeholders while supporting the continued growth of our transmission planning practice.

What you will do:

  • Serve as a technical leader and subject matter expert in transmission planning, interconnection, reliability, and related disciplines.
  • Lead the planning, execution, and delivery of complex, multidisciplinary projects.
  • Provide technical oversight and engineering direction for power system models, studies, analyses, and project deliverables.
  • Apply advanced engineering judgment to solve complex technical and business challenges.
  • Advise clients and serve as a primary point of contact for key stakeholders.
  • Lead technical reviews and quality assurance activities to produce high-quality, defensible work products.
  • Identify project risks, develop mitigation strategies, and communicate challenges and opportunities proactively.
  • Mentor engineers, consultants, and technical staff.
  • Support business development through client engagement, proposal development, scope definition, and technical strategy.
  • Represent the company through industry committees, working groups, conferences, publications, and presentations.
  • Advance engineering methodologies, tools, standards, and business processes while maintaining knowledge of industry requirements and emerging trends.

Areas of expertise:

Transmission planning

  • Reliability assessments and system performance evaluations
  • NERC TPL compliance studies
  • Transfer capability and congestion analysis
  • Long-range transmission planning
  • Contingency analysis, corrective action development, transmission expansion, and system reinforcement studies

Interconnection and Grid Integration

  • Load, generation, and energy storage interconnection studies
  • Large load and data center integration
  • System impact, deliverability, and network upgrade assessments
  • Utility and ISO/RTO interconnection processes

Utility Operations and Compliance

  • Transmission Owner and Transmission Operator (TO/TOP) support
  • Reliability compliance initiatives
  • Operational readiness assessments
  • Utility procedures and operational practices

Regulatory and Reliability:

  • Department of Energy initiatives and stakeholder coordination
  • NERC Reliability Standards, including CIP-014, TPL-001, TPL-007, PRC-019, and PRC-024
  • FERC Order No. 881
  • Regulatory and compliance-driven utility initiatives

Regional Experience:

  • NYISO and ISO-NE
  • Other ISO/RTOs and utility transmission systems throughout North America

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering from an ABET-accredited university required; advanced degree preferred.
  • Professional Engineer (PE) license required.
  • Minimum 15 years of relevant experience in transmission planning, interconnection, power system studies, utility operations, reliability, compliance, or related consulting services. Experience may be reduced to 12 years for exceptionally qualified candidates holding a PE license.
  • Demonstrated experience leading technical projects and client engagements within the electric utility industry.
  • Experience performing engineering studies for transmission systems, generation resources, energy storage facilities, and large load interconnections.
  • Knowledge of electric utility planning, operations, reliability, and regulatory practices.
  • Proficiency with power system analysis software such as PSS®E, PSLF, PSCAD, ASPEN, ETAP, TARA, or similar tools.
  • Experience with programming and automation tools such as Python, C, C++, or similar languages.
  • Strong technical writing, presentation, communication, mentoring, and engineering oversight skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to exercise independent engineering judgment and make discretionary technical decisions.

Why Join Us:

At ENTRUST Solutions Group, a Leidos company, we are driven by a commitment to innovation, technical excellence, and delivering the critical infrastructure that powers and connects communities. Together with Leidos, we are building a scaled, end-to-end energy and infrastructure organization focused on modernizing the grid, improving reliability, and helping utilities and network providers meet rising demand.

As an ENR top ranked firm, our team of more than 5,000 professionals brings deep technical expertise and advanced technology across electric, gas, and telecommunications infrastructure. We solve complex challenges for clients across North America and expanding markets, helping them strengthen reliability, expand capacity, and adapt to evolving infrastructure needs.

We foster a culture where innovation, collaboration, and continuous improvement are expected, and where people are empowered to challenge convention, think boldly, and make an impact. Whether you are looking to grow your expertise, lead transformative projects, or help shape the future of infrastructure, you will find opportunities to thrive here.

If you are ready to outthink the status quo, tackle meaningful challenges, and build what is next, we would love to hear from you.

What We Offer:

  • Generous paid time off and benefits
  • 401(k) retirement program with company match
  • Career development programs
  • Tuition reimbursement
  • Flexible work schedule
